109-1-LB311_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB311_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services - The bill requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to consult with the Director of Medicaid and Long-Term Care (or designee) of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) when evaluating applications for permits, certificates, or designations to provide medicaid nonemergency medical transportation (NEMT) services contracted with DHHS, Medicaid-managed care organizations, or agents of the department. \n- A designation authorizing a regulated motor carrier to provide NEMT must be found necessary for the present or future convenience and necessity of medicaid clients; applicants bear the burden to demonstrate responsiveness to public need, and protestants must show existing carriers meet the need or that the applicant would impair existing operations. \n- Transportation network companies and participating drivers are prohibited from providing transportation under contract with DHHS or its contractors without specific PSC authorization; the PSC must grant authorization unless protesters meet the statutory standard. \n- The bill contains no DHHS appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations. Adds a requirement that when the commission considers authorizing providers to offer Medicaid nonemergency medical transportation (NEMT) under contract with (i) the Department of Health and Human Services, (ii) a Medicaid-managed care organization contracting with the department, or (iii) another agent acting for the department under section 75-303.01, the commission must consult with the Director of Medicaid and Long-Term Care (or designee) to assess consistency with the public interest. No changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB312_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB312_Final_Copy.docx LB312 amends the Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act. It expands eligible student loan programs to include nurse anesthesia and dietitian nutritionist programs and adds nurse anesthetists and dietitian nutritionists to loan-repayment eligibility. It sets financial limits: student loans $30,000/year (caps: $120,000 for medical/dental/doctorate mental‑health; $30,000 for master's mental‑health/PA); medical resident incentive $40,000/year (cap $120,000); loan repayments $30,000/year (cap $90,000) for physicians/psychiatrists/dentists/psychologists and $15,000/year (cap $45,000) for PAs, NPs, nurse anesthetists, pharmacists, PTs, OTs, dietitian nutritionists, and mental‑health practitioners. Full debt repayment is authorized for qualifying psychiatrists/psychologists/mental‑health practitioners meeting five‑year practice and community‑supervision treatment criteria. The bill preserves departmental authority to set terms and requires using federal American Rescue Plan Act funds first for agreements entered by 12/31/2024 (usable through 12/31/2026) without a local-match requirement. It repeals the prior sections. The added language expands the list of approved programs to explicitly include a nurse anesthesia practice program and a dietitian nutritionist program, and enumerates eligible practitioner types — notably nurse anesthetists and dietitian nutritionists licensed under section 38-1813. No state agencies or departments are named in the underlined text, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations referenced. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB313_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB313_Intro_Copy.docx LB313 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48‑118 and 48‑118.04 (Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act) to explicitly recognize both employers and workers' compensation insurers as subrogated parties against third parties. It clarifies insurers may recover amounts beyond paid compensation and requires any recovery in excess (after recovery expenses) be paid promptly to the employee as an advance on future benefits. Settlements of third‑party claims must be in writing and agreed to by the employee and the employer's workers' compensation insurer (or the employer if uninsured), or approved by the court as fair and reasonable. If parties disagree on distributing judgment or settlement proceeds, the court must order distribution: after recovery expenses, one‑third to the employee, then payment to the employer/insurer for compensation paid or owed, with any remaining balance to the employee. No changes to state agency funding or appropriations are made. Adds a three-part allocation rule for recoveries: after reasonable recovery costs, one‑third of the remainder goes to the employee (or personal representative); next, the employer or workers’ compensation insurer is reimbursed for compensation already paid or obligations they may have to pay; any remaining balance then goes to the employee (or personal representative). No state agencies or departments are referenced and there are no changes to appropriations or budgetary funding. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB314_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB314_Intro_Copy.docx LB314 amends the Sports Arena Facility Financing Assistance Act (amending §13-3103 and §13-3106). It defines "lease" for coapplicants and clarifies allowable uses of state assistance for privately owned sports complexes: repayment of bonds borrowed for related public infrastructure, leasing to political subdivisions (coapplicants) at fair‑market rent for up to 20 years, promotion of public sporting events, and repayment of nonprofit corporation debt subject to voter approval. It caps state-funded promotion at 10 years (arts/cultural and sporting events) and 5 years for complexes in second‑class cities or villages. For large public stadiums approved on/after July 19, 2024, state assistance may fund up to 100% of final project costs. §13-3106 also clarifies temporary board approvals (tied to voter approval or issuance of a building permit within 24 months) and board quorum/voting requirements (majority, including the Governor). Adds a definition of "lease" as any contractual lease between the coapplicants identified in §13-3102(1)(b) for use of an eligible sports arena at fair‑market rent for up to 20 years. Establishes that an approval given solely to satisfy the §13-3103(1)(f) requirement is a temporary approval: it becomes permanent if a building permit for the eligible sports arena is issued within 24 months of that temporary approval; if not, the temporary approval expires. The text refers to action by "the board." No specific state agencies, departments, or any funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB315_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB315_Intro_Copy.docx LB315 amends Nebraska corporate statutes to impose a sunset on the mandatory biennial report and occupation‑tax regime for domestic and foreign corporations, making the reporting and tax requirements effective only through January 1, 2026. The Secretary of State is the central agency: prescribing report forms, receiving reports and occupation taxes, sending mandated notices to registered agents and foreign corporations, filing reports, returning nonconforming filings, signing and filing certificates of administrative dissolution or revocation, and serving copies. 109-1-LB316_Final Final Reading Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB316_Final_Copy.docx Department of Agriculture, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue - Department of Revenue: LB316 imposes a 10% excise tax on retail sales of cannabidiol products effective January 1, 2026. 109-1-LB317_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB317_Final_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Banking and Finance, Department of Economic Development, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military Department The bill assigns multiple administrative, regulatory, consultation, and funding duties across state agencies. 109-1-LB319_Intro Governor Veto Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB319_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Agriculture, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services LB319 directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to maximize Nebraska participation in the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), seek federal funding, minimize General Fund use, hire necessary staff, and submit an annual report (by Dec. 1) to the Legislature detailing options, actions, caseload, costs, and expenditures. DHHS must develop a USDA Food and Nutrition Service–approved state outreach plan, may accept gifts/grants/donations, partner with counties/nonprofits, submit the plan to FNS/USDA for approval and request federal matching funds, and may be exempt from implementation if private or federal funds are insufficient. DHHS shall create a TANF‑funded policy to establish categorical SNAP eligibility (including a temporary increase of gross income eligibility to 165% FPG through 10/1/2025), eliminate most asset limits (liquid assets capped at $25,000), and annually evaluate administrative costs and federal funding availability. The Department of Labor may administer a SNAP Next Step employment program (participants encouraged 131–165% FPG); the Legislature intends no General Funds be used by Labor for those processes. Change: SNAP eligibility for people convicted of drug-related felonies is limited to those who (1) have completed their sentence or (2) are currently serving parole, probation, or post‑release supervision.\n\nAgency impacts:\n- Department of Agriculture (Food and Nutrition Service): must update SNAP eligibility policy, application/verification procedures, IT systems, and staff training to implement the new criteria; likely increased casework/verification burden.\n- Department of Labor: potential need to coordinate with reentry/employment programs and verify supervision status for beneficiaries; may see increased referrals but no direct programmatic funding change.\n- Department of Health and Human Services: limited direct program change, but possible coordination/data‑sharing impacts for integrated benefit and reentry services.\n\nBudget: no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided in the text. 109-1-LB31_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB31_Intro_Copy.docx Requires the State Board of Education to develop and distribute a model policy governing school district use of student surveillance, monitoring, and tracking technology. The model must require districts to inventory tools and disclose vendor/government provider contact information, purchase and maintenance costs, tool descriptions and privacy protections, opt‑out availability, data sharing with law enforcement or disciplinary implications, accommodations for students with disabilities, biometric/personally identifiable information handling, and remedies available under the Consumer Protection Act, the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act, and section 79‑2,104. School districts must post the inventory online and provide hard copies on request. 109-1-LB338_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB338_Intro_Copy.docx LB338 (2025) bars life insurers, disability insurers, and long-term care insurers from using genetic information or genetic test results—absent a clinical diagnosis—to deny, cancel, limit coverage, set premium differentials, or impose preexisting-condition exclusions. Insurers also may not require or solicit genetic information or consider an individual's genetic-testing decisions for underwriting. Permitted actions include reviewing an applicant's medical record, asking about family history, and relying on documented clinical diagnoses. The bill cites the federal Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (29 U.S.C. 1182) and uses the definitions in Neb. Rev. §48-236. No state agencies are assigned new responsibilities, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes. The added text: (1) states legislative findings noting federal GINA (29 U.S.C. §1182) and the benefits of genetic testing; (2) bars life insurers, disability insurers, and long‑term care insurers — absent a clinical diagnosis — from canceling/denying/limiting coverage, setting premium differentials, requiring or soliciting genetic information, using genetic test results, or considering decisions about testing; (3) preserves insurer rights to review medical records, ask about family history, and consider clinical diagnoses in records; and (4) references state definitions in section 48‑236. Government entities mentioned are the Legislature and the federal Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act; no state agencies or departments are newly created or tasked, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. 109-1-LB349_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB349_Intro_Copy.docx LB349 revises oversight by the Nebraska Power Review Board (the board). It amends definitional provisions and explicitly brings electric energy storage resources under the board’s pre‑construction/acquisition approval regime for generation, storage, and transmission facilities above 700 volts, while preserving specified exemptions (service‑area extensions, small replacements, certain intra‑state transactions, qualified facilities). Privately developed renewable facilities complying with §70‑1014.02 are exempt. The board’s executive director may notify private electric suppliers and impose a $500 fine if construction begins less than 30 days before required notice; failure to cure may require cessation of construction or operation. Private suppliers may request a board hearing; the board issues decisions, can allocate hearing costs to violators, and may seek injunctive relief for unauthorized construction or service. The bill contains no changes to appropriations or budget allocations. Adds a definition of “electric energy storage resource” and minor clarifying wording. The definition: a resource that can receive electric energy from the grid or an associated generation source, store it, and later inject that energy back to the grid. Explicit exclusions: devices intended solely to inject/absorb reactive power (e.g., capacitors, synchronous condensers) and equipment intended solely to supply power for electric vehicles. Other insertions clarify “public or private” ownership and singular/plural references to one or more electric energy storage resources. Defines Coordinated Universal Time as the scale maintained by the General Conference on Weights and Measures and “interpreted or modified for the United States” by the U.S. Secretary of Commerce in coordination with the U.S. Secretary of the Navy. 109-1-LB366_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB366_Intro_Copy.docx LB366 creates a Legislative Economic Analysis Unit and a Chief Economist. Agencies proposing covered rules must publish notice, submit a report and any cost‑benefit analysis (including jobs added/lost, public vs. private), list related regulatory actions and aggregate economic effects, and electronically provide materials to the Legislature and Chief Economist before filing with the Secretary of State. The Unit must report on each major rule to the relevant legislative committee within 15 legislative days assessing procedural compliance and regulatory impact. Major rules cannot be published until ratified by law or 60 legislative days pass without a final vote; the Governor may permit earlier emergency effective dates only with a published justification. Emergency rules remain effective 90 days (renewable once); agencies must file them with the Secretary of State and publish online. The bill amends Administrative Procedure Act definitions and allows courts to review whether statutory requirements for a rule’s effect have been met. No appropriations or funding changes are included. Adds procedural requirements for agencies and legislative bodies. Key agencies/departments mentioned: the Legislature (must designate an email/electronic address for rule delivery), the Secretary of State (publication filing), the Chief Economist (receive rule submissions), the Legislative Economic Analysis Unit (must report on each major rule to the relevant legislative committee within 15 legislative days), affected state agencies (must publish rules in a newspaper, submit copies, a concise statement, major/nonmajor classification, related actions, proposed effective date, and a cost‑benefit analysis including jobs added/lost and public vs. private jobs), the Governor (may seek early effect with a public statement), and the courts (may review compliance and whether a rule is “major”). No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included; “federal funding” is only cited as a possible justification for expedited effect. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB367_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB367_Intro_Copy.docx LB367 amends the Uniform Credentialing Act to prohibit licensed providers under the Medicine and Surgery, Mental Health, Nurse, Pharmacy, and Psychology practice acts from providing conversion therapy (including gender-identity and sexual-orientation conversion therapy) to persons under 19. The bill defines conversion therapy, exempts pastoral/religious counseling by clergy, and makes violations both a disciplinary ground under the Uniform Credentialing Act (enforced by the department) and a deceptive trade practice. It also adds the prohibition to the list of bases for action against pharmacy technician registrations, allowing the department, with the recommendation of the board, to deny or discipline registrations. Sec. 3(5) bars the use of state funds or funds of political subdivisions to provide, refer for, or cover conversion therapy. Adds a ban on licensed health professionals (those credentialed under the Medicine and Surgery, Mental Health, Nurse, Pharmacy, and Psychology Practice Acts) from providing conversion therapy to anyone under 19. Defines conversion, gender-identity conversion, and sexual-orientation conversion therapy. Violations are classified as deceptive trade practices under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Exempts clergy/religious counselors acting in a pastoral (non-healthcare) capacity. Fiscal language prohibits any state or political‑subdivision (local) funds from being spent to conduct, refer for, or provide health‑benefit coverage for conversion therapy. No specific appropriations, dollar amounts, or new agency budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB368_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB368_Intro_Copy.docx LB368 creates the Nebraska Youth in Care Bill of Rights and prescribes duties for the state child‑welfare "department" (the responsible agency under existing statutes), caseworkers, guardians ad litem, and the courts. Key agency obligations include facilitating sibling placements/visitation, reunification and visitation with biological family, transition planning (per §43‑1311.03), ensuring confidentiality consistent with law, and providing access to birth certificates, SSN, medical/educational records and related documents. Caseworkers must be trained on the rights, provide paper notices and periodic discussions with youth, and explain a grievance process; the department must acknowledge grievances within three business days and inform youth of Administrative Procedure Act review. Guardians ad litem must discuss rights with youth and raise infringements to the court. The Nebraska Strengthening Families Act Committee (§43‑4716) will monitor implementation. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided. Adds duties for "the department" (child welfare agency) and related actors: caseworkers must be trained on and provide paper copies of youth rights, discuss them with children (age 14+) at specified intervals (within 72 hours and two weeks of placement, then quarterly), obtain acknowledgments, and offer private, regular grievance instruction. Guardians ad litem must discuss rights within two weeks of appointment and every six months and must raise alleged infringements with the court. The department must facilitate sibling placement/visitation, reunification/visitation as required by law, ensure confidentiality and access to vital records, and acknowledge grievances within three business days with info on the grievance and Administrative Procedure Act review. 109-1-LB36_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB36_Final_Copy.docx Department of Transportation The bill consolidates and clarifies authority in the Nebraska Department of Transportation (defined as “Department”), vesting the Director‑State Engineer and the Department as the direct custodians and primary authority over the state highway system and federal‑aid primary roads. 109-1-LB422_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB422_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends the Nebraska Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act to require transfer-on-death deeds to include a warning that the Department of Health and Human Services may require revocation of the deed by the transferor, the transferor's spouse, or both in order to qualify or remain qualified for Medicaid assistance. 109-1-LB425_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB425_Intro_Copy.docx LB425 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-3506 to expand homestead tax exemptions. Beginning January 1, 2026, veterans rated at least 80% but less than 100% service-connected disabled become eligible for a partial homestead exemption equal to their VA disability percentage of the exempt amount. The bill keeps existing 100% exemptions for fully disabled veterans and surviving spouses. It requires certification of status from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs and specifies application/certification frequency (certain applicants annually; some certification only in years evenly divisible by five). No changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are made. The original section is repealed. 109-1-LB426_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB426_Intro_Copy.docx LB426 amends education statutes to (1) authorize a one‑hour American flag education program (grades 5–8) that may be developed with local veterans organizations and whose costs may be paid from lottery education funds or private donations; and (2) revise distribution of State Lottery Operation Trust Fund money used for education. For FY2024‑25 through FY2028‑29, statute prescribes specific percentage transfers: 8% Behavioral Training Cash Fund; 2% College Pathway Program Cash Fund; 7% Community College Gap Assistance; 10% State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund; 3% for distance education incentives and flag education programs; 1% Door to College Scholarship; 8% Excellence in Teaching; 1.5% Expanded Learning Opportunity Grant; 1.5% Mental Health Training; and 58% Nebraska Opportunity Grant. Through FY2023‑24 funds went to the Nebraska Education Improvement Fund under prior allocations. Agencies (school boards, State Board of Education, superintendents, State Department of Education) have implementation duties; recipients must report annually to the Auditor of Public Accounts, who compiles a legislative report. The Education Committee must recommend allocations for FY2029‑30 by Dec. 31, 2027. The program may be developed in consultation with a local recognized veterans organization (see §80‑401.01). 109-1-LB427_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB427_Intro_Copy.docx Creates a Student Savings Account program administered by the State Treasurer (or a third‑party manager under the Treasurer's supervision). Establishes the Student Savings Account Support Fund, which the state investment officer will invest under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Beginning July 1, 2026, the Treasurer shall create an account per enrolled K–12 student and annually transfer $1,500 from the fund into each account; payments available by July 15 or 30 days after application. The State Board of Education must publish a list of qualified expenses on the State Department of Education website, accept appeals, and may adopt rules. The Treasurer will monitor, audit, and investigate misuse, refer suspected crimes to the Nebraska State Patrol, and require restitution; funds revert to the General Fund if a student no longer qualifies, graduates, or dies. Creates a Student Savings Account program and fund administered by the State Treasurer (or a third‑party manager under the Treasurer’s supervision). The State Board of Education must adopt a list of qualified educational expenses (posted on the State Department of Education website) and hears appeals to add expenses. Beginning 2026–27, parents/guardians/students are informed about applying; starting July 1, 2026 the Treasurer must open an account per enrolled student and annually transfer $1,500 from the newly created Student Savings Account Support Fund into each account (available by July 15 or 30 days after application). The state investment officer invests fund balances per the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Treasurer monitors accounts, audits, investigates misuse, and refers crimes to the Nebraska State Patrol; misused funds must be repaid, and terminated accounts revert to the General Fund. 109-1-LB428_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB428_Final_Copy.docx LB428 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-532 to require school districts to notify parents, guardians, and educational decisionmakers at least 15 days before administering surveys about drug, vape, alcohol, or tobacco use (via the school's electronic notification system or physical mail). Notices must describe question types, purposes/age-appropriateness, data use, access, privacy protections, and disclosure plans. Parents may request a copy of the survey, review it at school, or exempt their child. School personnel may not disclose personally identifiable student information unless required by law. Surveys asking sexual questions are prohibited for K–6 students. The bill references federal statutes/regulations that limit disclosure: FERPA, PPRA, COPPA, and the Children's Internet Protection Act (47 C.F.R. 54.520). The original §79-532 is repealed. No funding or appropriations are included. Adds parent-notification and opt-out rules for school surveys about drugs/vaping/alcohol/tobacco (15-day notice via school electronic system or mail; description of questions/purpose/privacy/access; right to request a copy, review in person, or exempt the child; prohibition on disclosing personally identifiable information unless required by law; bans sexual-content surveys for K–6).\n\nReferences federal authorities: the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (20 U.S.C. 1232h), the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 6501 et seq.), and the Children’s Internet Protection Act regulation (47 C.F.R. 54.520). No federal or state agencies are named explicitly beyond these statutes/regulations, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB429_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB429_Intro_Copy.docx LB429 restricts school board interactions with professional employees' organizations. It defines a professional employees' organization (focused on professional development or liability protection) and school employee (administrators, teachers, student teachers, paraprofessionals). If a school board allows one such organization access to employees' physical or electronic mailboxes, recruitment at employee meetings/events (including orientations), display/posting of signage or materials, or participation by name on school calendar days/breaks, the board must grant equal access or permissions to any other requesting professional employees' organization. The bill also prohibits designating calendar days/breaks using an organization's name. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds definitions for "professional employees' organization" and "school employee" and requires school boards to provide equal access to all such organizations. Specifically, school boards cannot grant one organization exclusive use of employees' physical or electronic mailboxes; if one organization may attend or display at employee meetings or orientations, others requesting permission must be allowed; the same parity must apply to posting signage or materials in schools; and school boards may not name school days or breaks after any professional employees' organization. No state agencies beyond school boards (or schools) are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB42_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB42_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services Defines "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and specifies that a "service provider" is a person certified by the department to provide developmental disabilities services. 109-1-LB430_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB430_Intro_Copy.docx LB430 amends student-discipline statutes (sections 79‑265, 79‑265.01, 79‑268). It modifies short‑term suspension procedures: principals must, within 24 hours (or up to 72 hours if reasonably necessary), send written notice to student and parent/guardian detailing the conduct, reasons for suspension, prior school interventions, resources available, and an actionable plan to keep the student in school; principals must document reasonable efforts to confer with parents/guardians before or at return. It adds an exception allowing suspension of pre‑K through grade‑2 students for violent behavior capable of causing physical harm (in addition to bringing a deadly weapon). Added provisions require schools to document (before suspension) actions taken to try to discontinue or alleviate a student’s behavior, list resources the school can provide or recommend to assist the student, and set out an actionable plan to manage the behavior going forward with the goal of keeping the student in school. The additions also clarify misconduct definitions (including bringing prohibited items and violent behavior causing physical harm). No specific government agencies or departments are referenced, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB431_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB431_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB431 amends the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and preserves an exemption for certain anabolic steroids intended for nonhuman use if approved by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. 109-1-LB43_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB43_Final_Copy.docx LB43 amends Nebraska electric law to add and clarify agency roles and certification duties. It (1) defines "military installation" to specifically include certain U.S. Air Force silos and bases (per 31 C.F.R.); (2) requires owners of generation facilities or transmission >700 volts located within a ten-mile radius of a military installation to certify to the board (and notify its executive director) that no electronic-related equipment or components are manufactured by a listed foreign adversary, with a NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) compliance exemption for retail electric suppliers and a similar NERC-based compliance option for privately developed renewable projects interconnected at ≥100 kV meeting specified size thresholds; (3) preserves board authority to preapprove otherwise prohibited equipment, issue acknowledgements within ten days, enforce compliance (including hearings and cessation orders), and bring actions in the name of the State. The definition of covered sites explicitly references certain U.S. Air Force ballistic missile silos and bases (31 C.F.R. 802.211(b)(3) and 802.227(c)). Owners of larger facilities tied to the grid (≥100 kV and specified MVA thresholds) must instead certify compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) critical infrastructure protection standards. 109-1-LB440_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB440_Intro_Copy.docx LB440 creates and funds the Education Leave and Support Act. Key agencies and fiscal actions:\n\n- State Department of Education: administers the State Education Leave Fund and Education Retention Fund, develops application/review/disbursement procedures, and must submit an annual report on expenditures, utilization, and balances.\n- State Treasurer: receives quarterly remittances of a 0.35% payroll fee on taxable wages of certificated teachers (beginning Jan 1, 2026) collected by districts and an employer match equal to total employee-collected fees; credits receipts to the State Education Leave Fund and transfers any surplus over 20% of projected annual needs to the Education Retention Fund on department notification.\n- State Investment Officer: invests fund balances per state law.\n- Auditor of Public Accounts: conducts annual audit of the State Education Leave Fund.\n\nFunding use: reimburse districts (beginning July 1, 2026) for substitute-teacher costs for the first six weeks of an employee's FMLA leave (capped at actual daily cost). Misused funds must be repaid and incur department penalties. Creates a State Education Leave Fund, administered by the State Department of Education, funded by a new 0.35% payroll fee on covered teachers' taxable wages effective Jan. 1, 2026. Employers must collect the fee from employees, remit it quarterly to the State Treasurer, and remit an equal employer match; funds are invested by the state investment officer per existing state investment law. Beginning July 1, 2026, the fund reimburses school districts for substitute-teacher costs for the first six weeks of a teacher's FMLA leave (not to exceed actual daily substitute cost as determined by the department); reimbursed teachers need not use accrued personal/sick leave for that period. The department will set application, review, and disbursement procedures and file annual reports to the Legislature. Surplus (>20% of projected needs) may be transferred to a new Education Retention Fund for shortages and professional development. Misuse requires repayment and department-prescribed penalties; the fund is audited annually by the Auditor of Public Accounts. DOCX | PDF

Virtual inspections are permitted for residential buildings under three stories and under 10,000 sq ft, require a provided list of onsite personnel, and must be live except that nonstructural reinspections may use video/photo documentation. Inspection records must be made available to the public if the structure is standing when requested. No appropriations or funding changes are included. Defines "authorized inspector" as a person credentialed by the state agency, county, city, or village issuing permits, or a third‑party inspector registered/licensed with the State of Nebraska (excluding self‑inspections). No funding or appropriation changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB442_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB442_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is directed to administer the state social services program and may contract for purchase of services at prevailing or departmental cost rates; statutory maximums for aid to dependent children apply only to public assistance grants, not social services. DHHS must establish and administer a state child care subsidy: providing assistance to families with incomes 130%–400% of FPL beginning October 1, 2026; determining eligibility (including a 10% earned‑income disregard after 12 continuous months and use of a sliding cost‑share plan with family contributions capped at existing transitional rates); adopting rules and a fixed annual reimbursement rate schedule (effective each October 1 and revised yearly); and prioritizing highest assistance for qualified apprentices. Funding: a 0.52% payroll tax (0.39% employer / 0.13% employee) will fund the program; General Funds may not be used for related state costs, including administration, beginning October 1, 2026. DHHS must expand and administer state social services to provide child care assistance to families with incomes from 130%–400% of FPL beginning Oct. 1, 2026, and adopt rules to implement the changes. DHHS will enforce Child Care Licensing Act criminal‑history checks for participating providers, apply a 10% gross‑earned‑income disregard after 12 continuous months, use a sliding cost‑share with family contributions capped at transitional program rates (as of Jan. 1, 2025), and create reasonable‑accommodation and enrollment exceptions effective Oct. 1, 2025. DHHS will set an annual fixed reimbursement rate schedule (effective Oct. 1 each year), with separate rates allowed for infants and children with special needs, not exceeding providers’ private rates. Funding: the program is financed by a 0.52% payroll tax (0.39% employer / 0.13% employee); General Funds cannot be used for costs (including administration) from the eligibility changes beginning Oct. 1, 2026. The program must prioritize qualified apprentices for highest assistance. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB443_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB443_Intro_Copy.docx LB443 amends the Nebraska Criminal Code (section 28-101) to create the offense of unlawful squatting and assigns duties to law enforcement. The citation requires the recipient to appear within three business days before a designee of the officer’s law enforcement agency and produce documentation authorizing residence (deed, title, rental agreement, proof of payments; photos/electronic copies acceptable). Failure to appear or produce authentic authorization exposes the person to arrest; conviction is a Class I misdemeanor. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. The prior version of section 28-101 is repealed. Creates the offense of "unlawful squatting" and assigns enforcement to law enforcement officers and their agencies. Officers with probable cause must issue a warning citation (probable-cause examples: signs of abandonment/inoccupancy or nonpermanent structures). The citation requires the recipient to appear within three business days before a designee of the officer's law enforcement agency and produce documentation authorizing residency (deed, rental agreement, proof of payments; photographic/electronic copies acceptable). Failure to appear or produce authentic authorization exposes the person to arrest and prosecution as a Class I misdemeanor. No specific state agencies, appropriations, or funding changes are referenced. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB445_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB445_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Transportation LB445 establishes the State Building Construction Alternatives Act and assigns administration to the state building division of the Department of Administrative Services (DAS). 109-1-LB447_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB447_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor LB447 directs the Department of Economic Development to update annually the workforce-housing construction cost caps (owner-occupied $275,000; rental $200,000 per unit) based on the most recent change in the Producer Price Index for All Commodities published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. 109-1-LB448_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB448_Intro_Copy.docx LB448 renames and codifies the Postconviction Relief Act and revises postconviction procedures. Key government actors: district courts (may appoint up to two attorneys, conduct hearings, order disclosure), county attorneys (must be served notice), appellate courts (appeals treated as civil), the Nebraska Supreme Court and U.S. Supreme Court (timing and retroactivity rules referenced), county boards (required to pay appointed counsel's fees and expenses in full as fixed by the court), prosecutors, and law enforcement (subject to new disclosure and discovery duties). The bill makes proceedings civil, taxes costs as in habeas cases, and expressly allows district courts to order prior trial/appellate counsel to produce complete case files. No statewide appropriations are created; the only funding directive requires county boards to pay appointed counsel. Adds a Postconviction Relief Act establishing relief for constitutional violations or actual innocence. Key provisions: standards for proving actual innocence (new evidence such as exculpatory DNA, alternative-suspect evidence, impeachment or undermining forensic science) and definitions for foundational and applied validity of forensic methods. Courts may excuse procedural defaults or timing limits to prevent manifest injustice, limited to whether the prisoner makes a colorable actual-innocence claim; failure to raise ineffective-assistance-at-trial on direct appeal is not a procedural default. The district court may order prior trial or appellate counsel to produce complete case files to the prisoner. No executive agencies or departments are newly created or mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB449_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB449_Intro_Copy.docx LB449 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §39-1365.01. It directs the department (the state transportation agency) to develop a specific, long-range state highway system plan, assign project priorities annually, and submit the plan and the report required by §39-1365.02 to the Legislature by December 1 each year; plans are to be referred to the appropriate legislative standing committees. The plan must (1) designate portions of the state highway system as expressways and (2) account for highway revenue by each district under §39-1102, requiring that at least 70% of revenue raised in each district be allocated to projects within that same district. The bill repeals the original section. Adds a requirement to account for highway revenue by each district referenced in section 39‑1102 and mandates that at least 70% of the revenue raised in each district be allocated to projects within that same district. No specific dollar appropriations or new agency names are included (it refers only to the districts in section 39‑1102). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB44_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB44_Intro_Copy.docx LB44 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-3001 (postconviction relief). It preserves court procedures: the court that imposed sentence (district court) must serve the county attorney, grant a prompt hearing unless records show no relief, may decide motions without producing the prisoner, and may bar successive similar motions. The one-year filing limitation for verified postconviction motions now runs from the latest of specified events, including a new trigger: the date the prisoner reaches 21 years of age. Other triggers reference the judgment becoming final, discovery of factual predicate, removal of state-created impediments, recognition of new constitutional rules by the U.S. or Nebraska Supreme Court (if made retroactive), and a procedural notice requirement tied to petitions for certiorari to the U.S. Supreme Court (filed in the district court within 30 days). No agencies receive new funding or appropriations. Adds a new clause "(f)" specifying that the relevant date/trigger is the prisoner's 21st birthday. No government agencies, departments, or any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced or changed. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB450_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB450_Intro_Copy.docx LB450 amends the Property Assessed Clean Energy Act, principally affecting municipalities (defined as counties, cities, or villages) that create clean energy assessment districts. Key changes for local government processes:\n- Expands eligible projects to explicitly include grid resiliency improvements and renewable energy systems.\n- Clarifies district creation: municipalities (not counties overlapping a city/village) may create districts; governing body of the municipality governs the district.\n- Requires a published public hearing before creation.\n- Requires ordinances (or county resolutions) to include a public-purpose finding, a standard assessment-contract form, designation of an official authorized to execute contracts, an application/eligibility process, and procedures for assessment calculation/collection.\n- For residential projects, mandates fixed interest rates and fixed repayment schedules for assessment installments.\n\nNo state agencies or departmental appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are specified. The bill repeals the original sections it amends. Adds a definition of "grid resiliency improvement" as any acquisition, installation, or modification—on public or private property—intended to anticipate, prepare for, withstand, respond to, and rapidly recover from major power disruptions. Examples expressly included: backup power generators (including those powered by renewable resources), solar panels with battery storage, and smart‑grid technology. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB451_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB451_Intro_Copy.docx Amends transfers from the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund and establishes related cash‑fund mechanics. Key agencies/officials: State Treasurer (authorized to make the transfers and deduct unclaimed‑property costs), Capitol Restoration administrator and commission (administer/use Capitol Restoration Cash Fund), State Investment Officer (invests fund balances), Legislature (may direct transfers to the General Fund), Auditor of Public Accounts (retains access to confidential records), and Department of Revenue (confidentiality standard reference).\n\nFunding changes:\n- On or before Nov. 1 each year 2025–2034, excess balances over $1 million in the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund: first $1 million transfers to the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund, remaining to the permanent school fund.\n- Beginning 2035, excess balances revert to transfers solely to the permanent school fund.\n- State Treasurer may deduct administrative costs into a newly created Unclaimed Property Cash Fund (investable; transfers to General Fund allowed at Legislature's direction).\n- Capitol Restoration Cash Fund receipts explicitly include legislative‑directed transfers from the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund and Nebraska Capital Construction Fund; fund used for Capitol restoration, collections, promotional work, and HVAC project manager costs. Adds an annual transfer schedule for the State Treasurer from the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund. Beginning 2025–2034, on or before November 1 each year the Treasurer must transfer any Trust Fund balance in excess of $1,000,000: the first $1,000,000 to the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund and any remaining excess to the Permanent School Fund. Beginning 2035, on or before November 1 each year the Treasurer must transfer any Trust Fund balance in excess of $1,000,000 entirely to the Permanent School Fund. Agencies/funds named: State Treasurer, Legislature (directive role), Unclaimed Property Trust Fund/Cash Fund, Capitol Restoration Cash Fund, and the Permanent School Fund. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB453_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB453_Final_Copy.docx LB453 amends Nebraska guardianship and conservatorship law. Key agencies: Nebraska State Patrol must forward nominated guardians’ fingerprints to the FBI and issue a criminal-history report to the State Court Administrator; the report must be filed with the court at least ten days before the appointment hearing unless waived or expedited. Applicants (except financial institutions, their officers/employees, or trust companies) pay the actual fingerprint/background-check cost. Temporary guardians and temporary conservators are exempt from the fingerprint/FBI check. The Public Guardian may serve as temporary guardian; if unable because of caseload limits (per §30-4115), the court shall appoint a limited temporary guardian subject to availability of funds appropriated under §81-3141. Counties pay court-fixed expenses/fees for such guardians and may seek reimbursement under §81-3141. Original sections are repealed. Authorizes the Nebraska State Patrol to submit applicants' fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and to forward those prints for a national criminal history record check. The State Patrol must issue a report to the State Court Administrator containing the applicant's criminal history record information. The applicant is required to pay the actual cost of fingerprinting and the criminal background check. No new appropriations or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB454_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB454_Final_Copy.docx LB454 amends statutory duties and funding administration for Nebraska’s behavioral health system. It clarifies that regional behavioral health authorities (RBHAs) operate under rules promulgated by the department and must submit annual budgets, funding/administration plans, and uniform fee/copay schedules (based on division standards) to the division. RBHAs may only directly provide division‑funded services after competitive bidding (with limited exceptions), written authorization from the director, and a contract with the division. The bill creates/defines the Behavioral Health Services Fund, administered by the division, to receive legislative appropriations and other directed funds (with Legislature-authorized transfers to the General Fund). Money credited under section 76-903 is dedicated to housing-related assistance for very low‑income adults with serious mental illness or substance abuse disorder; if obligations are met, up to 20% may be distributed to RBHAs for housing acquisition/rehabilitation. The state investment officer may invest fund balances. Adds that a behavioral health services provider may, with approval by "the department," establish new behavioral health services or expand existing capacity if the provider: (a) meets the department's network enrollment standards, (b) is enrolled as a network provider with both the department and a regional behavioral health authority, and (c) is contracted with a regional behavioral health authority. 109-1-LB455_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB455_Intro_Copy.docx LB455 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-144.01 (Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Act). The bill specifies the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court (and its administrator) as the custodian, prescribes forms/manner for filings and requests, and limits disclosure except when: the employee waives confidentiality; the requester is the subject employee (or their attorney/agent), the employer/insurer/risk pool/third-party administrator party to the report (or their counsel/agent), parties managing related claims or litigation, state or federal investigators compiling statistics, redacted employer-injury tallies, pleadings/exhibits, nonprofit grief outreach, or by court order. The original section is repealed. No appropriations or funding changes are included. Adds confidentiality rules for reports filed with the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court: reports are confidential except as needed for the Court to administer/enforce the Workers' Compensation Act. An employee may waive confidentiality; that waiver (or revocation) must follow a form prescribed by the administrator of the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court and remains effective across job changes until revoked. The Court must deny inspection requests unless the employee waived confidentiality or one of specified exceptions applies, including requests by the employee (or their attorney/authorized agent), the employer/insurer/risk management pool/third‑party administrator (or their attorneys/agents), attorneys handling related claims or lawsuits, state or federal investigators compiling statistics, requests to identify employer injury counts with employee redaction, pleadings/exhibits filed with the Court, nonprofits providing condolences/grief services, or by court order. All inspection requests must follow the administrator’s prescribed form. No funding or appropriation changes. DOCX | PDF

The Attorney General may, at the compensation court administrator’s request, move to convene a show‑cause panel and participate as a party. The court may examine insurer, pool, self‑insurer, adjuster, and third‑party administrator records (subject to work‑product and attorney‑client privileges) and adopt implementing rules. 109-1-LB460_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB460_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services The bill retains statutory directions that the State Treasurer make specified transfers from the State Settlement Cash Fund “on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services.” Those directed transfers listed are: $876,998 to the General Fund (on or before June 30, 2018); $1,756,639 to the General Fund (on or before June 30, 2019); $125,000 to the Legal Education for Public Service and Rural Practice Loan Repayment Assistance Fund (on or before April 30, 2018); $150,000 to that same loan repayment fund (on or before July 9, 2018); and a new transfer of $600,000 to the Nebraska Council on Economic Education Cash Fund (on or before July 1, 2025). 109-1-LB461_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB461_Intro_Copy.docx LB461 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §16-1027 governing municipal firefighter retirement benefits. 109-1-LB462_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB462_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill designates the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) as the "department" for child protection provisions and assigns multiple explicit duties: DHHS conducts or participates in investigations of child abuse/neglect; retains all reports and related records in a child protection tracking system; is to establish a statewide toll‑free reporting number (available 24/7); and is notified by law enforcement of reports the next working day. 109-1-LB464_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB464_Intro_Copy.docx LB464 (introduced by Bosn; referred to the Judiciary Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-101 and creates a criminal offense for organized retail crime. It defines key terms, allows aggregation of retail market value taken from one or more victims under a single charging instrument for offense classification (with limits), requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt of aggregate retail market value, and bars as a defense that merchandise was not actually stolen if it was represented as stolen. Prior convictions within ten years affect classification. The bill repeals the original §28-101. No state agencies or departments beyond the Legislature’s Judiciary Committee are named, and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds rules for aggregating retail market value in prosecutions of organized retail crime: losses from one scheme across multiple victims may be combined in the same charging instrument to determine offense classification, but may not be counted toward more than one offense. Limits lookback to ten years for prior acts. Establishes that aggregate retail market value is an essential element that the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt. Clarifies that it is not a defense that merchandise was not actually stolen if it was explicitly represented as stolen, embezzled, or converted. No government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned or changed. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB472_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB472_Intro_Copy.docx Creates the Office of Regulatory Management, led by a Director appointed by the Governor, to support and oversee state agencies' regulatory functions. The office must build and publish a baseline catalog of all regulatory requirements, require every state department/agency/division to submit internal reviews (initially within six months, then updated every two years or within 60 days of request), and publish a biennial report showing changes and estimated compliance costs for a median citizen or business. The office will collect, analyze, and publish agencies' evaluations, needs assessments, and cost‑benefit analyses, insist on empirical justification for regulatory action, and may request agencies and the Governor to reevaluate deficient actions. The office may not approve or reject agency regulations. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. Creates the Office of Regulatory Management under a Director appointed by and serving at the pleasure of the Governor. The office will supervise, support, and regulate other state agencies' regulatory functions and must be staffed appropriately. Agencies must inventory and submit all current regulatory requirements to the office (initial reviews due within six months; updates on request or every two years, or within 60 days of an update request). The office will maintain and publish a transparent baseline catalog and biennial report showing changes and estimated compliance costs for the median Nebraska citizen or business. The office collects and publishes agencies' evaluations and due diligence, requires rigorous evidence, cost–benefit and monetized/quantitative (or qualitative) estimates for new rules, may request reevaluation if best practices were not used, but cannot approve or reject agency rules. No funding or appropriation changes are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB477_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB477_Intro_Copy.docx LB477 amends the Workplace Privacy Act (sections 48-3502 and 48-3503). It expands the definition of "employer" to expressly include subcontractors and customers, and clarifies "personal Internet account." The bill prohibits employers from requiring employees or applicants to disclose login credentials, log into or alter personal Internet accounts, add contacts, or be compelled to use or wear location‑tracking apps/devices. An exception permits location-based contact tracing only during a Governor‑proclaimed pandemic state of emergency (pursuant to section 81-829.40) if limited to employer premises/work hours, authorized by the proclamation, and data are excluded from personnel files and destroyed within 48 hours after any Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)–recommended tracing period. Tracked property data linking employees must be stored by an independent third party and accessed only by warrant. No appropriations or funding changes. Adds an exception allowing employers to use electronic devices for contact tracing only if the Governor proclaims a pandemic state of emergency under section 81-829.40. The exception: (1) permits tracking solely for contact tracing; (2) limits tracking to employer premises during work hours; (3) prohibits inclusion of collected data in personnel files and requires destruction within 48 hours after the expiration of any tracing period recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Collected employee-associated tracking data must be stored by an independent third party and accessed only by warrant. No government funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. 109-1-LB487_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB487_Intro_Copy.docx LB487 creates the Restitution and Redress for Redlining Task Force (7 voting members: 2 appointed from the Commission on African American Affairs and 5 geographically distributed), appointed by the Governor with legislative committee confirmation. 109-1-LB48_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB48_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) must establish a Family Resource and Juvenile Assessment Center Pilot Program in metropolitan-class cities, operating 24/7 and terminating five years after the act's operative date. 109-1-LB492_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB492_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB492 amends the Nebraska Juvenile Code to specify that juvenile court jurisdiction includes any juvenile voluntarily relinquished pursuant to section 43-106.01 to the Department of Health and Human Services or to any child-placement agency licensed by the Department of Health and Human Services (amended §43-247(7)). The bill repeals the original sections replaced. It contains no changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. Adds a procedural defense to juvenile truancy adjudication: if, after subtracting specified excludable absences, a child has accrued fewer than 20 unexcused absences in a school year, the petition may be defended. Excludable absences include lack of adequate transportation; the school's failure to coordinate agreed interventions/attendance supports; physical or mental illness excused by a parent/guardian (with or without a doctor's note); or absences otherwise excused by the school or court. Referrals must indicate which unexcused absences, if any, were excused by a parent/guardian for physical or mental illness. 109-1-LB493_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB493_Intro_Copy.docx LB493 adopts the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (an anti‑SLAPP framework), eliminates prior provisions relating to actions involving public petition and participation, and repeals Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-21,241 through 25-21,246. The bill vests Nebraska courts with new procedures: a defendant may file a special motion to dismiss within 60 days of service; filing triggers an automatic stay of related proceedings (with limited discovery allowed for good cause); courts must hear the motion within 60 days (or later for permitted discovery/good cause) and rule within 60 days after the hearing. A party may appeal an adverse order as of right within 21 days. Courts must award costs, reasonable attorney fees, and litigation expenses to a prevailing moving party. The act is declared an emergency. No appropriations or agency budget changes are included. Adds procedural rules for special motions under the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act: filing such a motion stays other proceedings (including discovery and hearings) with narrow exceptions (limited discovery where necessary, injunctions for imminent public health/safety, motions for fees). Courts must hear the motion within 60 days (subject to limited extensions). Establishes standards for dismissal with prejudice, effects of voluntary dismissals on fee awards, a 21‑day appeal filing deadline, and mandatory award of costs, reasonable attorney fees, and litigation expenses to a prevailing moving party. No government agencies, departments, or changes to funding/appropriations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB496_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB496_Intro_Copy.docx LB496 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-6,111 (Rules of the Road) governing animals and animal-drawn vehicles on roadways. Riders/drivers of animals, animal-drawn vehicles, farm tractors, or implements of husbandry retain the rights and duties of vehicle drivers except where inapplicable. If their slowness obstructs traffic they must move to the nearest shoulder, except where subsection (3) applies. Subsection (3) (defining livestock) requires motor vehicle operators to exercise caution when approaching/herding livestock, stop if given a raised-hand distress signal (unless stopping would cause an accident), turn off the engine if requested, and yield right-of-way to livestock on the highway. No state agencies or departments are referenced and there are no funding or appropriation changes. 109-1-LB497_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB497_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB497 references the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) in three places relating to residency and payment rules for students in out-of-home placements. 109-1-LB498_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB498_Intro_Copy.docx LB498 requires the Department of Education to recalculate and timely certify foundation aid, district budget authority, and allowable reserve percentages on or before June 15, 2025, and on or before March 1 each year thereafter, and nullifies any such 2025-26 certifications completed before the bill’s effective date. Foundation aid: $1,500 per formula student for 2023-24 and 2024-25; beginning 2025-26 per‑student aid is the prior year amount increased by the annual CPI‑U percentage. Twenty-four percent of total foundation aid each year must be paid from the Education Future Fund. For 2025-26 and thereafter, only 60% of foundation aid is counted as a formula resource (100% for 2023-24 and 2024-25). The department must certify amounts to the Director of Administrative Services, Auditor of Public Accounts, Governor, Appropriations Committee, Education Committee, and local systems; the Appropriations Committee must include certified state aid in its budget recommendations. Adds an inflation‑indexing formula for state foundation aid starting in school year 2025‑26: each district’s aid equals the prior year’s foundation aid per formula student, increased by the prior calendar year’s percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U) as published by the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics, multiplied by the district’s current number of formula students. The only federal agency named is the BLS (CPI‑U data). No specific dollar appropriations are set; the change mandates how future education funding is calculated. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB4_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB4_Intro_Copy.docx LB4 amends statutes to add the Telecommunications Exchange Deregulation Act under the Public Service Commission's (PSC) jurisdiction (amending section 75-109.01 and section 86-124). Key PSC authorities: accept petitions (only from electing local exchange carriers) to deregulate exchanges, decide within 90 days, reclassify carriers, require information from carriers while protecting proprietary confidentiality, and adopt rules to administer and enforce the Act.\n\nDeregulation criteria include population thresholds or presence of competing carriers (including a 75% area-coverage option). Deregulated carriers are relieved of carrier-of-last-resort obligations, certain service-quality and reporting requirements, and pricing mandates except when pricing is a condition of receiving PSC‑administered grant funds. Transitioning carriers lose eligibility for Nebraska Telecommunications Universal Service Fund support for deregulated exchanges and the PSC must reduce fund allocations in its funding formula to account for deregulation. Original sections repealed. The added text gives the commission authority to require carrier disclosures, keep proprietary information confidential under section 84-712.05, and decide deregulation petitions (only an electing local exchange carrier may file) within 90 days. The commission will use most recent U.S. Bureau of the Census data to determine exchange population, may reclassify carriers, and adopt rules to administer the Act. Funding changes: transitioning carriers are ineligible for Nebraska Telecommunications Universal Service Fund support for deregulated exchanges, and the commission must, insofar as feasible in the funding formula, reduce their allocations to account for deregulated exchanges. 109-1-LB500_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB500_Intro_Copy.docx Creates the School Financing Review Commission (21 members) with specified membership including the Commissioner of Education (or designee), a gubernatorial appointee, three nonvoting legislative members (including members of the Education and Revenue Committees), the Property Tax Administrator (or designee), a postsecondary expert in school finance, a member of the Educational Service Unit Coordinating Council, regional school board members and administrators, a certificated teacher, and six at-large members. The commission must report initially to the Governor, State Board of Education, and Legislature by December 1, 2025; review the State Department of Education’s mission/goals; evaluate implementation of the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act; solicit school input; and file biennial adequacy-of-funding reports to the Governor, State Board, and Legislature on July 1 of even years 2028–2034. Emergency clause makes it effective on enactment. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. Creates a School Financing Review Commission (21 members) including: the Commissioner of Education (or designee); a Governor appointee; nonvoting legislative members; the Property Tax Administrator (or designee); a postsecondary rep with school‑finance expertise; an Educational Service Unit Coordinating Council member; multiple school board members and administrators from Class III–V districts; a certificated teacher; and six at‑large members. 109-1-LB505_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB505_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Agriculture, Department of Health and Human Services Intent to appropriate $10,000,000 for FY2025‑26 and $10,000,000 for FY2026‑27 in Federal Funds to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program No. 347 (Public Assistance). 109-1-LB506_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB506_Intro_Copy.docx Creates the Landlord and Tenant Radon Awareness Act. It requires lessors (which may include government agencies or subdivisions) to provide prospective tenants and tenants, on application or request, a radon-hazard disclosure form and any available radon test records; test results must be furnished within ten days of receipt. The bill references licensing under the Radiation Control Act for "radon measurement specialists" and "radon mitigation specialists," tying practitioner credentials to that regulatory framework. It bars lessors from withholding security deposits to pay for radon testing or mitigation, except where a tenant installed a mitigation system without the lessor’s consent and the system was not installed by a licensed radon mitigation specialist. Applies to leases executed on or after the act’s effective date. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. Adds the "Landlord and Tenant Radon Awareness Act," requiring lessors — expressly including any government agency or subdivision thereof — to provide prospective tenants (at application and on request) with radon information and any test results within 10 days of receipt. It mandates use of a specified radon-hazard disclosure form and recognizes radon measurement and mitigation specialists as individuals licensed under the Radiation Control Act (i.e., subject to the State's licensing regime). The State of Nebraska is cited as recommending testing and mitigation. It bars withholding security deposits to pay for radon testing/mitigation except where a tenant installed an unapproved or improperly installed mitigation system; itemized withholding must be provided. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB507_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB507_Intro_Copy.docx LB507 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-1129. It directs resident school boards to provide specified services for children with disabilities, including: (a) transportation expenses when a child must temporarily leave the district due to lack of services; (b) transportation when a child must attend a facility other than the normal attendance facility or requires special transportation; (c) certified visiting teachers for homebound children; (d) correspondence instruction; or (e) other instructional methods approved by the Commissioner of Education. Parent/guardian drivers are to be reimbursed at the mileage rate in §81-1176 for actual miles traveled, with payments calculated for one child if multiple children are transported and no payment for mileage not actually driven. Nonresident and resident districts may agree that the nonresident district provide transportation for preschool/child-care enrollees. The bill repeals the original section. No new appropriations or budget allocations are specified. The added phrase "enrolled in the school district" does not reference any government agency or department and contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. It appears to clarify or limit eligibility/coverage to persons who are enrolled in the school district. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB508_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB508_Intro_Copy.docx LB508 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §55-117 to clarify control and limits on deployment of the Nebraska National Guard. It reiterates the Governor’s authority (through the Adjutant General) to call the Guard and additional militia for state service and to exercise control over local police when quelling riots, rebellions, or insurrections. The bill prohibits ordering the Guard into "active combat" for U.S. military service except where U.S. Congress has declared war or called the Guard to execute federal law, suppress insurrection, or repel invasions. The Governor must review current federal orders placing Guard members into active combat, return any members if orders are noncompliant, and report findings and actions to the Legislature’s Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee within 30 days. "Active combat" is defined in three categorical terms. Original §55-118 is repealed. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds limits on deployment of the Nebraska National Guard: it may not be placed into "active combat" except where the U.S. Congress has declared war or has called the Guard to execute federal law, suppress insurrection, or repel invasions under the U.S. Constitution. Requires the Governor to review all current federal orders placing Nebraska Guardsmen into active combat for compliance with that standard, immediately return any noncompliant personnel to Nebraska, and report the review and any actions to the Legislature’s Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee within 30 days after the review. "Active combat" is defined (armed conflict; hazardous service in a foreign state relating to armed conflict; duty via an instrumentality of war). No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB509_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB509_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it administration and oversight responsibilities for the Opportunity Scholarships Act. The Department must certify (and may revoke certification of) scholarship‑granting organizations, receive and process notifications of taxpayers' intended contributions, and determine and notify organizations within 30 days if requested tax credits exceed availability. If partial amounts are available, the Department must notify organizations (which then notify taxpayers) within three business days. The Department will consider notifications in receipt order to enforce annual tax‑credit caps: $25 million for 2025–2027, with formulaic increases up to $100 million. No direct appropriations or other funding changes for the Department are specified. Defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it primary administration duties for the new Opportunity Scholarships Act. The Department must certify and may revoke certification of scholarship‑granting organizations, review their applications for compliance, and process organization notifications of taxpayers' intended tax‑credit contributions. The Department has 30 days to notify organizations if an intended credit would exceed the annual cap, and will report available amounts so organizations can inform taxpayers (within three business days). Contributions must be made 31–60 days after notice or the Department will exclude them from the cap. The act creates an annual statewide tax‑credit limit: $25 million for 2025–2027, then increased year‑to‑year by 125% (if prior year exceeded 90% of the cap) or 100% otherwise, up to a $100 million maximum. (No direct appropriation line items are added.) DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB50_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB50_Final_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB50 requires that all revenue remitted by the Department of Revenue under section 77-6203 be passed to county treasurers for distribution (5% to the local community college area; remainder to affected local taxing entities). It further prohibits the Department of Revenue from retaining any revenue collected under sections 77-6201 to 77-6204 or using, transferring, pledging, or allocating those funds to or from the General Fund, preventing diversion of the nameplate capacity tax receipts to state General Fund balances. Adds a two-part revenue allocation: (a) 5% of the specified revenue is to be distributed to the community college area where the renewable energy generation facility is located; (b) the remainder is to be distributed under the existing subdivision (1)(b) formula. For the Department of Revenue: this creates a new allocation instruction DOR must implement when calculating distributions, but the amendment does not create a new appropriation, appropriation line, or change total revenue—only the internal distribution percentages.
