109-1-LB510_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB510_Intro_Copy.docx LB510 amends state sales-tax and Good Life district statutes and assigns specific duties to the Department (Department of Revenue). Key points for agencies and fiscal effects:\n\n- Department: retains authority to approve/adjust/terminate Good Life districts, evaluate eligibility, accept evidence of investment commitments from applicants, cities, property owners or others, and transmit application/maps to affected cities or villages (with confidentiality limits). It may approve district development/design standards after a hearing. Termination limited to failure-to-commit thresholds (10% in 3 years; 50% in 7; 75% in 10) and not before three years.\n\n- Sales tax: reduced state rate (2.75%) on transactions in Good Life districts continues, but commencing July 1, 2025 it applies only after the city or village has imposed a local sales or occupation tax of at least 2.75%.\n\n- Cities/villages: must obtain voter approval before appropriating local revenues (including local option sales/use taxes and occupation taxes) to a Good Life District economic development program; election procedures specified.\n\n- Applicants must certify anticipated state sales-tax diversions will be offset or exceeded by sales taxes generated by development. The act is effective on enactment. - Changes the state sales tax effective July 1, 2025: a general rate of 5.5%, but transactions within a portion of a Good Life district located inside a city or village are taxed at 2.75% if that city or village imposes a local sales or occupation tax of at least 2.75% on those transactions. \n- Clarifies that, on and after July 1, 2025, transactions in a Good Life district receive the reduced state rate referenced in statute. \n- Refers repeatedly to "the department" (agency administering Good Life district matters): it must accept applicant evidence and treat the property owner(s) or the city/village as the Good Life district applicant for statutory purposes, and it may not terminate a Good Life district until at least three years after establishment. \n- Prohibits a city or village from using eminent domain to acquire property in a Good Life district for transfer or sale to a private party. 109-1-LB511_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB511_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles The bill imposes agency-specific duties and procedural changes. Department of Correctional Services must deliver, have signed, retain, and distribute Sex Offender Registration Act written notices to persons committed for registrable offenses prior to release (or before discharge, parole, or work release if immediately incarcerated) and forward a copy to the Nebraska State Patrol. Department of Health and Human Services must conduct education/outreach on healthy families, pornography, and prostitution; require affiliation agreements with qualified third‑party domestic violence/sexual‑assault providers under the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act; and assaults on DHHS employees are enumerated as racketeering offenses under the Public Protection Act. Department of Motor Vehicles must include the duty‑to‑register notice on operator and commercial license applications and its records must be checked when seized property is a Nebraska‑titled motor vehicle in forfeiture proceedings. The bill creates a law‑enforcement grant program but includes no specific appropriations to these three agencies. - Department of Correctional Services: New duty requiring DCS (or city/county jails) to have persons subject to sex-offender registration read and sign a written notification explaining the duty to register, retain a signed copy, and provide copies to the registrant and the Sex Offender Registration and Community Notification Division of the Nebraska State Patrol. No dedicated funding or appropriation to DCS is included.\n\n- Department of Health and Human Services: No changes, duties, or funding allocations appear in the added text.\n\n- Department of Motor Vehicles: No changes, duties, or funding allocations appear in the added text.\n\n- Related appropriations included elsewhere: intent to appropriate $100,000 General Fund (FY2025-26) to the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice for grants to law enforcement; intent to appropriate $25,000 General Fund (FY2025-26) to the Nebraska State Patrol for Sex Offender Registration Act implementation. 109-1-LB513_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB513_Final_Copy.docx LB513 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §24-201.01 to increase compensation for the Nebraska Supreme Court: effective July 1, 2025 the Chief Justice and associate justices' salary is set at $228,431.18, and on July 1, 2026 it rises to $231,857.65 (the statute also notes the July 1, 2024 figure of $225,055.35). Salaries are payable in equal monthly installments. The bill reiterates that the Chief Justice and Supreme Court judges may not hold other paid public office or compensated federal employment. 109-1-LB514_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB514_Intro_Copy.docx LB514 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §14-102 to expressly authorize cities of the metropolitan class to regulate housing authorities operating in the city. New powers allow the city to require code enforcement and pest control for housing authority–owned/controlled properties; mandate regular inspections; require registration of managed rental properties under local rental-registration ordinances; impose penalties for code violations or mismanagement; and require monthly reports to the city council. The bill repeals the original section. No changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds a new provision authorizing cities of the metropolitan class to regulate housing authorities operating within them. It directs municipal code enforcement and pest-control measures for properties owned/controlled by such housing authorities; mandates regular inspections; requires that managed properties be registered under the city’s rental-registration ordinance; permits the city to set penalties for code violations and mismanagement; and requires monthly updates to the city council. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB515_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB515_Intro_Copy.docx LB515 (introduced by Quick; referred to the Health and Human Services Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §38-28,104 (Pharmacy Practice Act). It (1) reiterates required prescription elements before dispensing by a pharmacist or a practitioner holding a pharmacy license under §38-2850(1) and (2) authorizes pharmacists to provide an emergency refill (up to a 30‑day supply or the most recent refill amount, whichever is less) when refill authorization cannot be readily obtained, provided: the pharmacist documents prescription information from a label, any pharmacy record, or a common database; the drug is not a controlled substance; it is a maintenance medication; and interruption would harm the patient. No funding or appropriations are included. The original section is repealed. No government agencies, departments, appropriations, or funding changes are referenced. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB516_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB516_Intro_Copy.docx Bill LB516 directs the repeal of two statutory provisions (sections 68-130 and 81-1139.01, Reissue Revised Statutes of Nebraska) and removes an existing county-level requirement regarding office space tied to the Department of Health and Human Services. 109-1-LB517_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB517_Intro_Copy.docx LB517 amends duties of the state school security director (appointed under section 79-2,143) within the State Department of Education. It requires each school district to provide the director with safety and security plans, annual inspection information for protective door assemblies, door‑locking systems, and double‑entry doors, and other requested security information (submissions may be withheld under Neb. Rev. Stat. §84‑712.05(9)). The director must collect plans, recommend minimum standards to the State Board of Education, conduct building security assessments, establish protective‑door standards requiring annual inspections by trained inspectors, identify deficiencies and advise school boards, develop training and mental‑health/behavioural programs (per §79‑2,146), set tornado preparedness standards, assist private/denominational/parochial schools, recommend cyberbullying resources, and administer duties under the School Safety and Security Reporting System Act. The original section is repealed. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds requirements that local school boards/school districts establish standards for and annually inspect protective door assemblies in student-instruction buildings, requiring inspections be done by trained inspectors with appropriate knowledge, training, and experience. Defines "protective door assemblies" to include doors with panic or fire-exit hardware; door assemblies in exit enclosures; electronically controlled egress doors; and doors with special locking arrangements (delayed egress, sensor-released egress, elevator‑lobby doors). No other state agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB518_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB518_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services LB518 amends §83‑1,100.03 to require the Department of Correctional Services, in consultation with the Board of Parole, to: adopt rules to reduce the number of inmates who serve their entire sentence and are released without supervision; ensure parolees receive at least nine months of supervision; and require that each parole-eligible inmate be assessed using a validated risk-and-needs assessment provided by the department, with assessed risk, criminal history, program completion, institutional conduct, and related factors incorporated into release decisions. The department and board must jointly submit an annual electronic report (by Feb. 1) to the Legislature, Supreme Court, and Governor detailing rates and characteristics of unsupervised releases and recommending policy/practice changes. No appropriations or funding changes are specified. The added text requires that the report be submitted electronically and enumerates three required sections: (a) Describe, (b) Document, and (c) Provide. The provided excerpt contains only those headings—no substantive content or details about what must be described, documented, or provided. There is no mention of the Department of Correctional Services, nor any language changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for that agency. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB51_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB51_Final_Copy.docx LB51 ratifies and implements the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact (34 U.S.C. 40316). It directs the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety to execute the compact and designates the Superintendent (or designee) as Nebraska’s compact officer. The Nebraska State Patrol is named the state repository for criminal history record information and authorized to perform duties necessary to carry out the compact, including adopting rules and procedures for interstate exchange of criminal history information with federal authorities for noncriminal-justice purposes. Ratification remains effective until the Legislature expressly renounces it. The bill affirms that the compact does not alter existing Nebraska obligations or public-access provisions under state law (including the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. The added language ratifies the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact (34 U.S.C. 40316). It names the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety to execute the compact for the state and to serve (or designate a designee as) the state's compact officer responsible for in‑state administration. The Nebraska State Patrol is designated the official repository of criminal history record information for compact purposes and is authorized to perform necessary actions, adopt rules and procedures, and coordinate exchanges with the federal government for noncriminal‑justice uses. Ratification remains until the Legislature expressly renounces it. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. The compact does not alter existing Nebraska State Patrol statutory duties or public access under state law. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB520_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB520_Intro_Copy.docx LB520 amends Reissue Revised Statutes to redefine "bed and breakfast establishment," carve specific food-safety obligations into the Nebraska Pure Food Act, and add fire- and life-safety requirements to the State Fire Code. The State Fire Marshal is directed to include bed-and-breakfast provisions in the State Fire Code and to enforce them via inspections, plan review, and code compliance (including existing plan‑review fees and a $50 penalty for late submissions). The bill requires the unspecified "department" to offer a food‑handler examination and certify bed‑and‑breakfast operators. Operational requirements (smoke/heat alarms, emergency lighting, egress or sprinkler compliance, fire extinguishers, kitchen suppression for larger operations) are placed on establishments. No appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations are included. Original sections amended are repealed. Adds extensive health and fire-safety requirements for bed and breakfast establishments. Key agency role: “the department” must certify operators (by exam), approve thawing methods, and may require demonstrated testing/maintenance procedures for battery-powered smoke alarms and emergency lighting. New mandates cover food safety (pasteurized Grade A milk only; limits on home-canned goods; temperature controls; utensil/hand hygiene; exclusion of infected food handlers), storage and sanitation, and laundry/animal separation. Fire/safety rules require smoke/heat detectors, egress standards (secondary egress or sprinkler exemption), 18-month compliance window to install secondary egress or a sprinkler system, specified fire extinguishers, and kitchen fire-suppression hoods for B&Bs serving hot meals to >10 guests. No funding or appropriation changes included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB521_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB521_Final_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Motor Vehicles LB521 directs the Department of Motor Vehicles to cooperate with the Secretary of State to match DMV records to the statewide voter registration list and to: provide a combined voter‑registration application at license/ID issuance; electronically transmit registration data (including digital image and signature) to county election officials within specified timelines; and notify counties when a registrant surrenders a Nebraska license/ID to another state. 109-1-LB522_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB522_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Labor LB522 ties newly authorized cost‑of‑living adjustments for certain long‑term weekly workers’ compensation benefits to the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers "as prepared by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics." The bill defines the COLA percentage as the greater of 1% or the most recent 12‑month CPI‑W change, with annual determinations and automatic adjustments beginning 2026. No provisions in the bill reference the Nebraska Department of Labor specifically, nor does the bill include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor. Beginning Jan 1, 2026, weekly workers’ compensation income benefits that have lasted longer than 12 months will receive annual cost‑of‑living adjustments (COLAs). COLA = greater of 1% or the 12‑month change in the CPI‑W as published by the U.S. Dept. of Labor, BLS. The Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Court will set the annual COLA each Jan 1; benefits are adjusted at the end of each 12‑month period by multiplying the current weekly benefit by that COLA and rounding up to the next dollar. Adjustments cannot exceed the statutory maximum weekly benefit (different citations apply to the two affected subdivisions); one provision clarifies section 48‑122.03 will not cap COLA increases. No Department of Labor administrative duties, new appropriations, or funding changes are created. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB523_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB523_Intro_Copy.docx LB523 creates the Student Teacher Compensation Act. It directs the Nebraska State Department of Education to establish a stipend program paying $4,000 per student‑teaching semester to eligible applicants enrolled in accredited teacher education programs. The bill requires the department to submit an annual report to the Legislature (due December 15) with counts of stipends awarded, demographic and geographic distribution, school type, and anonymized feedback. The State Board of Education may adopt rules to implement the Act. The Legislature states intent to appropriate funds annually to the State Department of Education for stipends; the department may also seek grant, private, or federal funding. Accrediting agencies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education are referenced for program eligibility. Operative July 1, 2025; emergency clause makes it effective on passage. Creates the Student Teacher Compensation Act. The State Department of Education must create a stipend program providing $4,000 per student‑teaching semester to eligible student teachers who apply. The Legislature intends to appropriate funds annually to the State Department of Education for these stipends; the department may also pursue grants, private donations, or federal funding. The State Board of Education may adopt rules to implement the Act. 109-1-LB524_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB524_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services The bill directs the State Treasurer to transfer specified General Fund sums to the Education Future Fund on dates and in amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. 109-1-LB525_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB525_Intro_Copy.docx Creates the Agricultural Data Privacy Act and assigns enforcement and administrative responsibilities to state officials. The Attorney General has exclusive authority to enforce the Act, with power to seek injunctive relief and recover civil penalties (amount left unspecified in text). Collected civil penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution pursuant to Article VII, section 5 of the Nebraska Constitution. The Attorney General must publish guidance on controller/processor responsibilities and consumer rights and provide an online complaint mechanism on the AG website. The bill prohibits private rights of action and declares contract provisions that waive or limit controller/processor obligations void. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included. Adds the "Agricultural Data Privacy Act" and designates the Nebraska Attorney General as the exclusive enforcement authority—authorized to seek injunctive relief and recover civil penalties (amount left unspecified). Collected penalties are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution per the Nebraska Constitution. The Attorney General must publish guidance on controllers' and processors' responsibilities and producers' rights on the AG website and provide an online complaint mechanism. No new appropriations or specific funding/budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB526_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB526_Final_Copy.docx LB526 authorizes Nebraska public power suppliers—defined as public power districts, municipal electric utilities, or other government entities providing electric service—to impose requirements on cryptocurrency mining operations (≥1 MW) to recover infrastructure upgrade costs. Permitted measures include requiring direct payment or letters of credit and imposing terms and conditions; such requirements must be fair, reasonable, and not unduly discriminatory. Before imposing requirements, suppliers must perform a load study to assess costs and impacts. Prospective miners must notify the local supplier and meet interconnection rules. Each supplier must publish on its website the count of mining operations under its jurisdiction and each operation’s annual energy use. Suppliers may interrupt service to miners per existing rate schedules and policies. No state appropriations or new budget allocations are specified. Summary:\n- Defines "public power supplier" as public power districts, municipal electric utilities, or other government entities providing electric service.\n- Authorizes public power suppliers to impose requirements on cryptocurrency mining operations (≥1 MW) to cover infrastructure upgrade costs, including direct payment or letters of credit, and other terms and conditions.\n- Requires requirements to be fair, reasonable, and not unduly discriminatory, and mandates a load study before imposing them.\n- Requires prospective miners to notify the local public power supplier and follow its interconnection rules.\n- Requires suppliers to publish counts of mining operations and each operation’s annual energy use on their websites.\n- Allows suppliers to interrupt service per existing rate schedules/policies.\n- No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. 109-1-LB530_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB530_Final_Copy.docx Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Transportation The bill affects five agencies as follows:\n\n- DHHS: Peace officers delivering certain juveniles must deliver them to DHHS, which may place/supervise temporary placements, consent to emergency medical/behavioral treatment, receive a written county-attorney report within 24 hours, and whose temporary custody ends if no court order within 48 hours. Requirements: specialty pharmacies must follow federal shipping laws (including USP general chapter 800), provide 24/7 access to a pharmacist or nurse, accept refill requests per PBM/health carrier procedures, and follow DSCSA track‑and‑trace for compounded/manipulated drugs. When a PBM or health carrier selects a specialty pharmacy, providers must give five business days’ delivery notice; shipments to providers require signature. PBMs/health carriers must maintain appeal/exception processes and may not force patient pickup for provider administration. Operative January 1, 2026. No funding or appropriation changes. Adds rules for specialty pharmacies dispensing clinician‑administered outpatient drugs, requiring compliance with applicable federal drug‑shipment laws (including United States Pharmacopeia General Chapter 800) and the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (21 U.S.C. 360eee et seq.) for track‑and‑trace of compounded or manipulated products. Specialty pharmacies must provide 24/7 access to a pharmacist or nurse, accept refill requests per payer utilization procedures, obtain five business days' notice of delivery details and a signature on delivery to providers, and not ship drugs to patients for them to transport to providers. Pharmacy benefit managers/health carriers must publish an appeal/exception process for delivery failures or urgent one‑time use. No agencies are newly created and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF

Stat. §48-601 (Employment Security Law) to disqualify claimants from unemployment benefits for any week in which they (1) fail to respond to a job offer within two business days or (2) fail to appear for a scheduled job interview without notifying the prospective employer. The bill repeals the original §48-601. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds disqualification criteria: an individual loses benefits for any week in which they (a) fail to respond to a job offer within two business days, or (b) miss a scheduled job interview without notifying the prospective employer. It requires "the department" to establish an online portal, email address, and telephone hotline for employers to report such failures. Before denying benefits under this section, the department must verify any employer-submitted information. No specific agency beyond "the department" is named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB545_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB545_Intro_Copy.docx LB545 (109th Legislature, 2025), introduced by Sen. 109-1-LB546_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB546_Intro_Copy.docx LB546 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-829.40 to clarify gubernatorial authority over emergencies and emergency management. It reaffirms the Governor’s responsibility for emergency management, gives the Governor general direction and control of the Nebraska Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), and authorizes assuming direct operational control of emergency management functions. Proclamations must describe the emergency, be promptly disseminated, and be filed with NEMA, the Secretary of State, and clerks of affected local governments. A proclamation activates state, city, village, county, and interjurisdictional emergency management organizations and plans and authorizes deployment of forces, supplies, and facilities. The Governor is commander in chief of the militia and may suspend regulatory statutes and utilize state and political‑subdivision resources. The Legislature may terminate a proclamation. No funding or appropriation changes are included. The act takes effect immediately. No underlined (added) text found in this bill. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB547_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB547_Intro_Copy.docx LB547 revises Nebraska tax exemptions for disabled and blind veterans. It requires that motor vehicle and mobile‑home tax exemptions apply only when the veteran's disability or blindness is recognized by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The bill aligns the term “disabled veteran” with 5 U.S.C. 2108 as of January 1, 2025. Motor vehicle exemption eligibility adds VA recognition, an honorable discharge or separation, and an approved application under section 60-3,189. The mobile‑home exemption likewise requires VA service‑connected recognition and expands acceptable separation status to include “general (under honorable conditions).” Operative January 1, 2026; original sections repealed. No changes to funding or appropriations. Adds a definition of "veteran" by adopting the meaning given in 5 U.S.C. 2108 as that statute existed on January 1, 2025. No federal agency or department is named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes included. The inserted wording contains a redundant/unclear phrase ("veteran means such veteran's veteran"). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB548_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB548_Intro_Copy.docx LB548 authorizes a "political subdivision" (e.g., a municipality) that owns and operates a natural gas system to contract directly to sell natural gas to industrial consumers located in Nebraska that average at least 3 billion BTU per day. Contracts must run at least two years (excluding renewals). Eligible industrial users may not, at the time of contract execution, be customers for the same operations of any investor‑owned or other government‑owned gas system. The facility is deemed within the political subdivision's service area for contract purposes. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided. Allows any political subdivision that owns/operates a natural gas system to contract to sell natural gas to industrial consumers located in Nebraska that average at least 3 billion BTU/day. Contracts must run at least two years (excluding renewals). The industrial buyer cannot already be served by an investor‑owned or governmentally‑owned gas system for the operations receiving service at contract execution. For contract purposes the buyer’s facility is treated as inside the subdivision’s gas distribution service area. No specific state agencies or departments are named and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB549_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB549_Intro_Copy.docx LB549 authorizes school boards to employ chaplains (including volunteers) without a Nebraska teaching, administrative, or special-services certificate. Chaplains must be licensed/ordained by a religious organization, subject to a criminal history background check (including FBI fingerprinting) conducted by the Nebraska State Patrol at the Commissioner of Education’s request. The Commissioner may deny a chaplain’s employment eligibility for felony convictions or misdemeanors involving abuse, neglect, or sexual misconduct, with consideration of mitigating information. The bill amends the State Department of Education/Commissioner enforcement provisions (secs. 79-804, 79-805) to exempt chaplains from certificate registration, withholding of school funds, and related board liability. School boards must adopt employment policies for chaplains. Boards set processing costs for background checks, which applicants pay; costs are limited to actual direct processing costs. No appropriations or budgetary allocations are included. Creates authorization for local school boards to employ (including volunteers) chaplains and requires school boards to adopt policies on hiring, discipline, continued education, and termination. Agencies mentioned: local school boards and the Commissioner of Education, who may deny a chaplain’s eligibility based on a criminal history record information check conducted under section 79-814.01. Chaplains need not hold state teaching or special services certificates. Chaplains must undergo the criminal background check and pay any required fees. The provision is optional for school boards and excludes chaplains covered by section 1 of the act. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB54_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB54_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB54 appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services for FY2025‑26 to raise reimbursement rates for developmental disability service providers. Specifically, the bill: (1) appropriates $XXX from the General Fund to DHHS, Program 424, to implement an 11% increase in those reimbursement rates (funds restricted to that purpose); and (2) appropriates $XXX in Federal Funds to DHHS, Program 348, for the same 11% increase (also restricted). The act takes effect immediately as an emergency measure. - Appropriates $XXX General Fund for FY2025‑26 to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program 424, to implement an 11% increase in reimbursement rates for developmental disability service providers; funds are restricted to that purpose. \n- Appropriates $XXX Federal Funds for FY2025‑26 to DHHS, Program 348, to implement the same 11% reimbursement increase for developmental disability service providers; these funds are likewise restricted to that purpose. 109-1-LB550_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB550_Intro_Copy.docx LB550 requires school districts to adopt a policy excusing students to attend released‑time courses for religious instruction, subject to parental consent and specified safeguards. School districts may not use public funds for the courses, and courses generally must be off district property unless the district has a neutral equal‑access policy opening facilities to community groups. Students excused to attend such courses "shall be considered as attending" their school for purposes of determining school funding and satisfying attendance requirements. Districts may award academic credit for released‑time courses only after secular evaluation criteria. The bill preserves equal access to district‑provided funds, benefits, or services for sponsoring entities and authorizes aggrieved persons or organizations to sue school districts for actual damages, equitable/declaratory relief, and attorney's fees. It takes effect immediately. Adds requirements for school districts regarding "released time" courses: districts must allow such courses off campus under a neutral equal‑access policy, may grant secularly evaluated academic credit, and cannot base credit decisions on religious content. For funding, any student excused to attend a released time course is still counted as attending the home school for purposes of school funding and attendance calculations. Districts also may not deny released‑time sponsors equal access to funds, benefits, or services the district provides to community groups. Enforcement: individuals or organizations may sue the school district for violations and seek actual damages, equitable/declaratory relief, and reasonable attorney fees. No new appropriations or specific budget allocations are made. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB551_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB551_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services LB551 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §85‑1511 to require community college boards to complete and file annual comprehensive audits with the Auditor of Public Accounts, the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education, and the Department of Administrative Services. Financial audits covering the most recently completed fiscal year must be filed by November 15; audits of full‑time equivalent student enrollment and reimbursable educational unit totals must be filed by August 15. The bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The added provisions prohibit the Board of Regents, the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges, and community college boards from creating or authorizing academic tenure for any employee who is not already tenured as of the bill’s effective date. Each board must adopt written policies covering employee agreements; acceptable dismissal grounds (including just cause, program discontinuance, financial exigency); annual faculty evaluations; minimum standards of practice; standards for review and discipline; and procedures for dismissal under the listed grounds. There are no provisions affecting the Department of Administrative Services, nor any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB552_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB552_Intro_Copy.docx LB552 bars public postsecondary institutions from establishing or maintaining "diversity, equity, and inclusion" (DEI) offices or conducting DEI programs that influence hiring or employment, promote differential treatment based on protected characteristics, implement race-/gender‑referenced policies, require employee or student participation as a condition of employment or enrollment, or use public funds for DEI. "Appropriate governing board" is defined as the Board of Regents (University of Nebraska), Board of Trustees (Nebraska State Colleges), or a community college's governing board. Exceptions include sexual‑harassment training, offices staffed by licensed attorneys solely for legal compliance, statements to grantors/accreditors about support for first‑generation/low‑income/underserved students or antidiscrimination compliance, data collection, scholarly research/art, student organization activities, and short‑term guest speakers. Enforcement: affected employees may sue and obtain injunctive relief. The bill prohibits public spending on DEI but contains no specific appropriations. Defines "appropriate governing board" as the Board of Regents (University of Nebraska), Board of Trustees (Nebraska State Colleges), or any community college governing board. Prohibits public postsecondary institutions from operating or funding "diversity, equity, and inclusion" (DEI) offices or programs that influence hiring, provide race/gender‑based benefits, or implement policies/training referencing race, color, ethnicity, gender identity, or sexual orientation; bars requiring participation or spending public money on such DEI efforts. Carves out exceptions: sexual‑harassment training; offices staffed by attorneys for legal compliance; statements for grants or accreditation; demographic data collection; scholarly research; recognized student organization activities; and short‑term guest speakers. Employees forced into DEI programs may sue and obtain injunctive relief. No new appropriations are made; the text restricts the use of public funds for DEI. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB553_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB553_Intro_Copy.docx LB553 amends the Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act to add dietitian nutritionist programs and licensed dietitian nutritionists to student loan and loan-repayment eligibility. It directs the commission to include dietitian nutritionist practice when designating health profession shortage areas. Financial terms: student loans remain capped at $30,000 per recipient per academic year (program caps retained); medical resident incentives up to $40,000 per residency year (max $120,000); loan-repayment limits set at $30,000/year (up to $90,000) for physicians/psychiatrists/dentists/psychologists and $15,000/year (up to $45,000) for physician assistants, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, physical/occupational therapists, dietitian nutritionists, and mental health practitioners. The department will make payments; state and local entities provide equal funding for repayments. Default repayment is 150% plus 8% simple interest. ARPA federal funds must be used first for certain agreements and need not require equal local funding. Original sections are repealed. The added language establishes program coverage in Nebraska including a “dietitian nutritionist program” and enumerates qualifying provider types — specifically naming a dietitian nutritionist licensed under section 38‑1813 among other listed categories. It otherwise appears to set out eligibility/terminology rules for dietitian nutritionists and their practice. No specific state agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the quoted additions. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB554_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB554_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB554 creates the Nebraska Health Professions Commission and expressly makes the chief medical officer of the Department of Health and Human Services (or a designee) a statutory member of the commission. The bill otherwise assigns the commission factfinding, review, reporting, and public‑hearing duties related to scope‑of‑practice and credentialing. No provisions in the provided text establish new appropriations, funding authorizations, or budget allocations for the Department of Health and Human Services. Summary (Department of Health and Human Services focus):\n\n- The bill creates the Nebraska Health Professions Commission and requires it to collect and analyze data (workforce shortages, public health impacts, health care quality, access, affordability) and hold public fact‑finding hearings. \n- The commission must file a detailed report with the board, the DHHS director, and the Health and Human Services Committee and forward annual recommendations to that Committee by October 1. \n- The chief medical officer of DHHS (or designee) is a required commission member. \n- The commission may monitor and evaluate the health care quality and public‑health impact of Legislature‑enacted scope or credentialing changes and may initiate reviews. \n- No specific funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DHHS or the commission are included. 109-1-LB555_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB555_Intro_Copy.docx LB555 (introduced by Sen. Riepe; heard by the Health and Human Services Committee) amends the Funeral Directing and Embalming Practice Act to create an "assistant funeral director" credential. Assistants may perform specified funeral-directing and establishment-management functions under the supervision and control of a licensed funeral director but are explicitly prohibited from embalming. Licensed funeral directors must execute, supervise, and retain collaborative agreements with assistants. The bill amends disciplinary provisions to add failure to comply with the collaborative-agreement requirement as a basis for action and ties enforcement to existing departmental/regulatory authority under the credentialing statutes. It repeals the replaced statutory sections and contains an emergency clause making it effective on passage. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds a defined "assistant funeral director" role: assistants may perform principal funeral-directing functions (services, interments, family arrangements, daily management and operation tasks) under supervision and control of a licensed funeral director. Assistants are expressly prohibited from embalming; violation results in immediate termination of the collaborative agreement and employment in Nebraska. Employing funeral directors must enter into and retain collaborative agreements, supervise assistants, and keep records of duties. The text also adds "failure to comply with section 8 of this act" as an additional noncompliance ground. No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB556_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB556_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services LB556 amends juvenile justice statutes to (1) clarify that a "staff secure juvenile facility" does not include any institution operated by the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) and to prohibit placing or assigning certain categories of juveniles to adult correctional facilities or the DCS-operated secure youth confinement facility. (2) Require peace officers to deliver custody of juveniles taken under specified noncriminal or protective subsections to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), which must make and supervise temporary placements, may consent to emergency medical/behavioral treatment, and whose temporary custody ends absent a court order within 48 hours. For mental-health-dangerousness detentions, officers must execute a DHHS-prescribed certificate and forward a copy to the county attorney. No funding or appropriation changes are included. No provisions here name or change responsibilities, funding, appropriations, or budget lines for the Department of Correctional Services or the Department of Health and Human Services.\n\nSubstantive additions (summary):\n- Defines "detention" as temporary care in a physically restrictive facility.\n- Requires probation officers to recommend detention, release, or alternatives for felony arrests and forward intake to a judge; the judge consults the officer but is not bound by statutory factors.\n- For non‑felony arrests, sets criteria judges/probation must consider (threat to persons, flight risk/failure to appear, absconding, violent or multiple property offenses, threats of self‑harm/other‑harm).\n- Limits some detentions for non‑felonies to cases where the juvenile’s counsel and the county/city attorney agree, and emphasizes detention only when immediately necessary for protection. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB557_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB557_Intro_Copy.docx LB557 amends multiple education statutes. Key agency roles and fiscal changes:\n\n- Commissioner of Education: prescribes option application and withdrawal forms. \n- State Board of Education: hears appeals of rejected enrollment-option applications. \n- State Department of Education: reimburses resident districts for transportation of option students with disabilities under section 79-1144 and annually certifies school-building percentages qualifying for free/reduced meals to learning communities and member districts. \n- School boards: continue authority over student fee policies and transportation charges. \n- Learning community coordinating councils: authority to administer funds under 79-2111, levy for specified purposes (historical reference to pre‑2017–18 levies), fund juvenile-justice diversion programming, and hold public hearings.\n\nFiscal changes: establishes a $2,500 educational support payment to parents when an option enrollment application is rejected; revises net option funding (FY2023‑24 onward) to equal net option students × (statewide average basic funding per formula student minus foundation aid per formula student); transportation allowance rules clarified (285% of state mileage rate) and excluded for learning‑community students who qualify for free/reduced lunches. Added provisions affect school districts and learning communities. Key points:\n- If a student's option-enrollment application is rejected by the school district, the parent or legal guardian is eligible for a $2,500 educational support payment for that school year; the bill adds a process for requesting that payment (subsection (3)).\n- Districts must use a random selection process and consider student and parent/guardian interest when handling enrollments.\n- The bill defines "student who contributes to socioeconomic diversity" using certification under section 79-2120 (free/reduced-price lunch percentages and the community eligibility provision) to compare school-building rates to the learning community average.\n- Statutory references include sections 79-2120 and 79-769. No other state agencies or new appropriations beyond the $2,500 payment are specified in the added text. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB558_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB558_Final_Copy.docx LB558 (2025) creates an "Infrastructure Review Task Force" charged with duties related to transportation infrastructure. 109-1-LB559_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB559_Final_Copy.docx LB559 creates new criminal offenses for skimmer devices and a continuing criminal enterprise involving financial transaction offenses and amends forfeiture procedures. Key government roles and fiscal provisions:\n\n- Attorney General: administers the newly created Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund, determines eligibility and reimbursement amounts, prescribes application form, and may distribute funds pro rata.\n- State Investment Officer: invests fund assets pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.\n- State Treasurer: receives funds remitted after a retention period for distribution under Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution.\n- Prosecuting authorities must specifically plead forfeiture in charging instruments; district courts handle pretrial/evidentiary forfeiture hearings and related procedures.\n\nNo direct appropriations are specified; the bill directs forfeited assets into the new fund with a 36-month retention/claims period before remittance. Adds criminal provisions for skimmer devices and defines "financial transaction offense," and establishes the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund. Key agency roles and funding mechanics:\n- The Attorney General will administer the Fund, determine victim eligibility, set reimbursement amounts, and prescribe application forms; distributions are pro rata if claims exceed available funds.\n- The Fund consists of assets forfeited from financial transaction offenses (per §28-1601) and any investable money shall be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.\n- Funds transferred into the Fund remain for at least 36 months (or until pending claims resolve); thereafter unclaimed funds are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution.\nNo direct appropriations are created; funding is from forfeited assets. 109-1-LB55_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB55_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill expresses legislative intent to appropriate $1,500,000 for FY2025‑26 from the Hospital Quality Assurance and Access Assessment Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services’ Medical Assistance program. 109-1-LB560_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB560_Final_Copy.docx LB560 amends §81-3725 to revise tourism grant programs administered by "the commission" and its executive director. It requires the commission to maintain marketing-assistance grants for national/international-caliber events (applicants must document out-of-state draw, marketing plans, tracking methods, and press potential). It expands "innovative tourism grants" eligibility to include projects that increase nonlocal in-state visitors (or both nonlocal in-state and out-of-state visitors), prohibits use for equipment or capital facility development, and limits awards to up to $500,000 to any city or village per fiscal year. The executive director must convene a technical review committee (public, private, citizen representatives) to score applications; recipients must file a final report within 90 days. The commission will adopt rules; the original section is repealed. Adds that "the commission" (the agency administering the tourism program) shall award innovative tourism grants of up to $500,000 to any qualifying city or village each fiscal year. 109-1-LB561_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB561_Final_Copy.docx Department of Transportation LB561 directs the Department of Transportation to create a statewide "bridge map" (identifying prohibited bridge structures) by January 1, 2026, review it annually, and publish the latest version on the department's public website. The department (or Nebraska State Patrol for applicable highways) may issue special permits, including new overweight raw‑milk vehicle permits, and may revoke individual permits for violations or revoke all such permits if they risk loss of federal aid. The department may adopt rules, require financial security to cover roadway damage, make permit applications available in county treasurers’ offices (and other locations), and grant limited length exceptions to meet axle-weight limits. The department may sue to recover bridge‑repair costs caused by prohibited crossings; recovered funds must be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Roads Operations Cash Fund. Summary (Dept. of Transportation):\n\n- Defines Department of Transportation as lead agency for new "overweight raw‑milk vehicle" permits (max gross weight 107,500 lbs and axle weights per federal bridge formula). Vehicles must carry the bridge map, avoid prohibited bridges, and not use the Interstate unless both DOT and FHWA authorize on the permit.\n- DOT must create a statewide "prohibited bridge" map by Jan 1, 2026, review it annually, and publish updates on its website.\n- DOT may revoke permits for violations (with written‑notice/APA appeal rights) and may revoke all permits if federal aid is at risk.\n- DOT may pursue owners for bridge repair costs; recovered funds go to the Roads Operations Cash Fund.\n- DOT may grant reasonable vehicle‑length exceptions to meet axle limits.\n\nNo new appropriations or line‑item budget allocations are specified. 109-1-LB563_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB563_Intro_Copy.docx LB563 amends the Motor Vehicle Registration Act to (1) add a definition of "commercial fertilizer trailer" (a trailer owned by an individual or business that sells agricultural fertilizer or chemicals as a going concern) and (2) authorize permanent trailer license plates for commercial fertilizer trailers. 109-1-LB564_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB564_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services LB564 amends section 77-7304 to require the State Treasurer to transfer $750 million from the General Fund to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund in fiscal year 2024-25 "on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services." 109-1-LB565_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB565_Intro_Copy.docx LB565 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §84-901.03 (Administrative Procedure Act) to tighten requirements for agency guidance documents. Key agency obligations: publish each guidance and an index of current rules/guidance in one public location and online; submit the index to the Clerk of the Legislature annually by December 31; include on the first page a prescribed notice and an estimated fiscal-impact description covering state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated persons/businesses; and post agency decisions publicly. Individuals may request revision, repeal, or conversion of guidance to rules; agencies must respond within 60 days. Agencies are barred from issuing guidance from July 1, 2025, to July 1, 2027, except for federal compliance; guidance may not exceed federal requirements. Guidance and provider bulletins issued July 1, 2022–July 1, 2025, are revoked pending rulemaking unless federally required. The bill contains both an operative date (July 1, 2025) and an emergency clause; no funding or appropriation changes are included. Requires state agencies (and political subdivisions) to stop issuing guidance documents from July 1, 2025 to July 1, 2027 except when needed to comply with new or amended federal rules. Any agency guidance must not impose stricter requirements on Nebraska residents or businesses than federal rules. All guidance documents and provider bulletins issued between July 1, 2022 and July 1, 2025 are revoked until they undergo formal rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act, unless explicitly required for federal compliance. No specific agencies are named and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB573_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB573_Intro_Copy.docx LB573 creates the "Meat and Poultry Workers and Contractors Protection Act" and assigns primary enforcement duties to the commissioner (who must receive disaster mitigation plans, monitor compliance, investigate complaints, develop a compliance process within 90 days, assess civil penalties up to $15,000, and may sue or bring actions on behalf of aggrieved workers/contract growers). During a declared "disaster mitigation event" covered industrial operators must offer Nebraska Workers' Compensation coverage for related injury/illness for the event and two years after, provide 12 weeks' severance for workers terminated within 60 days, and pay affected contract growers lost revenue equal to the prior 180 days. Operators with 25+ employees must notify workers of collective-bargaining/FLSA rights; the commissioner may penalize misinformation, intimidation, or wrongful termination. The bill creates a commissioner-appointed Workers and Contractors Task Force (includes legislative nonvoting members from the Legislature's Agriculture Committee) that must meet regularly and submit annual reports to the commissioner and Legislature. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Creates duties for "the commissioner" (who will receive, investigate, and enforce complaints) to: require covered industrial operators to file disaster mitigation plans; develop a compliance‑monitoring process within 90 days; require employers (25+ employees) to provide workers information on collective‑bargaining/NLRB and FLSA rights; and assess civil penalties up to $15,000 for violations or anti‑union misconduct. References federal OSHA and the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act for workplace safety/compensation standards and permits commissioner civil suits on behalf of workers. Establishes a Workers and Contractors Task Force (appointed by the commissioner, with two nonvoting legislative Agriculture Committee members) to meet regularly and report annually to the commissioner and Legislature. No new appropriations or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB574_Intro Withdrawn Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB574_Intro_Copy.docx LB574 applies to certified firefighters and emergency personnel (including EMTs and paramedics). The bill also guarantees safe working conditions, access to training, equipment, mental‑health services, off‑duty political activity, and access to personnel/training records. No state agencies or budget appropriations are named or modified. Adds comprehensive firefighter protections and procedural requirements for agencies that investigate firefighters: definitions (complaint, firefighter, formal investigation, interview); mandates that formal investigations be timely; written complaint summaries provided before interviews; interviewees may have legal or union representation; interviews must be audio‑recorded; investigators must send written outcomes; complaints, statements, and recordings remain confidential absent law or consent; firefighters can seek damages (including attorney fees) for false complaints; may use grievance/union/legal channels; and cannot be compelled to take polygraphs. Also guarantees safe working conditions, access to training, equipment, support, and mental‑health services; confidentiality of personal information; off‑duty political activity allowed; and access to personnel and training records. 109-1-LB575_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB575_Intro_Copy.docx LB575 amends two revenue statutes. Under §77-1633 (Property Tax Request Act) counties, cities, school districts, and community colleges seeking to increase property tax requests beyond the allowable growth percentage must participate in a county-organized joint public hearing (held between July 14–24 after 6 p.m.), with designated representatives, and submit prescribed information electronically to the county assessor by July 4. The county clerk organizes the hearing; initial postcard printing costs are paid from the county general fund and then charged proportionately to participating political subdivisions. The statute prescribes detailed postcard and notice content and reporting duties of the county clerk.\n\nAmendments to §77-3442 (levy limits) add a statewide cap: when a political subdivision’s taxable valuation rises, its levy may be no higher than needed to raise the same dollar amount as the prior year, except if two-thirds of its governing body vote to exceed that limit. The act is effective immediately. Adds a levy cap for political subdivisions: if a jurisdiction’s total taxable valuation rises from the prior year, its property tax levy is limited to the dollar amount necessary to raise exactly the same total property tax revenue as the prior year (i.e., no increase in dollars despite higher valuation). A political subdivision can exceed that limit only by an affirmative two‑thirds vote of its governing body. Applies except as provided in section 77‑3444. No specific state agencies, new appropriations, or budget allocations are created or changed. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB585_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB585_Intro_Copy.docx LB585 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-2404.02 governing the Community-based Juvenile Services Aid Program. It requires the commission administering the program to: (1) continue developing and maintaining a common data set (with assistance and evaluation by the University of Nebraska at Omaha, Juvenile Justice Institute), (2) set aside an additional 10% of the annual General Fund appropriation (excluding administrative funds) for grants to community-based organizations located in qualified census tracts with budgets ≤ $1 million that provide primary prevention, and (3) apportion remaining General Fund aid by a commission formula based on youth population/contact with the juvenile justice system. The commission may require up to a 5% local match and must consult/coordinate with the Office of Probation Administration, juvenile diversion programs, law enforcement, courts, the Nebraska Association of County Officials, and relevant directors in rulemaking and annual reporting to the Governor and Legislature. Records in the common data set are exempt from public disclosure for evaluation purposes. Requires that 10% of the annual General Fund appropriation to the Community-based Juvenile Services Aid Program (excluding administrative budget funds) be set aside for grants to community-based organizations located in qualified census tracts (per 26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I), as of Jan 1, 2025) with annual budgets ≤ $1 million that focus on preventing juvenile crime before system involvement. Fund distribution must consider: staff with lived juvenile‑justice experience, organization budget size, program location in a qualified census tract, and client demographics. The University of Nebraska at Omaha’s Juvenile Justice Institute is directed to assist grantees in creating logic models and evaluation measures to assess program impact. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB586_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB586_Intro_Copy.docx LB586 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32-944 (Election Act). It directs county election commissioners or county clerks to develop plans, consistent with Secretary of State rules, to ensure voting access for individuals housed in county jails/detention centers who cannot vote in person. Plans must address voter registration/verification access, ballot return locations within facilities (collected by two registered voters not of the same party), methods/deadlines for return, and procedures to cure ballot deficiencies. County sheriffs, facility directors, or designated staff must carry out duties under the Election Act. Noncompliance by jail officials exposes the county to a civil penalty set by the local district court. The bill repeals the prior version of §32-944. No appropriations or budget changes are specified. Requires county jails/detention centers to ensure restricted/incarcerated eligible voters can verify/change/register to vote, access ballot return locations inside the facility (collected by two registered voters of different parties), receive information on return methods/locations/deadlines, and have a process to cure ballot deficiencies. Assigns operational responsibility to the county sheriff or facility director/designated staff, with the election commissioner or county clerk required to adopt procedures consistent with the Election Act and Secretary of State rules. Noncompliance by a county jail/direct facility subjects the county to a civil penalty set by the local district court. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB587_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB587_Intro_Copy.docx LB587 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§76-1425 and 76-1427 (Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act). It shortens and clarifies notice/termination timelines for tenant termination following landlord noncompliance and for repeat violations, and expands tenant remedies for landlords' failure to maintain dwelling units or essential services. New remedies allow tenants, after written notice, to (a) procure and deduct reasonable costs for hot/running water, heat, and essential services; (b) remediate and deduct costs for mold or pest infestations; (c) recover diminution in fair rental value and diminution to personal property; (d) be excused from paying rent during the noncompliance period; and (e) recover substitute-housing costs if the landlord's failure is deliberate. Reasonable attorney fees are recoverable. Original sections are repealed. No state agencies, departments, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced or affected. Added provisions expand tenant remedies when a landlord fails to remediate a known mold problem or pest infestation: tenants may (a) purchase supplies or hire services to remediate the condition during the landlord’s noncompliance and deduct actual, reasonable costs from rent, and (b) recover damages reflecting diminution in value of their personal property caused by the landlord’s deliberate or negligent noncompliance. The text also includes editorial/renumbering of remedy subsections. No government agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are affected. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB588_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB588_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB588 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-512 to revise procedures and duties of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) for aid to dependent children. DHHS retains authority to accept applications, investigate via its agents and employees, file findings with the county or authorized attorney when a parent can contribute, determine allowance/denial and set monthly assistance by unit size, and hear appeals to its chief executive officer. Beginning September 10, 2025, the bill requires the department to calculate the maximum monthly assistance level tied to the annual inflation factor. DHHS must adopt rules establishing work‑incentive, training, and transitional benefit programs (including transitional payments, child care, and up to 12 months medical assistance). No explicit appropriations or budget allocations are included. Adds a provision establishing September 10, 2025 as the date when specified amounts will be calculated and tied to the annual inflation factor. For the Department of Health and Human Services: the underlined text does not itself change or appropriate funds, nor does it specify new budget allocations; it only mandates inflation-based adjustment of applicable amounts beginning on that date. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB589_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB589_Intro_Copy.docx LB589 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-1142 (special education reimbursement). Key agencies: State Board of Education (sets percentage cap for support-services reimbursement), Nebraska Department of Education (administers reimbursements, audits documentation, and files annual reports to the Governor, Appropriations Committee, and Education Committee), State Treasurer, and Director of Administrative Services (certifies funds and draws warrants). Funding changes/clarifications:\n- Reimburses school districts 80% of total allowable excess special education costs; if General Fund appropriations are insufficient, payments are prorated from the General Fund and the remainder paid from the Education Future Fund.\n- Requires Legislature-set aside amounts for support services and special education reimbursements; board cap on support-services percentage tied to that set-aside.\n- Payments made monthly (min. seven payments); transfers tied to Extraordinary Increase payments move to the Education Future Fund.\nOperational change: allowable costs include substitute costs and districts must provide four days/year professional leave for special-education staff, supported by substitutes. Adds that allowable/reimbursable special education and support costs explicitly include substitute service costs. Requires each school district to provide special education staff four days of professional leave annually, with substitute personnel provided, to be used onsite solely to complete essential documentation for students on their caseloads. No specific state agency is named and no explicit new appropriation or dollar amount is indicated beyond making substitute costs reimbursable. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB58_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB58_Final_Copy.docx LB58 (Sanders) repeals Nebraska’s statutory provisions governing jeweler’s liens by outright repealing R.R.S. §§ 52-301 through 52-304. 109-1-LB590_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB590_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Transportation LB590 authorizes the Department of Transportation to, by rule and regulation, establish, use, and operate a mitigation bank or an in-lieu fee program consistent with applicable state and federal law. The bill also requires that owners of mitigation banks acquired to restore, enhance, preserve, or create suitable habitat pay a sum in lieu of ad valorem taxes to counties. No direct appropriations or other budget allocations to the Department of Transportation are specified. The Department of Transportation is newly authorized to adopt rules and to establish, use, and operate mitigation banks and in‑lieu fee programs consistent with state and federal law. These tools are for compensatory mitigation of incidental take of threatened or endangered species and their habitat from permitted activities, focusing on restoring/creating/enhancing/preserving habitat, applying fair and practicable mitigation ratios, and achieving a net increase in conservation functions and values. Fiscal change: owners of mitigation banks (state/local agencies or private parties) must pay a sum in lieu of ad valorem taxes to counties for lands acquired for mitigation. No direct appropriations, budget allocations, or funding transfers to the Department of Transportation are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB591_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB591_Intro_Copy.docx LB591 amends the Nebraska Installment Loan Act (sections 45-1003 and 45-1004). It clarifies licensing authority tied to "the department" (the licensing department) by expanding when a license is required: nonfinancial persons who market, own, hold, acquire, service, or otherwise engage in loan activity with an installment-loan borrower must be licensed, including where a financial institution originally made the loan. The bill exempts affiliates whose in-state activities are limited solely to securitization provided servicing rights remain with the licensee or are assigned to a financial institution, licensee, or permittee. It defines affiliate and control (ownership of 25% of voting shares or control of a majority of director elections). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are contained. The inserted text is simply the phrase "or that services, or interest ," and does not reference any government agency or department. It contains no provisions affecting funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB592_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB592_Final_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services The bill amends section 77-1407 to require the State Treasurer and the Accounting Administrator of the Department of Administrative Services to jointly determine the state fund types needed to comply with section 529A and state policy. It also requires the State Treasurer to transfer from the ABLE Expense Fund to the State Investment Officer’s Cash Fund an amount equal to the pro rata share of the budget appropriated to the Nebraska Investment Council for investment-management expenses, and to report annually (and prior to each such transfer) the amounts transferred to the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services (with an electronic copy to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst). Adds a blanket anti‑seizure clause: amounts in the referenced account are immune from levy, execution, judgment, garnishment, seizure, or other judicial enforcement to satisfy debts or liabilities of the account’s owner or beneficiary, notwithstanding other law. \n\nNo provisions affect the Department of Administrative Services’ responsibilities, and there are no changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations for DAS. 109-1-LB594_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB594_Intro_Copy.docx LB594 (introduced by Rep. Prokop; referred to Transportation and Telecommunications) amends §60-6,179.01 to prohibit the use of handheld wireless communication devices while operating a motor vehicle. Explicit exemptions are provided for law enforcement officers, firefighters, ambulance drivers, emergency medical technicians performing official duties, and employees/contractors of utility service providers responding to utility emergencies; an emergency driver communicating with emergency services is also exempt. The bill clarifies device definitions and allows functions initiated without touching the device or with a single touch. Violations are traffic infractions with license points assessed per §60-4,182 and fines of $200/$300/$500 (first/second/third+ offenses). No funding or appropriations are included; the original section is repealed. Adds narrow exemptions to the handheld‑device-while-driving prohibition: employees or contractors of a utility service provider responding to a utility emergency, and persons communicating or attempting to communicate with emergency services, are exempt. It also permits using a handheld wireless device while driving if used without touching it or to initiate a function with a single touch. No specific government agencies or departments are named beyond generic "utility service provider" and "emergency services," and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
