109-1-LB595_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB595_Intro_Copy.docx Creates the Research Excellence Cash Fund, to be administered by the University of Nebraska. The fund may receive gifts, grants, bequests, and transfers authorized by the Legislature. Authorized uses are research-based investments in data, data collection, and ongoing research important to Nebraska’s economy (explicitly including the Nebraska Mesonet). Available monies shall be invested by the state investment officer in accordance with the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. No specific appropriations or dollar amounts are set. Emergency clause makes the act effective upon passage and approval. Creates the "Research Excellence Cash Fund," to be administered by the University of Nebraska. The fund may receive gifts, grants, bequests, and transfers authorized by the Legislature and may be used for research investments in data, data collection, and ongoing research that supports Nebraska’s economy (explicitly including the Nebraska Mesonet). Funds available for investment will be managed by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. No specific dollar appropriations are included; legislative transfers are authorized as a potential funding source. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB596_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB596_Intro_Copy.docx LB596 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25-2228 to allow legal notices to be published on the website or application of a digital news publication that does not have a print edition, and to treat such online publication (for the required number of days/weeks) as lawful publication. It retains that notices published in print remain valid and preserves the existing requirement (effective Oct. 1, 2022) that newspapers or digital news publications also post notices on a statewide repository website established and maintained by a majority of Nebraska newspapers; failure to do so does not affect validity. The bill repeals the original section. No state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. Adds authority for required publication to be satisfied by posting on a digital news publication’s website or application for the specified number of days or weeks when the outlet lacks a print edition. No government agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are mentioned or changed. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB597_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB597_Intro_Copy.docx LB597 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act and affects multiple state agencies.\n\n- State Department of Education: revises foundation aid — for 2025-26 onward each district receives the greater of $1,500 per formula student or 7.5% of basic funding; 24% of total foundation aid must be paid from the Education Future Fund; only 60% (vs. 100% for 2023-24–2024-25) of foundation aid is counted as a formula resource beginning 2025-26. The department must certify state aid amounts to the Director of Administrative Services, Auditor of Public Accounts, and local systems and report required funding to the Governor, the Appropriations Committee, and the Legislature’s Education Committee.\n\n- Property Tax Administrator / Tax Commissioner / Tax Commission: adjusted valuations for agricultural/horticultural land drop from 72% to 65% of actual/special value beginning 2025-26; certification, objection, hearing, and appeal procedures are retained. The local effort rate used for certification beginning 2025-26 is the maximum levy less $0.10 (previously less $0.05), affecting local effort rate yield calculations.\n\n- Director of Administrative Services: receives certification for aid and issues warrants for lump-sum payments when authorized.\n\n- Appropriations Committee: must include the amount necessary to fund certified state aid (certified on or before June 15, 2025, and March 1 thereafter) in its budget recommendations.\n\n- Additional provisions nullify any state-aid, budget authority, or reserve-percentage certifications completed for school year 2025-26 prior to the act’s effective date. Adds new school funding rules effective for school fiscal year 2025-26 and thereafter. Key points affecting government actors and funding:\n- Foundation aid to each school district equals the greater of $1,500 per formula student or 7.5% of basic funding (per §79-1007.16).\n- For state aid certification (§79-1022) the local effort rate = the maximum levy under §77-3442(2)(a) minus $0.10.\n- For final state aid calculations (§79-1065) the local effort rate is set to produce the amount needed to meet total formula need when combined with state aid appropriated by the Legislature and other local receipts; local effort yield = adjusted valuation × local effort rate.\n- Adjusted valuation for aid calculations (2025-26 onward) uses 65% of actual value and 65% of special valuation (per §§77-1359, 77-1363, 77-1343). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB598_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB598_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services • Transfers: The State Treasurer is directed to transfer $1.0 billion (FY2023‑24) and $250.0 million (FY2024‑25) from the General Fund to the Education Future Fund on dates/amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services; the bill expresses intent for $250.0 million annually thereafter.\n\n• Certification: The State Department of Education must certify amounts to the Director of Administrative Services (along with the Auditor and local systems) on or before June 15, 2025, and March 1 annually thereafter.\n\n• Payments/warrants: For special education reimbursements, the State Treasurer will notify the Director of Administrative Services monthly of available funds in the General Fund and Education Future Fund, and the Director shall draw warrants against those appropriated funds for payments. No provisions affect the Department of Administrative Services. The additions direct the State Department of Education to administer Education Future Fund payments for school districts with extraordinary limited-English-proficiency (LEP) costs: districts may apply by Jan 15; payments are issued by Jan 31. Payment formula: baseline = (prior-year LEP expenditures ÷ 2) × 107%; maximum payment = current-year LEP expenditures minus that baseline; if total awards exceed the Fund balance, payments are reduced proportionally. Beginning 2025–26, the department must also reimburse districts/cooperatives for additional costs for students served under Section 504 at the same percentage as special-education reimbursements, with reporting/documentation procedures established. No DAS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB599_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB599_Intro_Copy.docx LB599 (2025), introduced by Senator DeBoer and referred to the Education Committee, requires the State Board of Education to adopt a prescribed cybersecurity policy applicable to schools. 109-1-LB59_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB59_Final_Copy.docx Bill LB59 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §2-3224 governing natural resources districts. It authorizes district funds to be disbursed by electronic payment systems (including electronic funds transfers and automated clearinghouse transfers) in addition to written instruments signed by the treasurer or an authorized designee. Written authorization for others to sign on the treasurer’s behalf must be filed with the district secretary. If the treasurer’s bond does not cover losses from persons so authorized, the district must procure and file a corporate surety bond approved in writing by two officers other than the treasurer. The secretary must report any such bonds or changes at each board meeting. The original section is repealed. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds authorization for payments to be made either by check signed by the treasurer or by electronic payment systems (including electronic funds transfer and automated clearinghouse transfers). Also adds authority for the treasurer to designate another person to sign on the treasurer’s behalf and addresses related signature/delegation procedures. No other state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB5_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB5_Intro_Copy.docx LB5 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-470 to provide immunity related to opioid antagonists (e.g., naloxone) for specified actors. Health professionals licensed under the Uniform Credentialing Act (physicians, PAs, nurse practitioners, pharmacists) may prescribe/dispense/administer without administrative or criminal penalty. Family/friends, school personnel, emergency responders (licensed under the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act or EMS Compact) and peace officers or law enforcement employees who obtain antagonists from their EMS organization or law enforcement agency (police departments, town marshals, offices of sheriff, Nebraska State Patrol) and act in good faith are protected from administrative action, criminal prosecution, and personal civil liability, except for willful, wanton, or gross negligence. Liability of employers/agencies remains unaffected. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. The prior version of the section is repealed. Adds a definition of "opioid antagonist" to mean naloxone hydrochloride or any opioid antagonist approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration for emergency reversal of known or suspected opioid overdose. The only government agency mentioned is the U.S. Food and Drug Administration; no funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB600_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB600_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Transportation LB600 assigns multiple powers and duties to the Department of Transportation (DOT):\n\n- DOT (or its agents) may remove vehicles/objects from highways or shoulders that impede traffic and is immune from liability for damage caused by removal.\n- DOT may temporarily reduce maximum lawful speeds for weather, traction, emergency, or congestion reasons, subject to electronic/digital signage, five-mile-per-hour increments, no minimum speed during reductions, recordkeeping, policy development, and rulemaking authority.\n- DOT may enforce school-crossing and highway-work-zone speed limits using speed-control enforcement systems, may contract operators, and (with local authorities) assess civil penalties (proceeds remitted to the State Treasurer). \n- DOT must create guidance for administrative fee calculation, ensure systems receive independent annual calibration, and erect/maintain controlled‑access highway signage for the move‑over requirement.\n\nNo direct appropriations or budget allocations to DOT are specified. The additions give the Department of Transportation (DOT) expanded operational and enforcement authority and procedural duties:\n\n- DOT may remove vehicles/objects from highways/shoulders that impede traffic without owner consent and is immune from damage liability. \n- DOT may temporarily lower posted speed limits (in 5 mph increments) for weather, traction, emergencies, congestion, etc., requiring prominent electronic/digital signage, a written policy, and recordkeeping of changes and each highway’s limit; rulemaking authorized. \n- DOT may use (and contract for) speed control enforcement systems in school crossing and highway work zones, subject to activation/signage and worker-warning-light conditions; systems must meet calibration, operator-training, daily-log, data-confidentiality, and appeals/hearing requirements. \n- Penalty structure, notice, administrative-fee guidance, and remittance of civil penalties to the State Treasurer are specified.\n\nNo direct funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB602_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB602_Intro_Copy.docx LB602 creates the "Data Elimination and Limiting Extensive Tracking and Exchange Act" and assigns primary administrative duties to the Secretary of State and enforcement to the Attorney General. Key agency actions:\n\n- Secretary of State: establish by Jan 1, 2028 an accessible deletion mechanism (consumer single-request portal); publish data-broker registration and deletion-mechanism information on the Secretary of State website; set an annual data-broker registration fee up to $300; may charge data brokers an access fee not to exceed the Secretary’s reasonable costs; select independent third-party auditors for triennial audits (first by Dec 31, 2030); adopt rules to implement the Act.\n- Attorney General: may seek civil penalties, injunctive relief, and recover attorney fees.\n\nMonetary provisions: registration fee (≤ $300); civil penalty of $200 per day per unfulfilled deletion request; Secretary may collect access fees. No other appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Added provisions assign primary operational and enforcement roles to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General. Key Secretary of State duties: host public registration and the statewide accessible deletion mechanism on its website; establish the deletion system by Jan 1, 2028; adopt implementing rules; set an annual data-broker registration fee (not to exceed $300); and may charge data brokers an access fee not to exceed the Secretary's reasonable costs. Data brokers must register annually, use the deletion mechanism (beginning Aug 1, 2028), and submit triennial third‑party audit reports (first by Dec. 31, 2030). Noncompliance triggers a $200-per-day civil penalty per incomplete deletion request payable to the Secretary of State. The Attorney General may enforce penalties, seek injunctive relief, and recover attorneys' fees and costs. No direct appropriations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB603_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB603_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB603 assigns several duties to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). DHHS will determine the poverty threshold (up to 300% of a federal poverty level/index) used to set a care management client family income schedule, promulgate that schedule as rules, and thereby permit clients below the threshold to contribute between 0% and 90% of care management service costs. DHHS may reimburse care management units based on actual casework time units, covering personnel, administration, eligibility review, contractual and indirect costs; DHHS must adopt standardized reimbursement rates and adjust them at least every three years. Appropriations for DHHS reimbursement and DHHS administrative costs for the program must be made separately from funds under the Nebraska Community Aging Services Act. Adds that care management clients may make voluntary contributions toward care management service costs (per section 81-2230). Contributions are to be determined by a client family income schedule based on federal poverty guidelines. No specific appropriations, budget allocations, or funding amounts are included; any revenue or administrative impact on the Department of Health and Human Services is not specified in the text. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB604_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB604_Intro_Copy.docx LB604 amends initiative and referendum procedures (secs. 32-1405, 32-1412). Key agency duties and procedural changes:\n\n- Secretary of State: requires filing of petition object/text and sworn sponsor list before circulating; transmits text to the Revisor of Statutes; keeps filings confidential for five days after the Revisor’s review; must provide petition form to sponsor within five business days and post measure text/notice on its website until the filing deadline. If refusing to place a measure on the ballot for legal insufficiency (other than signature insufficiency), the Secretary must announce the refusal and state reasons when posting circulation notice; failure to state reasons waives those defenses.\n\n- Revisor of Statutes: must review proposed measures and suggest form/draftsmanship changes within ten business days.\n\n- Courts: mandamus suits go to Lancaster County District Court; suits challenging sufficiency (other than signature insufficiency) must be filed within 60 days of the Secretary’s posting (or by the petition-filing deadline if earlier); the sponsor of record is a necessary party defendant in injunction/removal suits. If practicable, the Nebraska Supreme Court may hear non-signature insufficiency suits in original jurisdiction; appeals to the Court of Appeals within ten days.\n\nNo funding or appropriations are included. Original sections repealed. Adds procedural duties for the Secretary of State and timing/venue rules for legal challenges. Key points:\n- Secretary of State must post the measure text and a notice that it is in circulation on the Secretary of State website until the petition filing deadline.\n- If the Secretary refuses to place a measure on the ballot for any legal insufficiency other than insufficient signatures, the Secretary must announce that refusal on the same date as the circulation posting and state the reasons; failure to state reasons waives those defenses.\n- Suits challenging petition legal sufficiency (other than signature insufficiency) must be filed within 60 days of the circulation notice—or by the petition filing deadline if the 60th day falls after that deadline.\n- When practicable, the Nebraska Supreme Court shall hear such suits under its original jurisdiction (section 24-204) on petition.\n- Parties may assert substantive facial insufficiency without ripeness dismissal.\nNo agencies beyond the Secretary of State and the Nebraska Supreme Court are added; no funding or appropriation changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB605_Intro Withdrawn Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB605_Intro_Copy.docx LB605 requires each school board to adopt a policy governing student participation as a transgender student in school-sponsored extracurricular activities and in activities run by any athletics or activities association of which the school is a member. The bill directs school administrators or athletic directors to submit a written application identifying the student as transgender and listing desired activities. School boards must determine eligibility under the adopted policy, require documentation (current registration, a written statement from student and parent/guardian, corroborating statements from others), and, when association approval is needed, submit required documentation and cooperate with that association. Participation on sex-separated teams defaults to the biological sex on the student’s birth certificate unless board approval is granted. The bill contains no funding or appropriation provisions. Adds requirements for school boards (with school administrators or athletic directors) to: receive written requests from transgender students listing desired activities; determine eligibility under locally adopted policy; and, when applicable, submit eligibility applications and required documentation to any athletics or activities association of which the school is a member. Authorizes sharing student registration, a written statement from the student and parent/guardian, and corroborating documentation from others with those associations. If approved, school boards must cooperate with associations to obtain determinations. Establishes that eligibility for sex-separated teams defaults to the biological sex on the birth certificate unless approved under the local transgender or cross‑gender policy. Clarifies the policy does not encourage medical transition and does not alter existing cross‑gender exceptions. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB606_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB606_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue LB606 consolidates parole supervision by eliminating the Division of Parole Supervision and the Director of Supervision and Services and vesting those powers and duties in the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) and its Director. DCS must operate facilities; develop treatment, reentry and parole programs; maintain Board of Parole records and complete electronic offender files; implement validated risk‑and‑needs assessments, performance metrics, and related training; and may pilot a technical‑violation residential housing program. DCS may contract with private providers for community work‑release and reentry centers, use available Board funds for reentry housing, and is intended to receive a $1,000,000 General Fund appropriation for the Community Work Release and Reentry Centers Act. Parolees pay a $25 monthly fee credited to the Parole Program Cash Fund for DCS use. The Department of Health and Human Services may subpoena confidential records for licensing investigations, and DCS is an authorized recipient of certain records for lifetime community supervision. Department of Revenue employees under section 77‑366 are not defined as law enforcement officers. Department of Correctional Services: New provisions require the department to maintain all records and files for the Board of Parole, specifically including records for persons under lifetime community supervision (sec. 83‑174.03), and expressly allow the department to keep daily records related to the Board of Pardons. The additions also clarify departmental/director implementation authority and emphasize that continued in‑custody correctional treatment, medical care, or vocational/other training may be provided when it substantially improves an offender’s ability to lead a law‑abiding life after release.\n\nDepartment of Health and Human Services / Department of Revenue: No substantive duties, funding changes, appropriations, or budget allocations for DHHS or Revenue are added. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB607_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB607_Intro_Copy.docx The bill places primary implementation and enforcement with the Department of Environment and Energy. It establishes the Environmental Stewardship of Batteries Act, Extended Producer Responsibility Data Collection Act, and Minimum Recycled Content Act; the department will adopt rules, set annual fees (including a $1,000 baseline manufacturer registration fee and fees for battery stewardship organizations sufficient to cover department costs), certify third‑party compliance, and impose civil penalties appealable to the Environmental Quality Council (fines remitted to the State Treasurer). Disposal fees at regulated landfills increase to $2.25/ton (1/1/26), $3.25/ton (1/1/27) and $4.25/ton (1/1/28); receipts split 50/50 between the Integrated Solid Waste Management Cash Fund and the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund, with up to 5% of prior‑year disposal‑fee revenue available to reimburse political subdivisions for remediation. Manufacturers must report resin‑specific virgin/postconsumer plastic data annually beginning 1/1/27; initial recycled‑content shortfall penalties are $0.20/lb (with a post‑2029 pricing option). The department may join a multistate clearinghouse, administer grants (including up to $1.5M/year for scrap tire projects through 6/30/29), and reimburse its administrative costs from the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund; legislative transfers to the General Fund are permitted. The act is operative 1/1/26. Adds and centers the Department of Environment and Energy as the implementing agency for multiple new programs. Key duties: adopt rules, approve battery stewardship plans, establish and collect fees to cover the department’s full implementation/enforcement costs, host an online registry of approved producers, create an electronic registration system, and produce reports/assessments (battery end‑of‑life assessment due July 1, 2027; report to Legislature by Oct. 1, 2027). Financial provisions: a graduated disposal fee ($2.25 in 2026; $3.25 in 2027; $4.25 in 2028); annual manufacturer registration fee ($1,000, adjustable); battery stewardship organizations pay annual department fees and must reimburse local governments for demonstrable collection costs; civil penalties specified (e.g., up to $1,000/day, up to $10,000/day for repeated violations; 20¢/lb penalty for recycled‑content shortfalls initially). Penalties remit to the State Treasurer; confidentiality requests go to the Director of Environment and Energy. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB608_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB608_Final_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Revenue - The bill defines “correctional officer” to include individuals employed full‑time by a jail or by the Department of Correctional Services responsible for supervision and security of incarcerated persons.\n\n- The Department of Revenue is designated to administer and enforce the First Responder Recruitment and Retention Act (rulemaking authority), to receive annual documentation from applicants proving employment/status and Nebraska residency, and to maintain records of qualifying children who receive tuition waivers. Institutions must provide lists to the Department by December 31; the Department must report by August 1 each year which waiver recipients failed to file a tax return documenting Nebraska residency.\n\n- Beginning July 1, 2028, subject to available appropriations, the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education shall reimburse state universities for 50% of tuition waivers granted the prior year for correctional officers, youth detention officers, certain formerly employed disabled persons, and their qualifying children. Reimbursement claims require documentation and will be prorated if appropriations are insufficient. - Department of Correctional Services: The bill adds a definition of "correctional officer" as a full‑time employee of a jail or the Department of Correctional Services responsible for adult facility supervision. Correctional officers (and their qualifying children) are included in tuition‑waiver eligibility; waivers for correctional‑officer‑related eligible disabled persons and their children are limited to state‑university attendance beginning July 1, 2027. Disabled former correctional officers must have had satisfactory performance at time of disability. No direct appropriations or new operating funds are directed to the Department of Correctional Services.\n\n- Department of Revenue: The bill requires applicants (first responders, eligible disabled persons, and qualifying children) to file annual documentation with the Department of Revenue proving employment/status and Nebraska residence to receive waivers.\n\n- Funding: Beginning July 1, 2028, the Coordinating Commission will reimburse state universities 50% of these specific waivers, subject to available appropriations and prorating if funds are insufficient. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB609_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB609_Final_Copy.docx LB609 creates the Controllable Electronic Record Fraud Prevention Act and imposes regulatory requirements on operators of controllable electronic record kiosks. Relevant government entities and duties:\n\n- Consumer Protection Division, Office of the Attorney General: must publish model notice language for gift‑card fraud warnings; may issue written citations for violations and assess civil penalties up to $250 after an initial warning.\n- "The department" (as used in the bill): may require additional receipt disclosures and may request evidence that kiosk operators use blockchain analytics to prevent fraud.\n- State and local law enforcement agencies and other government agencies: must be listed on kiosk displays and transaction receipts as contacts for reporting fraud; law enforcement has an established dedicated contact requirement for operators.\n- Courts and law enforcement: section 29‑817 is amended to explicitly include "controllable electronic records" within the definition of property for search‑warrant provisions.\n\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds multiple obligations involving unspecified "the department," state and local law enforcement, and the Attorney General's office. Key agency points:\n- "The department" may require additional disclosures on kiosks/receipts and may request evidence that operators use blockchain analytics. \n- Kiosk operators must display contact information for relevant state or local law enforcement and other government agencies for reporting fraud; receipts must list relevant state law enforcement and government agencies. Operators also must maintain a daily-monitored law-enforcement contact method. \n- The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General must publish model notice language for gift‑card fraud warnings; the Attorney General may issue citations and impose civil penalties (up to $250 after multiple citations). \nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are added. 109-1-LB60_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB60_Intro_Copy.docx LB60 (Quick) amends the State Lottery Act by revising section 9‑829, removing the statutory prohibition on selling lottery tickets via vending or dispensing devices. The bill retains existing constraints on lottery game retailers: tickets must be sold only on premises specified in the retailer contract, may not be sold by telephone or mail, and retailers may not extend credit for ticket purchases. The original version of section 9‑829 is repealed. Agencies affected: Nebraska State Lottery and licensed lottery game retailers. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. No underlined (added) text found in this bill. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB610_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB610_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB610 revises the Department of Health and Human Services’ duties under the Ground Emergency Medical Transport Act. Key DHHS provisions: seek necessary federal approvals by January 1, 2026; specify the evidence, data submission, and records governmental entities must provide to support certifications and claims; limit the program to costs allowable under Title XIX as of January 1, 2025; implement the intergovernmental transfer program only if federal funding and approvals are available; authorize the department’s CEO to refuse or return IGTs and adjust payments to ensure Medicaid compliance; and submit claims and annual assurances to CMS that only allowable expenditures are claimed. The bill allows increased capitation payments to begin as of January 1, 2025 if federal approval is obtained. No direct state appropriations or budget allocations are specified. DHHS must base ground emergency medical transport payments on "actual and allowable" costs as defined by regulations in effect on January 1, 2025, and comply with any applicable federal requirements. In 2026 the department is directed to seek any federal approvals needed to implement subsection (2) of the Ground Emergency Medical Transport Act (implementation referenced to January 1, 2025). The added text does not specify any new appropriations, funding amounts, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB611_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB611_Intro_Copy.docx LB611 updates Nebraska's state building and energy code references and assigns implementation duties to state agencies. Key provisions:\n\n- Department of Environment and Energy (DEE): review plans/specifications for state‑funded buildings for compliance with the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), provide copies of reviews to the funding agency, and receive verification that constructed buildings meet or exceed the code. The DEE Director may adopt rules, in consultation with DAS State Building Administrator.\n\n- Department of Administrative Services (DAS) — State Building Administrator: may specify a more recent IECC edition, added efficiency/renewable requirements, or life‑cycle cost analysis (LCCA)‑justified waivers; agencies receiving state funds must supply LCCAs and verification.\n\n- Counties, cities, and villages: may adopt local codes but must notify DEE if deleting specified IBC/IRC provisions.\n\nThe bill adopts the 2021 IECC and updated IBC/IRC references. No appropriations or budgetary allocations are specified. Adds or updates statutory references to the 2021 editions of the model codes — specifically calling out Chapter 13 of the 2021 International Building Code and Chapter 11 of the 2021 International Residential Code — and ties those provisions to the act’s effective date. The text does not mention any government agencies or departments and contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB613_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB613_Final_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Labor, Department of Revenue LB613 amends disclosure and administration provisions involving the Department of Revenue (Tax Commissioner), and references the Department of Labor and Department of Administrative Services. Key agency provisions:\n\n- Department of Revenue: retains collection/remittance of municipal local option sales taxes, credits 3% (after refunds) to the Municipal Equalization Fund, and must notify municipalities of pending refund deductions (with revised annual estimate/adjustment reporting beginning 2025). Expands/clarifies authority to provide municipalities lists of retailers, to furnish confidential sales/use tax returns to a certified municipal representative (10 business days to prepare; secure electronic transmission allowed), and to provide lists of qualifying businesses on June 30 annually. For certain Nebraska Advantage/data‑center projects, Tax Commissioner/data disclosure requirements to municipalities are mandated.\n\n- Department of Labor: may receive tax return information necessary to administer Employment Security, Contractor Registration, or Employee Classification laws.\n\n- Department of Administrative Services: referenced in confidentiality prohibition; unauthorized disclosure by its employees is a Class I misdemeanor.\n\n- Budget impact: amounts held by municipalities for specified sales/use tax refunds are excluded from municipal restricted fund, cash reserve, and Property Tax Growth Limitation Act calculations. Department of Revenue: Adds that the Tax Commissioner must, upon request (by June 30 annually), provide municipalities a list of businesses that applied for tax incentives under the Employment and Investment Growth Act, Nebraska Advantage Act, ImagiNE Nebraska Act, or Urban Redevelopment Act, provided the information excludes detailed data on any particular business’s revenue, expenses, or operations. A municipal official certified under this provision may share copies of returns/return information with another municipal employee solely to verify collection/analysis/forecasting, allocation between municipalities, or that taxes are spent as voter‑approved. If tax proceeds are received but the originating incorporated municipality cannot be identified within six months, amounts are credited to the Municipal Equalization Fund. \n\nDepartment of Administrative Services and Department of Labor: no changes, funding, or appropriations affected. 109-1-LB614_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB614_Final_Copy.docx LB614 amends Neb. Rev. Statutes §§16-901 and 17-1001 governing extraterritorial zoning. It clarifies ETJ distances (city of the first class: generally 2 miles, but 1 mile for chapters 70-1001–70-1020; second-class cities/villages: generally 1 mile, but 1/2 mile for those same chapters). Cities and villages may apply municipal zoning, building, electrical and plumbing ordinances within their ETJ but may exempt certain farm buildings by action of the board of adjustment when consistent with the comprehensive plan. The bill defines qualifying farm buildings (per §77-1359; farmstead ≥20 acres and ≥$1,000 annual production). It requires written notice to the county board 30 days before final ETJ zoning decisions, with exceptions for counties >100,000 population or where a joint planning commission/department exists. Original sections are repealed. No funding or appropriations are included. Adds authority for local boards of adjustment to exempt certain farm buildings from zoning, building, electrical, plumbing, and related ordinances within a city’s or village’s extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction. The exemption may be granted by the board of adjustment of a city of the first class, city of the second class, or village if the structure is consistent with the comprehensive development plan and required population/economic projections (citing sections 19-907 to 19-915 and section 16-240). Defines "farm building" by reference to section 77-1359: on a 20+ acre farmstead producing ≥ $1,000/year in farm products. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB615_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB615_Intro_Copy.docx LB615 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §49-1401 to prohibit distribution of deceptive or fraudulent deepfakes and synthetic media depicting candidates, requires clear on-screen or audio disclosure for synthetic content, and permits candidates to seek injunctive or other equitable relief to stop such publications. Exceptions cover bona fide newscasts, broadcasters (including cable/satellite operators) when paid and acting in good faith, internet and print news outlets of general circulation that disclose inaccuracy, and satire/parody; federal-law-required candidate ads are preserved. The bill repeals the original §49-1401. No state agencies or departments are named in the bill, and it contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. No government agencies or departments are named or created, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. The added text sets disclosure rules for deceptive deepfakes: readable on visual media, displayed for the full video duration, and audio disclosures must be spoken at start and end and every ≤2 minutes for audio >2 minutes. Candidates may seek injunctive or equitable relief to block publication of deceptive deepfakes. Exemptions cover bona fide news broadcasts and broadcasters (including cable/satellite) when federally required to air candidate ads or when paid and a good‑faith check was made; routine news publications and internet outlets that clearly state the media is inaccurate; and satire/parody. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB616_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB616_Intro_Copy.docx LB616 authorizes limited use of automatic license plate reader (ALPR) systems and adjusts agency roles and fee handling.\n\n- Department (DMV) responsibilities: approve driver's safety training curriculum and fees; adopt rules/regulations; allow jurisdictions to use training fees to operate programs and other safety/education efforts.\n- Local authorities may enforce red‑light violations using ALPRs if they offer violators a choice to pay a fee or attend an approved driver's safety training (pretrial diversion). If the violator attends, the local authority must waive the program fee; no points assessed and no warrant for nonpayment/nonparticipation.\n- County treasurers collect unpaid fees as a condition of registration renewal and allocate proceeds to the county, local school system, school district, city, and village in the vehicle’s tax district.\n- Law enforcement ALPR use is otherwise restricted but permitted for specified enforcement purposes (including red‑light violations); ALPR evidence is limited to proceedings under this enforcement authority.\n\n[NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.] Adds authority for local authorities to enforce red‑light violations using automatic license plate reader (ALPR) systems (as defined in §60‑3202) for steady red indications (§60‑6,123) if specified conditions are met: offenders may pay a fee or enter a driver's safety training program via a pretrial diversion plan (see §§29‑3605 to 29‑3609); the program fee is waived if chosen; no motor‑vehicle points (§60‑4,182) or warrants for nonpayment are allowed. Noncompliance requires payment of the fee to the county treasurer before vehicle registration renewal (§60‑392). The county treasurer must allocate fee proceeds to the county, local school systems/districts, cities, and villages in the vehicle’s tax district. ALPR‑derived data is admissible only in proceedings enforcing this section. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB619_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB619_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Transportation The bill requires the Department of Transportation to award grants jointly to cities of the primary class and their counties to construct motor‑vehicle infrastructure connecting a highway (per §39‑101) to the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways. Recipients must report annually to the Department until grant funds are spent; unused funds must be repaid to the Department, which will remit them to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The Legislature intends a $15 million General Fund appropriation in FY2025‑26 to the Department of Transportation for this purpose. The act takes effect immediately. The added text directs the Department of Transportation to jointly award grants to primary-class cities and their counties to construct motor-vehicle transportation infrastructure that links a highway (per §39‑101) to the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways. Recipient cities/counties must file annual reports to DOT until grant funds are fully expended. Any grant money not used for its intended purpose must be repaid by the recipients to DOT, which will remit repayments to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The Legislature intends to appropriate $15 million from the General Fund to DOT in FY 2025–26 for this program. DOCX | PDF

Key new requirement: DHHS must, no later than September 30, 2025, submit an application to CMS to amend the aged-and-disabled Home and Community‑Based Services waiver to include a memory‑care rate for assisted‑living facilities. The statute also retains multiple DHHS deadlines for state plan amendments/waivers and program coverage duties (e.g., glucose monitors, postpartum extension, medical respite designation, breast pumps/lactation services, interpretation services), with several items funded by the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund and an intent that lactation consultation funding reflect a 145% rate increase. 109-1-LB620_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB620_Intro_Copy.docx LB620 creates the Neighborhood Revitalization Act and assigns primary implementation and enforcement roles to Nebraska district courts and local municipal corporations (counties, cities, villages, townships). District courts hear in rem actions, may issue orders of compliance, appoint receivers, establish and enforce a first-priority receiver's lien (subject only to general property tax liens), and supervise receiver auctions consistent with existing sale procedures (sec. 25-1516). Municipal corporations must be notified, may inspect parcels, may secure and maintain properties at their discretion and charge owners for costs, and must provide periodic updates to the court. Receivers must satisfy delinquent property tax liens within 30 days and may pay outstanding municipal fines, taxes, and assessments. Applications to serve as certified receivers are filed with the applicable court. No state appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Adds court-led Neighborhood Revitalization procedures that involve local governments and court offices. Key agency/office roles:\n- Municipal corporations (cities, counties, townships, villages) must be notified, may inspect parcels, may secure/maintain nuisance properties, and must provide periodic updates to the court; costs incurred may be charged to the property owner.\n- District courts have in-rem jurisdiction, may appoint receivers, approve plans, record orders, and supervise auctions.\n- County offices (clerk; register's office/register of deeds) must record notices, liens, and orders and handle filings.\n- References to state/local tax law (sections 77-203, 77-207) make receiver liens subordinate only to general property tax liens; receivers must satisfy delinquent property tax liens within 30 days.\n\nFunding/appropriations: no new government appropriations or budget allocations are created. The bill shifts costs to owners (municipal cost recovery, receiver liens/fees — 10% of receiver costs, minimum $2,500). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB621_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB621_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Health and Human Services • Department of Administrative Services — The bill conditions a transfer of up to $15 million from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to the Board of Regents for UNMC pancreatic cancer research on receipt of matching private/other funds certified by the budget administrator of the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services; upon such certification the State Treasurer must transfer an equal amount.\n\n• Department of Health and Human Services — The bill directs an increase of $7,500,000 in FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27 from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to DHHS (Program 502) for aid to specified community health centers (Charles Drew, OneWorld, Good Neighbor, Community Action Partnership of Western Nebraska, Nebraska Medicine Midtown, Bluestem, Heartland). Each center receives $700,000; remaining funds distributed proportionally by prior-year uninsured patient counts (Uniform Data System). Department of Health and Human Services: The bill directs that an increase of $7.5 million in each of FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27 from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund be transferred to DHHS (Program 502) to provide aid to named community health centers (Charles Drew, OneWorld, East Central/Good Neighbor, Community Action Partnership of Western Nebraska, Nebraska Medicine Midtown, Bluestem Health, Heartland Health). Each center receives $700,000; remaining funds are distributed pro rata based on the prior fiscal year's uninsured patient counts per the Uniform Data System. 109-1-LB622_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB622_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development, Department of Revenue - Department of Economic Development (DED): DED shall use the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to finance loans, grants, credit enhancements, the new Statewide Housing Assistance Program, and departmental expenses as appropriated by the Legislature (Sec. 58-705). DED must allocate at least 30% of available annual funds to each congressional district, announce a ≥90-day application period, develop a qualified allocation plan prioritizing lowest‑income projects and homebuyers, may contract for services or provide funds to governmental entities, and may recapture unused awards (Secs. 58-708, 58-706). The Statewide Housing Assistance Program will be administered by a nonprofit contracted by DED, providing lien‑secured downpayment loans up to $30,000 (Sec. 6). DED must report annually its budget for administration and planned fund distribution, including amounts for projects and administrative purposes (Sec. 58-711).\n\n- Department of Revenue (Tax Commissioner): The Tax Commissioner designs documentary stamp tax stamps and issues declaratory rulings; registers collect the tax. From each $2.55 collected, $0.50 stays with the county and $1.25 is credited to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (with specified credits to other funds); the Department will not overturn county assessor sale determinations without its own review (Secs. 76-903, 77-1327). Creates a Statewide Housing Assistance Program to be administered by a nonprofit contracted by the Department of Economic Development. The program provides statewide downpayment assistance (limited to $30,000 per homebuyer), available to applicants defined in department rules. Assistance must be used for a primary residence, is structured as a loan secured by a lien, and is repaid on transfer of title. Priority for trust-fund assistance is given to lowest-income homebuyers located in designated enterprise zones, federal opportunity zones, and areas declared extremely blighted under section 18-2101.02. No changes to the Department of Revenue or explicit appropriations/funding amounts are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB626_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB626_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor LB626 amends Community Development Law definitions to require the Department of Economic Development to annually update workforce housing construction-cost thresholds (Sec. 18-2103(33)(c)) using the most recent Producer Price Index published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. The bill contains no references to the Nebraska Department of Labor and includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. 109-1-LB627_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB627_Intro_Copy.docx Authorizes the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska to design and construct student residential facilities for nursing and allied health in Norfolk. The Board may enter long‑term financing agreements with private parties through June 30, 2045, may use conveyance/lease or lease‑back arrangements to facilitate financing, and may schedule payments monthly, quarterly, or semiannually; it may not pledge the State’s credit except for legislative appropriations. On or before August 31, 2045, unused project funds from the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund and the General Fund held in the treasury or by trustees must be transferred to the General Fund. Legislative intent protects appropriations until obligations are satisfied but not beyond FY ending June 30, 2045. Also an intended $250,000 appropriation to the Board for educational technology in Norfolk. Creates authority for the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska to design and build student residential facilities in Norfolk. State-supported project cost: $23,000,000, funded by the Legislature via intent to appropriate $1,150,000 annually for 20 years. Regents may enter long‑term financing agreements with private parties (payments through June 30, 2045), may convey/lease/lease‑back property to facilitate financing, and may schedule payments monthly/quarterly/semiannually. Regents may not pledge the State's credit except for legislative appropriations. Any project funds from the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund or the General Fund held in the treasury or by trustees and not needed for financing agreements must be transferred to the General Fund by August 31, 2045. 109-1-LB628_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB628_Intro_Copy.docx LB628 amends §§76-214 and 77-202 to adopt the Recreational Trail Easement Property Tax Exemption Act. It exempts a portion of property subject to qualifying recreational-trail easements from property tax and adds that exemption to the list in §77-202. It modifies recording procedures in §76-214: grantees must continue filing prescribed statements with the register of deeds, who forwards them to the county assessor; the county assessor processes statements per the Property Tax Administrator and the Tax Commissioner; statements are accessible at the Tax Commissioner, county assessor, or register of deeds per the State Records Administrator’s retention schedule. The bill excludes routine easements and oil/gas/mineral leases from the statement requirement but retains the requirement for conservation, preservation, and easements that qualify for the new recreational-trail exemption. Operative date: January 1, 2026. No funding or appropriations are included. Adds standards and procedures governing qualifying recreational trail easements: (1) criteria to ensure alignment with public access and conservation goals; (2) procedures for certifying public benefit, including connectivity requirements to existing or planned trail systems; and (3) methods to ensure ongoing compliance with the act’s public-purpose requirements. Also clarifies that easements (and portions of taxpayer-owned property) used to qualify for the property tax exemption under the Recreational Trail Easement Property Tax Exemption Act are covered. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB629_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB629_Intro_Copy.docx LB629 creates the County Initiative and Referendum Act, reserving to qualified electors of each Nebraska county the powers of initiative (to enact) and referendum (to amend or repeal) for measures affecting county governance. The bill governs use of those powers at the county level, defines "circulator" (a person soliciting petition signatures) and "measure" (an ordinance, charter provision, or resolution within a county board’s legislative authority), and excludes actions authorized under the Nebraska Advantage Transformational Tourism and Redevelopment Act. No state agencies beyond county governments or county boards are newly created or altered, and the bill includes no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. Creates the "County Initiative and Referendum Act," reserving initiative and referendum powers to qualified electors of each county and subjecting county governance measures to that Act. It recognizes county boards as the local legislative authority whose ordinances, charter provisions, or resolutions may be enacted or amended/repealed via initiative or referendum. Defines "circulator" (person soliciting petition signatures) and limits "measure" to matters within a county board's authority, excluding actions authorized under the Nebraska Advantage Transformational Tourism and Redevelopment Act. No state agencies or departments are newly created or referenced, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB62_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB62_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services LB62 appropriates $19,000,000 from the General Fund for FY2025‑26 to the Department of Administrative Services (Program 245). DAS is directed to provide those funds to the Office of the Chief Information Officer to: (1) establish interoperable communications between state agencies and volunteer departments (portable and mobile radios, programming, installation), and (2) fund a grant program for training and connecting volunteer departments to the Statewide Radio System. Grant eligibility is based on number/type of radios required; the CIO may not charge subscription, programming, or training fees to volunteer departments after a grant. The Legislature intends all grant funds distributed by June 30, 2028. The bill takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. The bill appropriates $19,000,000 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Department of Administrative Services (Program 245). DAS must transfer these funds to the Office of the Chief Information Officer to run a grant program that equips volunteer departments and agencies for interoperability with the Statewide Radio System — including portable/mobile radios, programming, installation, and interoperability training. Eligibility is based on each volunteer department's size and radio needs. Grantees may not be charged subscription, programming, or training fees after receiving a grant. 109-1-LB630_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB630_Intro_Copy.docx LB630 amends the Occupational Therapy Practice Act. Key agency actions:\n\n- The board (state occupational therapy licensing board) retains authority to approve training courses and examinations, identify subjects for the national licensure exam, and recognize equivalent certification entities (e.g., Hand Therapy Certification Commission).\n- The department is directed to issue certificates authorizing occupational therapists to apply physical‑agent and instrument‑assisted modalities and to authorize occupational therapy assistants to set up/implement superficial thermal modalities when board‑approved training/exams and onsite supervision requirements are met.\n- Temporary licenses may be issued to applicants but only to practice in association with a licensed occupational therapist; examination results are sent to the board.\n- Supervision is defined with clear accountability for therapists and assistants.\n\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds licensing and scope provisions for occupational therapy. Key agency references: the state occupational therapy licensing board (the “board”) and the entity that administers the national licensure examination. New provisions require applicants to follow the exam administrator’s rules, and exam results must be sent to the board to verify entry‑level competency. A temporary license now expires on issuance of a permanent license, on denial, 180 days after issuance, or upon notification of exam failure. Substantive additions define required evaluation domains (ADLs, IADLs, performance patterns/skills, client factors), intervention approaches (remediation, compensation, maintenance, health promotion, prevention), specific interventions (therapeutic occupations, training, remediation, injury prevention, occupational justice, group interventions), and a supervision standard making therapists accountable for assistants/aides. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB632_Intro Select File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB632_Intro_Copy.docx LB632 (2025) requires health care facilities that perform elective abortions to provide individual disposition of the physical remains of an aborted unborn child by cremation or interment (burial), or otherwise as directed by the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services’ Board of Health. The bill makes other methods of depositing or disposing of such remains unlawful and does not require notice to the woman treated. Introduced to the Legislature and heard by the Health and Human Services Committee. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds requirement that health care facilities performing elective abortions must individually dispose of fetal remains by cremation or burial (interment); if those are not possible, disposition is to follow directions from the Board of Health. Declares legislative purpose to protect public health/welfare and express respect for the dignity of unborn children. Prohibits disposal methods other than those specified. Specifies no obligation to notify the patient of the method of disposition. No agencies other than the Board of Health are referenced and no funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB633_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB633_Intro_Copy.docx LB633 amends section 79-239 and creates the "Nebraska Option Enrollment Tuition Account Program," assigning primary roles to the State Board of Education and the State Department of Education. Rejecting school districts must provide certified written notice to parents explaining reasons for rejection and advising parents of (1) the right to appeal to the State Board under the Administrative Procedure Act or (2) the right to decline appeal and request a tuition/scholarship account. Parents have 30 days to file either action; upon receipt the State Board must issue an option enrollment tuition account. Beginning July 1, 2024, school districts must annually submit prescribed data on rejected applications to the Commissioner of Education; the Commissioner compiles and reports to the Legislature annually. The State Board may use up to 5% of scholarship account funds for program administration or contracting and may adopt rules. The act is effective on passage (emergency clause). Adds a process letting parents who decline to appeal a rejected enrollment option request an “option enrollment tuition” (scholarship) account from the State Board of Education. The request plus a copy of the rejection notice must be received by the State Board within 30 days of the parent's notification; upon receipt the Board must issue the account. Defines terms (Board = State Board of Education; eligible student = student whose application was rejected; parent; Program = Nebraska Option Enrollment Tuition Account Program). An eligible student satisfies compulsory attendance if parent and student meet program requirements. Clarifies the State has no new authority over participating schools. Budget: the State Board may use up to 5% of scholarship account funds for program administration or contracting. The Board may adopt rules to implement the program. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB634_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB634_Intro_Copy.docx LB634 creates the Legislative Sunset Review Act, abolishes the Legislature’s Planning Committee, and repeals sections 50-419.03, 50-435, 50-1401–1404, R.R.S. The bill establishes a Legislative Sunset Review Committee (membership: Executive Board chair, Appropriations Committee chair, and five legislators appointed by the Executive Board with geographic representation). The committee receives staff support from legislative divisions and the Legislative Council. Reviewable entities (state agencies, reviewable entities, and their advisory committees) must submit detailed performance, compliance, and advisory-committee reports to the Clerk of the Legislature; initial reviews begin in 2027 and recur every five years. The committee may access records, request assistance from state agencies and officers, and exercise standing-committee powers. References include the Auditor of Public Accounts, the Open Meetings Act, and public records statutes. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are specified. Operative January 1, 2026. Creates a Legislative Sunset Review Committee (membership: chair of the Legislature's Appropriations Committee plus five members chosen by the Legislative Council Executive Board with geographic balance); chair/vice-chair elected by the committee; initial appointments after Jan 1, 2026; legislative divisions provide staff support. The committee must publish a review schedule on the Legislature's website, begin reviews in 2027, and review each "reviewable entity" every five years. Reviewable entities must electronically file detailed reports with the Clerk of the Legislature (performance measures, compliance with public records/Open Meetings and small/minority purchasing laws, Auditor of Public Accounts findings, advisory committee details, privatization options, overlap/duplication, etc.), validated by the entity’s administrator. The committee may access records, request assistance from reviewable entities, state agencies, and officers, inspect files, and exercise standing-committee powers. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB635_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB635_Final_Copy.docx LB635 expands regulation of combat sports to authorize the State Athletic Commissioner to regulate professional bare‑knuckle mixed martial arts, professional mixed martial arts on ice, professional and amateur muay thai, and amateur kickboxing, and harmonizes licensing and enforcement across covered disciplines. The commissioner may adopt rules, grant/revoke licenses for promoters, officials, physicians, managers, matchmakers, contestants, etc., set license fees (specified minimum/maximum ranges), require bonds ($1,000 minimum for amateur; $5,000 minimum for professional), limit number of events, and establish banned‑substance testing with graduated suspensions/fines. License and event reporting obligations include payment of a 5% tax on gross receipts (and 5% of television rights). Administrative fines are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution pursuant to Article VII, section 5, and contested fines are adjudicated under the Administrative Procedure Act. Adds extensive, repetitive coverage of combat-sport activities—naming professional bare‑knuckle mixed martial arts, professional mixed martial arts on ice, professional muay thai, amateur muay thai, and amateur kickboxing, and referring to matches and contestants. No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB636_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB636_Intro_Copy.docx LB636 authorizes counties to seek state reimbursement for medical services provided to county jail inmates and assigns administration to the Jail Standards Board. The board may define eligible costs, audit county records (at least biennially or as needed), set rules, require counties to retain supporting records two years, deny claims caused by jail or staff misconduct, and request warrants on the State Treasurer to pay approved amounts to county treasurers (credited to county general funds). Claims must be filed within 45 days after each fiscal quarter. The Legislature caps annual appropriations for the Jail Standards Board’s eligible criminal court cost reimbursements at $21 million beginning FY2025-26. LB636 also revises sheriff and distress-warrant fee schedules (dollar amounts, mileage calculation, $10 minimum per service, reporting to county boards, and commissions on tax collections), redirects specified fees to county general funds, and takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. Adds procedures and limits for county jail medical-cost reimbursement administered by the Jail Standards Board. Key agency actions: county boards must certify reimbursement claims and submit them to the Jail Standards Board within 45 days after each quarter end or lose eligibility; the Board may audit county records (at least once every two years), request additional information, and has sole authority to determine reimbursable medical costs and adopt rules. If approved, the Board requests a warrant from the State Treasurer to pay the county treasurer; funds are credited to the county general fund. Reimbursement is barred for costs caused by negligence, recklessness, or intentional misconduct. For FY2025‑26 and thereafter, legislative appropriations to the Jail Standards Board for eligible criminal court cost reimbursement are capped at $21 million annually. The text also authorizes county sheriffs to charge fees for additional officers serving warrants (minimum fee language appears). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB637_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB637_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Transportation - The Department of Transportation is authorized to enter into agreements with approved Destination Nebraska district applicants to construct roads, bridges, and other infrastructure within destination districts; such infrastructure must comply with applicable federal and state laws and codes.\n\n- The Department of Economic Development is directed to update workforce housing unit cost limits annually based on the most recent change in the Producer Price Index for all commodities published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics (explicit federal Department of Labor reference).\n\n- The bill contains no department-specific appropriations, funding allocations, or budgetary changes directed to these agencies. - Department of Economic Development (DED): DED is authorized to accept destination-district applications through Dec. 31, 2025, review/approve up to two statewide districts meeting strict eligibility (>$3 billion new development; ≥10 million annual visitors). DED sets the additional state occupation tax rate for transactions in a district after public hearing, may designate a trustee to hold occupation-tax proceeds and use them in agreements, may approve boundary adjustments, and may form and staff a Community Redevelopment Authority for a district. Applicants may issue bonds (not state obligations) and use district funds for eligible costs.\n\n- Department of Transportation (DOT): DOT may enter agreements with district applicants to construct roads, bridges, and other infrastructure within a district (must meet federal/state codes).\n\n- Department of Labor: Not mentioned; no changes to Labor agency duties or funding. 109-1-LB638_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB638_Intro_Copy.docx LB638 assigns administration of the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Act to the Nebraska Department of Natural Resources (DNR), authorizing collaboration with Natural Resources Districts. It (re)creates the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund under DNR control, permits transfers/gifts/grants into the fund, and requires DNR to apply (before the FY2025‑26 deadline) for a $25 million Nebraska Environmental Trust grant payable in five $5 million annual installments. If awarded, the State Treasurer will credit proceeds to the cash fund and DNR must maintain a subaccount for the Trust grant; monthly interest earnings to that subaccount trigger an equal transfer from the cash fund back to the Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund. Awarded grants are credited to the cash fund. The state investment officer will invest fund balances under existing investment statutes. The Act now terminates December 31, 2030, and takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. The added provisions require the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to apply, before the FY2025‑26 application deadline, for a $25 million grant from the Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund (NETF), payable in five $5 million annual installments. If awarded, the State Treasurer will credit the grant proceeds to the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund to support the project purposes consistent with that fund. DNR must create a subaccount within the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund for the NETF grant receipts, calculate monthly interest earned on that subaccount, and notify the State Treasurer, who will transfer an equal amount from the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund back to the NETF. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB639_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB639_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Insurance LB639 designates "Department" as the Nebraska Department of Insurance and assigns it duties related to dental plan carrier minimum dental loss ratios. 109-1-LB640_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB640_Final_Copy.docx LB640 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §47-502 to change good‑time credit rules for persons confined in city or county jails, including those serving custodial sanctions for parole or probation violations. After the fifteenth day of confinement, the bill requires that the aggregate remaining term—including the sum of all consecutive sentences received at the same time or during confinement—be reduced one day for each day the person does not commit a breach of discipline or other violation of jail regulations. 109-1-LB641_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB641_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB641 amends Medicaid estate-recovery provisions administered by the Department of Health and Human Services (the department). Key department authorities/requirements: recover Medicaid payments from a recipient’s estate (debts accrue in life but are collected after death subject to spouse/qualifying-child exceptions); refrain from foreclosing liens on a home in specified sibling/adult-child residency/care situations (physician attestation suffices); certify to personal representatives or other authorized parties whether reimbursement is due (applications may be delivered as designated, including email; department to post acceptable delivery methods); may release property, waive or compromise claims, and adopt rules and regulations; recover from third-party recoveries with pro rata share of attorney fees; retroactive application to Aug. 30, 2015. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. For the Department of Health and Human Services: the bill allows physician attestation that a sibling, adult child, or other relative provided care which delayed a recipient’s admission to a medical institution to serve as sufficient documentation for two purposes: (1) to enable the department to avoid foreclosure on its medical-assistance lien when such familial care occurred; and (2) to exclude a retained life‑estate interest in real property from the recipient’s estate — provided the life estate has been recorded at least 12 months and the relative resided solely and continuously with the recipient and demonstrates to the department that their care delayed institutionalization. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB642_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB642_Intro_Copy.docx LB642 creates the "Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Act" regulating high‑risk AI deployments. Key government roles:\n\n- Nebraska Attorney General: may, in ongoing investigations, compel deployers or contracted third parties to produce risk‑management policies, impact assessments, and related records within 90 days; may evaluate compliance; disclosed materials are exempt from public‑record release and may be designated proprietary. The Attorney General also determines whether federal/state prudential regulator guidance for banks/credit unions is "substantially equivalent" for exemption purposes.\n\n- Federal references: research exceptions must comply with 45 C.F.R. part 46 and applicable FDA requirements; law enforcement and other federal/state/municipal authorities are recognized for compliance and investigatory actions.\n\nNo changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are contained in the bill. Adds roles for multiple government actors but no funding changes. Key points:\n- The state Attorney General may, during investigations, compel deployers or contracted third parties to produce risk‑management policies, impact assessments, and related records within 90 days, may evaluate compliance, and may designate disclosures as nonpublic or trade secrets.\n- Exempts entities subject to examination by state or federal prudential regulators (banks, credit unions, affiliates, service providers) if the regulator’s guidance is deemed by the Attorney General to be substantially equivalent or stricter and requires regular audits and mitigation of algorithmic discrimination.\n- Permits cooperation with law enforcement and compliance with federal, state, or municipal authorities and subpoenas.\n- References federal authorities: FDA requirements and HHS Common Rule (45 C.F.R. part 46) for research exceptions.\n- No appropriations, budget, or funding provisions are added. 109-1-LB645_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB645_Final_Copy.docx Bill LB645 amends state retirement funding and administrative procedures, naming agencies and fiscal actions:\n\n- Retirement Board: certifies annual state deposits to the School Retirement Fund; administrator of Class V systems must supply membership data for actuarial calculations.\n- State Treasurer and Director of Administrative Services: execute transfers from appropriated state funds on the Board’s warrant.\n- State Investment Officer: may invest amounts in the Service Annuity Fund under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.\n- Appropriations Committee/Legislature: may consider supplemental transfers to Class V districts upon request following an actuarial finding.\n\nKey funding changes:\n- Employee contributions to the School Retirement Fund become funded‑ratio‑based starting July 1, 2025 (9.75%, 8.75%, 8.0%, or 7.25% depending on funded ratio).\n- State deposits to the School Retirement Fund become funded‑ratio‑based (2.0%, 0.7%, or 0%) beginning July 1, 2025.\n- Beginning July 1, 2025, the state will transfer 2% of compensation annually to Class V school districts for their retirement systems; Service Annuity Fund transfers for normal cost and amortization continue.\n- Nebraska State Patrol Retirement: survivor benefits increase to 100% of an officer’s annuity effective July 1, 2027.\n\nThe act contains an emergency clause making it effective upon enactment. Adds funding and benefit rules for Class V school district and statewide school retirement systems. Key points:\n\n- State must annually transfer to a Class V district’s retirement fund an amount equal to 2% of members’ compensation beginning FY 2026 (transfer due by July 1); statute clarifies this does not shift district liability to the state.\n- Employee contribution rates to the School Retirement Fund (set July 1 each year, based on the funded ratio from the actuarial valuation prepared for the retirement board under §84-1503) are tiered beginning July 1, 2025: <96% = 9.75%; 96–<98% = 8.75%; 98–<100% = 8.00%; ≥100% = 7.25%. Deposits transmitted with employer contributions.\n- State deposits into the School Retirement Fund (also based on funded ratio) beginning 2025: <96% = 2.0% of pay; 96–<100% = 0.7%; ≥100% = none.\n- Effective July 1, 2027, surviving spouses and dependent children receive 100% of an officer’s annuity (spouse for life; children under 19 divided equally). 109-1-LB655_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB655_Intro_Copy.docx LB655 establishes a statutory "right of medical conscience" allowing health care providers and payors to opt out of participating in or paying for specific health care services based on sincerely held religious, moral, or ethical beliefs. The Attorney General may investigate, administer oaths, take depositions, inspect (when authorized), issue and serve subpoenas, compel evidence and witnesses, commence civil suits for damages or injunctive relief, award attorney fees, and adopt implementing rules. 109-1-LB661_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB661_Intro_Copy.docx LB661 assigns specific investment and reporting duties to state financial entities. The Nebraska Investment Council (appointed members) and the state investment officer are designated fiduciaries for investments of retirement systems administered by the Public Employees Retirement Board, the Nebraska educational savings plan trust, the ABLE program, and state funds; they must avoid investments whose primary objective is economic development or social purposes and must not invest with listed "restricted entities." The state investment officer must identify and divest retirement-system holdings in restricted entities and provide monthly pooled-accounts reports to the Governor, State Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Department of Administrative Services, and the council.
