109-2-LB1130_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1130_Intro_Copy.docx The bill revises the Community Improvement District Act, assigning specific duties to state and local officials and expanding fiscal and oversight powers. City/village councils and clerks must approve CID formation, plans and levies; county treasurers serve ex officio as CID treasurers, create CID funds/accounts, collect/disburse CID property taxes, special assessments and municipal sewer charges, and must segregate/manage special assessment funds per directions. County clerks, election commissioners and registers of deeds receive filings/notices; election commissioners administer trustee elections by mail. The Auditor of Public Accounts receives CID budgets/audits (filed annually), may waive or order audits, and may appoint an administrator for troubled CIDs who can assume board powers, negotiate/issue bonds or warrants and levy a separate tax. District courts review bonds/warrants, adjudicate appeals, may approve warrant-extension proceedings (including limited court-ordered levy increases) and enforce court settlements. The Secretary of State will design uniform recall petition forms. The act takes effect immediately. Added provisions identify and assign roles to government entities and clarify fiscal processes for community improvement districts (CIDs). Key agencies and duties:\n\n- City/village clerk and city council/village board: file and publish formation/amendment/annexation/dissolution/assessment notices, hold hearings, approve plans, ordinances, and levy limits.\n- County treasurer: serves as ex officio treasurer for the CID, establishes funds/accounts, collects taxes and special assessments, deposits and disburses CID funds per trustees/administrator.\n- Register of deeds, election commissioner, county clerk: receive filings, notices, and handle election administration (filing clerk defined as election commissioner or county clerk).\n- Auditor of Public Accounts: receives annual budgets and audits, may waive audits, has access to records, and—if a CID is in default—may appoint an administrator.\n- District court: oversees contests, approves debt compromises and certain tax-levy increases.\n- Secretary of State: designs uniform recall petition papers.\n\nFunding: CIDs may levy property taxes up to a stated maximum, create general/bond/other funds, issue bonds/warrants, and levy special assessments. Audits and bond premium costs are paid from CID funds; audit fees can become a lien if compelled by the Auditor. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1131_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1131_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue LB1131 creates the Domestic Violence and Human Trafficking Service Providers Tax Credit Act (operative Jan 1, 2027). It authorizes refundable Nebraska income tax credits totaling $6,000,000 annually: $480,000 equally to qualifying tribal domestic violence/sexual‑assault programs; $300,000 to a statewide coalition of nonprofits that have an affiliation agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services under the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act; and $5,220,000 to be distributed among providers (including $2,088,000 equally to the tribal and coalition groups, $2,505,600 by program service‑area population, and $626,400 by service‑area square mileage). The bill defines "department" as the Department of Revenue, requires the Department of Revenue to distribute the credits each taxable year, authorizes rulemaking, and requires credit sellers to notify the Department of Revenue prior to a purchaser claiming transferred credits. Creates the "Domestic Violence and Human Trafficking Service Providers Tax Credit Act" (effective for tax years beginning/treated as beginning on/after Jan 1, 2027). Establishes $6.0 million annually in refundable Nebraska income tax credits administered by the Department of Revenue, distributed each year as: $480,000 equally to tribal-run domestic violence/sexual assault programs; $300,000 to a statewide coalition of nonprofits that have an affiliation agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to serve victims under the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act; and $5,220,000 allocated (a) $2,088,000 equally to the tribal programs and the DHHS‑affiliated coalition, (b) $2,505,600 by program service‑area population, and (c) $626,400 by service‑area square miles. Credits are transferable/sellable with 30‑day prior notice to Revenue; Revenue may adopt implementing rules. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1132_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1132_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB1132 amends Neb. Rev. DHHS must, by October 1, 2026, file a Medicaid state plan amendment with CMS to provide coverage for FDA‑approved long‑acting injectable and extended‑release medications when administered for serious mental illness or substance use disorder in any hospital, emergency department, or inpatient setting, including state hospitals and state psychiatric facilities. 109-2-LB1134_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1134_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services References to the Department of Administrative Services are limited to the State Building Administrator. Under amended section 72-804, the State Building Administrator of the Department of Administrative Services, in consultation with the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, may (a) specify a more recent edition of the International Energy Conservation Code, (b) set additional energy efficiency or renewable energy requirements, and (c) grant waivers supported by life-cycle cost analyses; agencies receiving state funding must provide those analyses to the State Building Administrator. Under amended section 72-805, the Director of Water, Energy, and Environment may adopt rules in consultation with the State Building Administrator. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. Adds requirements limiting local code updates: counties, cities, and villages cannot adopt or enforce local building, electrical, or energy code updates unless independent third‑party evidence shows the change is necessary to protect the public from "eminently dangerous situations" or required by state/federal law. The third party must have no financial interest and possess expertise in public safety or municipal codes; "eminently dangerous" = imminent, unreasonable risk of death or severe injury. Until Jan. 1, 2031, local construction/building, electrical, and energy codes may not be more stringent or more up‑to‑date than the state building code, the National Electrical Code adopted by the State Electrical Board, or the Nebraska Energy Code. No changes to the Department of Administrative Services' duties, appropriations, or budgetary allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1135_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1135_Intro_Copy.docx Bill updates the Nebraska Municipal Land Bank Act. Key agency/department items:\n\n- Board composition and appointments: voting members (minimum seven) appointed by a municipality’s chief executive and confirmed by two‑thirds of its governing body; nonvoting members must include the municipality’s planning director (or designee) and a governing‑body appointee. Clerk roles specified for removal hearings.\n- Removal authority: for multi‑municipal banks, removal is by the chief executive of the municipality in which the majority of land‑bank property is located, subject to governing‑body review.\n- Powers/financial interactions: land banks may borrow from municipalities, the state, federal funds, or private lenders, and procure state/federal insurance or guarantees; bond issuance is prohibited after Nov. 14, 2020. Contracts may be executed with municipal agencies or departments to perform functions on behalf of one another.\n- Property rules: jurisdictional holding limits by city class; commercial acquisitions limited (e.g., three years vacancy or failed nuisance abatement); requires community benefits agreements when holding property for private/nonprofit entities over one year.\n- Reporting: boards must report to creating municipality after each meeting or quarterly and submit an annual electronic report to the Chair of the Legislature’s Urban Affairs Committee by March 1 with specified financial and property details.\n\nNo new appropriations or state budget allocations are included. Adds residency requirements and reporting and community-benefits conditions for land banks. Key agency references: municipal land banks, the creating municipality, counties, and properties held under agreements with nonprofit or private entities per subsection 18-3408(8). Changes:\n- Board membership: each voting member must reside in the creating municipality, within 10 miles, in its extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction, or in the county; a majority must reside in the creating municipality (with location-of-property clarifications where property is held under 18-3408(8)).\n- Deposited property held on behalf of others for more than one year may require the depositing entity to enter a community benefits agreement (land bank plus local community groups) committing to specified benefits (e.g., affordable housing, local hiring).\n- Reporting: board must provide an electronic report after each meeting or at least quarterly, including whether property is held on behalf of a nonprofit/private entity under 18-3408(8) and the intended use of such property.\nNo changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1136_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1136_Intro_Copy.docx LB1136 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §13-905 (Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act). Key agency/departamental provisions:\n- Requires each political subdivision to post on its website the official or law department authorized to receive tort claims, identifying that person/department by name, title, and mailing address.\n- Permits governing bodies to designate claims be filed with the subdivision’s law department.\n- Filing with the listed official or law department constitutes substantial compliance.\n- If the subdivision fails to keep the website information accurate and up to date, statutory deadlines for submitting a written claim and for filing suit under §§13-919 and 13-920 are tolled.\n- Confirms the duty of the receiving official to present claims to the governing body and retains existing content requirements for written claims.\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The original §13-905 is repealed. Requires every political subdivision to post on its website home page a notice naming the official or law department authorized to receive claims, giving that person/department's name, title and a mailing address. Filing a claim with the named official/department counts as substantial compliance with the statutory claim-filing requirement. If the subdivision fails to keep that information accurate and current, the time limits to submit a written claim and to file suit under sections 13-919 and 13-920 are tolled. No funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1137_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1137_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Insurance The bill adds and clarifies several provisions involving the Department of Insurance (department). It criminalizes knowingly making false entries in material documents filed with or required by the Department of Insurance (Insurance Fraud Act amendments). It directs the Department of Insurance to strictly enforce insurer obligations under subdivision (13) of §44-1540 (reasonable, accurate explanations for claim denials or compromise offers). Public adjuster provisions require contracts and certain compensation terms to be provided to or available for inspection by the department or its director (no redaction of compensation; contracts must be available for inspection), and insurers must verify a public adjuster’s license with the department upon receiving an insured-signed authorization. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included. Adds multiple consumer-protection and licensure provisions affecting the Department of Insurance (DOI). Key points: expands prohibited conduct enforceable under the Public Adjusters Licensing Act (unlicensed representation/operation, unlawful rebates, knowingly misrepresenting claim damages); defines and bans "post‑loss assignments" (voids such contracts; licensed public adjusters may accept assignments only to the extent of their fee); requires insurers, upon receiving a public adjuster notification, to verify the adjuster’s license with the DOI; mandates homeowner cancellation notices and a five‑business‑day cancellation right for certain contracts; prohibits adjuster advertising of damage without inspection and offering to pay/waive deductibles as inducements. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1138_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1138_Intro_Copy.docx LB1138 enacts the Nebraska Protection of Seniors from Insurance Exploitation Act, authorizing insurers and designated “trained individuals” to notify permissible third parties and initiate internal reviews when they reasonably suspect financial exploitation of a senior or vulnerable adult. The bill requires insurers to notify the Director of Insurance within seven business days of any delay of a disbursement and to provide review status updates on request. It allows timed delays of 15, 25, or up to 55 business days depending on continued concern, and permits the Director or other interested parties to petition a court to terminate, extend, or modify a delay. The bill grants civil and administrative immunity to insurers, trained individuals, and good‑faith third parties acting under the Act. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds the "Nebraska Protection of Seniors from Insurance Exploitation Act" and designates the Director of Insurance as the official ("Director") to be notified. Insurers who delay a disbursement due to suspected exploitation must notify the Director within seven business days, provide reasons and review status, and supply updates on request. The text allows the Director to petition a court to terminate, extend, or modify a delay. It also permits insurer/individual reviews by the insurer, Director, or a "relevant agency" (and involvement of law enforcement) without prior third‑party notice. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1139_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1139_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB1139 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-371 to make a Title IV-D Division payment history from the Department of Health and Human Services admissible as prima facie evidence that child or spousal support payments are current. Such a payment history (showing payments current for the prior 12 months or the life of the order, whichever is shorter) operates to release the statutory lien for purposes of transferring a specific parcel of real property. A certified copy from the Title IV-D Division is likewise prima facie evidence and is valid for 30 days after certification. No funding, appropriation, or budgetary provisions for the Department are included. Adds that a child- or spousal-support judgment creates a lien on a debtor’s real or personal property that attaches when a payment is due and ends when the payment is made. It authorizes the Title IV‑D Division of the Department of Health and Human Services to provide a current payment history showing that support payments have been made as ordered for the past 12 months (or for the order’s entire duration if shorter); that record is prima facie proof the payments are current and, for purposes of transferring a specific parcel of real property, operates to release the lien. No changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1140_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1140_Intro_Copy.docx Amends Laws 2025, LB261, §54 (Agency No. 13 — State Department of Education, Program No. 351 Vocational Rehabilitation). FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 appropriation lines are shown (General Fund: $6,561,850 → $6,724,525; Cash Fund: $557,883 → $571,719; Federal: $30,807,902 → $31,596,542; Program total: $37,927,635 → $38,892,786; Salary limit: $15,709,139 → $16,203,613). Each year includes $49,289 GF and $8,560,706 federal funds earmarked for state aid. It directs the SDE’s Division of Rehabilitation Services and DHHS’s Division of Developmental Disabilities to collaborate on employment for individuals with disabilities and maximize federal matching funds under WIOA and the HCBS Final Rule. Adds a FY2026‑27 appropriation of $500,000 General Fund to "this program" to establish a multi‑trade pre‑apprenticeship pilot serving young adults, preparing them for registered apprenticeships and entry‑level construction employment in a city of the metropolitan class. 109-2-LB1141_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1141_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Labor The bill amends §81-407 to (1) confirm the Department of Labor as administrator of the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund and specify permitted uses (workforce development grants; program administration; unemployment insurance tax and benefit costs; labor studies; and Manufacturing Modernization and Workforce Development Pilot Investment Act purposes); (2) add the Nebraska Youth Pre‑Apprentice Conservation Program Fund as an allowable transfer destination from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund (transfers may also be made to the General Fund or Nebraska Opportunity Grant Fund) at the Legislature’s direction; and (3) retain the Commissioner of Labor’s authority over grant approvals and related reporting. It also authorizes transfers to be made administratively as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. The added language authorizes the budget administrator in the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services to direct administrative transfers “after the effective date of this act, on such dates and in such amounts” and explicitly adds the Nebraska Youth Pre‑Apprentice Conservation Program Fund as a fund subject to those directions. 109-2-LB1142_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1142_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Transportation - Designates the Department of Economic Development (DED) as the agency to administer the Nebraska Visitors Development Act (defines "Department" as DED). DED will appoint a Director of Tourism, locate and staff the Nebraska Tourism Commission, absorb commission employees, adopt rules, run grant programs, and administer the State Visitors Promotion Cash Fund, the Nebraska Tourism Promotional Cash Fund, and the Tourism Conference Cash Fund.\n\n- Requires DED to comply with Department of Administrative Services (DAS) procurement rules for contracts and references the DAS budget division's budget administrator in directing a $1,000,000 transfer from the State Visitors Promotion Cash Fund to the General Fund on or before June 30, 2019.\n\n- Directs the Department of Transportation to erect and maintain highway tourism markers and determine their exact locations (with public safety consideration).\n\n- Fiscal provisions: 10% of the cash-device tax is allocated to the Nebraska Tourism Promotional Cash Fund; beginning October 1, 2024, investment earnings on the State Visitors Promotion Cash Fund are credited to the General Fund. - Department of Economic Development (DED): Adds/clarifies that DED will administer the Nebraska Visitors Development Act and establishes a Director of Tourism within DED. DED may employ staff and contract for services; procure and evaluate data; develop/approve state marketing campaigns; run a promotional/technical-assistance/state-aid program for local governments and the tourism industry; cooperate with public and private partners; and adopt rules to implement the Act. The Director of Economic Development appoints the Director of Tourism (salary set by the Director of Economic Development; serves at pleasure). For administrative purposes the commission will be located and staffed within DED. \n- Department of Administrative Services: no changes or funding actions specified. \n- Department of Transportation: no changes or funding actions specified. \n- Funding/appropriations: none provided in the added text. 109-2-LB1143_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1143_Intro_Copy.docx Amends §68-949 to require the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to: identify the total dollar appropriation for Medicaid nursing facility rates in the state budget and use that amount as the base for rate calculations (including the annual inflation factor); consider client utilization and preferred setting when setting prospective rates; and, if DHHS uses a different dollar amount or projection of resident days, report those figures to the Legislature. DHHS must file an annual August 1 report to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst and Clerk explaining the inflation-factor calculation and a December 15–31 report identifying any remaining unobligated prior appropriations for Medicaid nursing facility payments (including encumbrances and retroactive payments). DHHS also must submit an application to CMS to establish a Money Follows the Person program by December 31, 2026, and develop recommendations on eligibility and defined-benefit modifications. The original section is repealed. Adds requirements for the state "department" (state Medicaid/long‑term care agency) to:\n- Consider client needs and preferred setting utilization when setting prospective nursing facility rates.\n- If the department uses a dollar amount different from the appropriation in its rate calculation, report that dollar amount and the projected number of nursing facility resident days to the Legislature in the required subdivision (4)(b) report.\n- By December 31, 2026, submit an application to the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to establish a Money Follows the Person program to help qualified individuals move from institutional to community long‑term care settings.\n\nNo new appropriations are specified; the additions impose reporting and an application deadline and increase transparency around any divergence from budgeted appropriations. 109-2-LB1144_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1144_Intro_Copy.docx LB1144 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 68‑927 and 68‑928 (Medical Assistance Act). At the department's request (the agency administering state benefit programs, including the medical assistance program), licensed insurers and self‑funded insurers must provide coverage information without an individual's authorization for eligibility determinations and benefit coordination. Such requests must specify the individual and be answered within 30 days unless good cause is shown. Coverage information for limited‑benefit policies is restricted to whether coverage exists and a description, and may be used only for eligibility determinations. Entities issuing a health plan (explicitly including service benefit plans, managed care organizations, pharmacy benefit managers, and other parties legally responsible for payment) must respond to department claims submitted within three years of service and may not deny claims solely for late submission, form type, or point‑of‑sale documentation when department conditions are met; responses must be provided within 30 days. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The original sections are repealed. Requires entities that issue health plans—including service benefit plans, managed care organizations, pharmacy benefit managers, or any party legally responsible for payment—to respond to requests from "the department" about claims submitted within three years of the date of service. Such issuers may not deny a department-submitted claim solely for late submission, claim form type/format, or lack of point-of-sale documentation if (1) the department submitted the claim within three years of service and (2) the department begins enforcement action within six years of claim submission. Issuers must provide the requested information to the department within 30 days unless good cause is shown. Requests must specify the individual covered. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1145_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1145_Intro_Copy.docx LB1145 amends Neb. §84-1411 (Open Meetings Act). It requires each public body to use a notice method designated by the body and recorded in its minutes and to transmit notice to members and the public. If a newspaper refuses publication, the public body must (i) post the notice on its website if available, (ii) request the newspaper post to a statewide repository if available, and (iii) post in a conspicuous public place, keeping written records. Agenda alteration cutoffs are specified (generally 24 hours; 48 hours for some off‑site municipal meetings).\n\nThe bill clarifies virtual‑meeting authority and procedures for numerous entities including state agencies/boards/committees and advisory committees, interlocal and joint public agencies, public power and irrigation districts, educational service units and their coordinating council, community college boards, the Nebraska Brand Committee, local public health departments, metropolitan utilities districts, regional transit authorities, natural resources districts, risk‑management pools, and similar bodies. It authorizes expanded virtual meeting rules during gubernatorial emergency declarations and repeals the original section. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds notice rules for "public bodies": each must designate a notice method and record, at least twice yearly in its minutes, the regular meeting schedule, location, and how it will provide reasonable advance publicized notice. It requires notice by publication in a legal newspaper of general circulation in the public body's jurisdiction. Exempted are governing bodies of cities of the second class, villages, their advisory committees, and governing bodies of rural or suburban fire protection districts. Noncompliance with the cited subdivision does not render actions (motions, resolutions, ordinances, etc.) void or voidable. The insertion includes cross‑reference/numbering language about newspaper publication options. No state agencies or departments beyond local governing bodies are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are added. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1146_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1146_Intro_Copy.docx LB1146 amends §79-209 to tighten school attendance reporting and intervention procedures. School districts must have a written attendance policy developed and reviewed annually in collaboration with the county attorney in the county of the district’s principal office. Superintendents, principals, teachers, or board members must report suspected violations to the school attendance officer, who must investigate within three days. The bill requires provision of services after twenty days of absence, outlines required collaborative meetings (involving attendance officers, school social workers or administrators, caregivers, and the student when appropriate), and allows referral to the county attorney only after documented interventions have failed and the student has accrued 20+ unexcused absences. Schools must notify families in writing before referral; failure to document required efforts is a defense to prosecution. Exceptions include illness, certain pregnancy/parenting policies, IEP/IFSP/504/McKinney-Vento cases. No funding or appropriations are included. Adds exclusions from "unexcused" absences for: parent/guardian/educational-decisionmaker‑excused illness per Neb. §79‑530; pregnant/parenting students per policy under Neb. §79‑2,151; and students with an IFSP, an IEP under the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (20 U.S.C. 1400 et seq.), Section 504 accommodations (29 U.S.C. 794), state-defined special education (Neb. §79‑1125), or McKinney‑Vento homelessness services (42 U.S.C. 1141 et seq.) when absences relate to those plans/services. Federal programs referenced are administered/overseen by the U.S. Department of Education (including the Office for Civil Rights for Section 504). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1147_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1147_Intro_Copy.docx LB1147 requires the Auditor of Public Accounts to investigate any impoundment of state funds by the Governor or any official or employee of the executive branch and to submit a quarterly report of those investigations to the Nebraska Legislature, with procedural detail to be as prescribed. The bill names the Auditor, the Governor, the executive branch (as the subject of impoundment), and the Legislature (as report recipient). It includes an emergency clause for immediate effectiveness. No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are specified. No underlined (added) text found in this bill. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1148_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1148_Intro_Copy.docx LB1148 establishes statutory parentage rules for children conceived by assisted reproduction. Key provisions: donors are not parents; an individual who consents to assisted reproduction with intent to be a parent is a parent (consent generally must be in a signed record); exceptions allow courts to find consent based on clear-and-convincing evidence or two years of cohabitation and holding out. It sets posthumous parentage conditions (written consent or clear evidence plus embryo/ birth time limits). Parentage disputes are adjudicated in court using best-interest and equitable factors; a child may not have more than two parents. The act excludes births by sexual intercourse, surrogacy agreements, and preserves Nebraska Indian Child Welfare Act rules. No state agencies, appropriations, or funding changes are mentioned. Adds detailed definitions and parentage rules for children conceived by assisted reproduction: who is a parent when an individual consents, required signed consent (with clear-and-convincing-evidence exceptions), posthumous reproduction conditions (consent/evidence plus embryo in utero within 36 months or birth within 45 months), limits to two parents, and factors courts must use to adjudicate competing claims (best interest criteria and considerations for genetic-test challenges). It restricts a spouse’s ability to challenge parentage with time and evidentiary limits. It also states these sections do not apply to children conceived by sexual intercourse, do not recognize surrogacy agreements, and do not supersede the Nebraska Indian Child Welfare Act. Government bodies mentioned: courts (judicial branch) and implicit tribal jurisdiction under the Nebraska Indian Child Welfare Act. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1149_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1149_Intro_Copy.docx LB1149 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §73‑302 to expand reporting requirements for any state agency seeking to contract out services under §73‑301. Agencies must submit to the Director of Administrative Services: the proposed contract; a long‑term actual cost‑savings review; measurable service‑quality goals; an assessment of in‑house alternatives; and disclosure of any contracts the proposed private contractor has with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The bill also retains detailed twelve‑ and sixty‑month cost projection requirements (direct costs, attributable indirect overhead, transitional costs, and additional state performance costs). The original section is repealed. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed by this bill. Adds a new subsection (e) that explicitly covers any contracts a private entity enters into with the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1150_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1150_Intro_Copy.docx Amends §77‑6827 (ImagiNE Nebraska Act) to require applicants to disclose any contracts with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and to bar the director administering the Act from approving incentive applications for taxpayers that have entered into contracts with ICE. The bill retains the $5,000 nonrefundable application fee, which is remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Incentives Fund. Existing procedural provisions — the director’s 90‑day decision period (with tolling for information requests) and the prohibition on new applications after December 31, 2030 — remain in place. Adds a requirement to disclose any contracts between the taxpayer and the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and prohibits the director from approving applications for taxpayers that have such contracts with ICE. No other agencies are mentioned. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1151_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1151_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB1151 treats each shipment into Nebraska by holders of certain shipping licenses as a sale establishing Nebraska tax nexus and requires those licensees to collect applicable taxes and remit sales taxes to the Department of Revenue (excise taxes are remitted monthly to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission). Apart from that remittance requirement, the bill assigns tax reporting, collection, bond, and enforcement duties to the Commission and local bodies and includes no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue. Adds a “regional craft brewery” definition (20,000–200,000 barrels/year) and creates a new regional craft brewery license under the Nebraska Liquor Control Act that: authorizes aggregate production across up to eight physical locations; allows sales to beer wholesalers and retail sales for on- and off‑premises consumption (with other retail licenses required for non‑brewery products); permits obtaining related licenses (annual catering, special designated, entertainment district, promotional farmers market); and allows authorized offsite storage of tax‑paid product with commission approval, location notice, and perpetual inventory (consumption at storage prohibited). The commission may adopt rules. No provisions change Department of Revenue responsibilities, nor do they include any new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB1152_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1152_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Economic Development and assigns it authority to administer the New Taxpayer Recruitment Grant Act. Key department duties: prescribe the grant application form; accept and consider applications in received order and notify approvals within 30 days; approve grants only within available appropriations; disburse grants (50% at award, 50% upon meeting half the household goal) and reaward unspent remainder; receive semiannual program outcome reports; adopt rules and regulations. Fiscal provisions: creates the New Taxpayer Recruitment Grant Cash Fund to be administered by the department to finance grants; fund sources include legislative transfers, gifts, grants, and bequests; fund investments follow existing state investment law. Grant limits: maximum $250,000 per applicant per fiscal year. Summary (Department of Economic Development):\n\n- The Department of Economic Development is defined as the administering agency and must prescribe application forms, consider applications in receipt order, and notify qualifying applicants within 30 days. \n- The department will award grants to finance new taxpayer recruitment program administration and household relocation incentives, subject to available appropriations. \n- Grants are capped at $250,000 per applicant per fiscal year and are paid 50% at award and 50% upon meeting half the program’s household goal; unmet halfway goals suspend the second payment and remaining funds may be reawarded. \n- A New Taxpayer Recruitment Grant Cash Fund is created and administered by the department; it receives legislative transfers and gifts/grants/bequests (including federal) and may be invested by the state investment officer. \n- The department may adopt rules to implement the Act. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB1154_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1154_Intro_Copy.docx LB1154 amends Neb. Rev. 109-2-LB1155_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1155_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue LB1155 tightens confidentiality and limited disclosure of tax-return information and clarifies agency-specific uses of that information. For the Department of Revenue, auditors (Auditor of Public Accounts and Legislative Audit Office) must notify the Tax Commissioner in advance, follow Department confidentiality safeguards, use a secure on-site storage area or secure remote access, keep standardized request records, restrict access to necessary personnel, report on procedures, and return records; the Tax Commissioner may permit other state tax officials to inspect returns only for tax enforcement and must compile school-district income data (including total AGI) with rules to protect taxpayer confidentiality. 109-2-LB1168_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB1168_Intro_Copy.docx LB1168 (2026) amends the Community Development Law to allow redevelopment authorities to issue conduit revenue bonds and to enter into taxpayer agreements that can (a) guarantee or secure bond payments (including shortfalls in pledged real‑estate tax revenues) and (b) create property‑tax‑like liens enforceable under section 77‑203. Authorities may pledge up to 100% of annual excess tax revenues from tax‑increment financing to pay such bonds. Conduit revenue bonds are carved out from the statute treating authority bonds as general obligations and tax‑exempt. The bill affirms obligees’ rights to enforce taxpayer agreements, mortgages, and pledges against authority property, rents, fees, grants, or revenue. Procedural changes affect city bodies, planning commissions, county assessors, county boards of equalization, county clerks/treasurers, the Property Tax Administrator (annual reports to the Legislature), and the Tax Equalization and Review Commission. Notices to county assessors must be filed by July 1 of the effective year. Creates authority power to issue conduit revenue bonds for redevelopment and to pledge up to 100% of annual excess ad valorem (property) tax revenues into an authority special fund solely to pay bond principal, interest, and premiums; any unpledged taxes continue to flow to the respective public bodies. Allows an authority issuing such bonds to enter taxpayer agreements that (a) limit challenges to tax assessments and/or (b) guarantee or otherwise secure bond payments (including covering tax shortfalls) when the taxpayer's property is inside the redevelopment area and taxes are subject to division. Payments under such agreements that create a property tax lien are treated as property taxes under section 77-203. Those liens have parity with property tax liens, take priority over mortgages and other encumbrances, and may be enforced and collected as real property taxes. No specific state agency is named beyond “authority” and “public bodies.” DOCX | PDF

Voided checks must be charged off in county accounting, and the treasurer must credit the proceeds, including any interest, to the county general fund. Voided checks under this provision are removed from owners' intangible personal property and are not subject to the Uniform Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act. The bill authorizes transfers from the Panhandle Improvement Project Cash Fund to the Animal Damage Control Cash Fund at the Legislature’s direction and directs the State Treasurer to transfer any unobligated Panhandle fund balance to the Animal Damage Control Cash Fund on or after July 31, 2026. - Department of Agriculture: The bill expresses the Legislature’s intent to appropriate $26,000 for FY2026‑27 from the Animal Damage Control Cash Fund to the Department of Agriculture for the animal damage control program (per §81‑2,236). 109-2-LB730_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB730_Intro_Copy.docx LB730 requires public governing bodies and state agencies to designate restrooms and locker rooms by sex and restrict use to the designated sex. 109-2-LB731_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB731_Intro_Copy.docx LB731 creates the Gender Transition Malpractice Accountability Act (operative Jan. 1, 2027). Key government-related effects:\n- Waives sovereign immunity for claims arising from recommendation, approval, or provision of gender‑altering procedures, exposing state actors/providers to suit. \n- Amends the limitations framework: a 12‑year statute of repose for actions against providers under the Act and an explicit exemption from the existing §25‑222 professional‑negligence timing. The Let Them Grow Act civil‑action timing is aligned to this 12‑year rule. \n- Requires any health insurance policy that has ever covered a covered individual's gender‑altering procedure to (regardless of enrollment at time of procedure) cover all adverse consequences, annual baseline/follow‑up testing, and any treatment to manage, reverse, reconstruct, or recover from the procedure (see cross‑reference to §44‑3,131). \n- Prohibits contractual waivers of provider liability; allows recovery of actual damages and attorney fees.\n\nNo appropriations, funding changes, or specific state agency budget allocations are included. No state agencies or departments are named or created. Key additions: sovereign immunity is waived so the state can be sued for injuries from recommending/providing gender‑altering procedures; a 12‑year statute of limitations for such claims; providers cannot contractually waive liability; plaintiffs may recover actual damages and attorney’s fees. Providers must give written risk disclosures (and to parents/guardians if under 19). Defines and narrows “gender‑altering” and excludes medically verifiable disorders of sex development, certain acute/necessary surgeries, and treatments for complications. Effective January 1, 2027. Health insurers that currently or previously covered gender‑altering procedures must continue covering all adverse consequences, annual baseline and follow‑up testing, and any management/reversal/reconstructive care, regardless of enrollment at the time of the original procedure. No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB755_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB755_Intro_Copy.docx LB755 (Emergency Service Peer Support Act) authorizes Nebraska "emergency service agencies" — defined to include law enforcement agencies, fire departments, emergency medical services, correctional facilities, hospitals, dispatch centers, rescue services, and other emergency response entities — to establish or approve peer support programs and approve/train peers (who may be current, former, or other approved individuals). Agencies must develop program policies, may discipline peers who violate confidentiality, and may refer employees internally or to programs of other agencies; participation cannot be mandated. Communications in peer support sessions are privileged and exempt from public disclosure under sections 84-712 to 84-712.09, with specified exceptions. The bill provides civil immunity for peers acting in good faith. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Creates the Emergency Service Peer Support Act establishing privileged, confidential peer‑support programs for employees of "emergency service agencies" (defined to include law enforcement agencies, fire departments, emergency medical services, correctional facilities, hospitals, dispatch centers, rescue services, and similar emergency‑response entities). Communications in peer support sessions are inadmissible in civil, criminal, administrative, or arbitration proceedings; peers and program staff cannot be compelled to testify or produce records. Records are exempt from disclosure under sections 84‑712 to 84‑712.09. Exceptions to confidentiality include threats of future suicide/homicide/felonious assault, legally mandated reports (e.g., domestic violence, sexual assault, child/elder abuse), admissions of criminal conduct, or admissions indicating refusal to protect others. Agencies must adopt program policies and discipline peers who violate confidentiality; agencies may cross‑refer employees to other agencies' programs and participation is voluntary. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB756_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB756_Intro_Copy.docx LB756 revises Nebraska tax-exemption procedures for disabled or blind U.S. veterans (service‑connected disability recognized by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) and their surviving spouses for one motor vehicle and for mobile-home property tax exemptions. It requires affected individuals to apply to the county treasurer within specified registration windows; the county treasurer must approve or deny within 20 days, and denials may be appealed to the county board of equalization within 20 days. For organizational vehicle exemptions, the county treasurer recommends status to the county board within 20 days; the board holds a hearing on ten days’ notice, decides within 30 days, and its decision may be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days. The Tax Commissioner promulgates rules. Operative date: January 1, 2027. No funding or appropriation changes. Adds wording to reorganize and clarify who qualifies for the exemption: it inserts a "person:" label and divides the provision into numbered subsections (1) and (2), where (1) covers an individual and (2) covers a surviving spouse of a disabled or blind veteran who would have qualified at the veteran's death and who has not remarried. It also updates an internal cross‑reference (from subdivision (2)(a) to subdivision (1)). No government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned or changed. 109-2-LB757_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB757_Intro_Copy.docx LB757 amends section 77-2704.28 (Neb. Rev. Stat.) to add a targeted sales and use tax exemption under the Nebraska Revenue Act of 1967 for purchases of aircraft to be leased among related entities (parent/subsidiary or brother‑sister companies). Eligibility requires (1) annual gross lease receipts (including related‑party leases) equal at least 7.5% of the aircraft’s net acquisition price (including trade value, excluding third‑party sales commissions) and (2) collection and remittance of sales tax on lease payments. The bill becomes operative October 1, 2026, and repeals the original section. No state agencies are specifically named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the bill. Adds a sales/use tax exemption under the Nebraska Revenue Act of 1967 for purchases of aircraft intended for lease—even when transferred among parent, subsidiary, or sister companies—if (1) annual gross receipts from leasing (including related-party leases) are at least 7.5% of the aircraft’s net acquisition price (counting trade value, excluding third‑party sales commissions) and (2) sales tax is collected and remitted on lease payments. Agencies: references the Nebraska Revenue Act of 1967 (state tax authority/collection). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB758_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB758_Intro_Copy.docx LB758 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §30-2715 to add a statutory process allowing 501(c)(3) charitable beneficiaries to claim nonprobate interests or obtain information by presenting an affidavit to the property holder or any person with relevant information. The affidavit must include the charity's IRS determination letter, a certificate of existence (or equivalent) from its state/country of incorporation, proof of the decedent's death or probate notice, a corporate resolution authorizing the affiant, and a completed IRS Form W-9. The bill references the Internal Revenue Service and federal Internal Revenue Code requirements and invokes notarization. Upon receipt of a compliant affidavit the holder must pay, deliver, or transfer the property (or provide information); the bill also creates an enforcement right of action. No state agency budgetary changes, appropriations, or funding allocations are included. Adds a procedure allowing 501(c)(3) charities to claim a decedent's property by submitting an affidavit plus specified documents. Government entities referenced: the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) — charities must provide their IRS tax‑exempt determination letter and a completed IRS Form W‑9; the Internal Revenue Code is cited. It also references state/country incorporation records (e.g., a Secretary of State certificate of existence), death records or probate notices (vital records offices/courts), and notarization by a notary public. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB761_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB761_Intro_Copy.docx LB761 directs the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment to restructure fee collection and fund flows and creates a new dedicated fund.\n\nKey agency actions and fiscal changes:\n- Department to collect increased water‑well registration fees ($200 per well/series/groups as specified) and hazardous‑waste and NPDES/pretreatment permit fees.\n- Integrated Solid Waste Management Cash Fund is amended to receive hazardous‑waste fees (per 81‑1505(13)(c)) and forfeited financial‑assurance funds; fees must be used to implement hazardous‑waste rules. Transfers from that fund to the General Fund may be made by the Legislature. Money in the fund may be invested by the state investment officer under applicable state investment laws. Beginning July 1, 2027, the department may charge application and annual fees for NPDES and pretreatment permits (capped at actual administrative costs or necessary reimbursement); permits under §54-2428 are exempt. 109-2-LB765_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB765_Intro_Copy.docx LB765 amends school bond voting and joint-entity bond procedures. For Nebraska school districts (section 10-702) it requires that bond questions be submitted to district electors, receive votes from at least 50.1% of qualified electors, and obtain a majority of votes cast; retains filing deadlines with county clerks or election commissioners (March 1 for primary, September 1 for general), special‑election procedures, 20‑day publication notice, canvass/certification responsibilities, and a six‑month resubmission bar after defeat. For joint entities including a Nebraska school district or educational service unit (section 13-809) bonds require similar per-district approval, a 50‑day election notice, and Election Act conduct; Public Facilities Construction and Finance Act voting rules remain. The bill reiterates prohibitions on using public funds or paid employee time to advocate for bond campaigns and bans campaign materials on school/ESU property. No appropriations or funding changes are made. Adds prohibitions applying to school districts, educational service units (ESUs), and joint entities that include them: public funds — explicitly including building funds, cash funds, and discretionary funds — may not be used to establish, conduct, underwrite, promote, subsidize, or otherwise support or advocate for campaigns in school district or joint-entity bond elections. Privately raised funds (e.g., concessions, booster clubs, PTOs) are exempt. No district or ESU employee may use paid work time to advocate for such bond campaigns, though employees may provide neutral factual information (subject, amount, election date). Campaign materials advocating for a bond may not be posted or distributed on any facility, grounds, or vehicles associated with a district or ESU; generic informational materials are allowed. No new appropriations or budget allocations are created—these are restrictions on use of existing public funds. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB766_Intro Withdrawn Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB766_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB766 locates the Charitable Gaming Division within the Department of Revenue and requires annual electronic reports to the Governor, Legislature, Auditor, and Attorney General on tax revenue received, expenses, and related activities. It creates the Charitable Gaming Operations Fund: 40% of taxes collected under specified sections are made available to the Charitable Gaming Division for administration/enforcement and to the State Racing and Gaming Commission to provide administrative support to the Nebraska Commission on Problem Gambling; the remaining 60% is transferred to the General Fund. The bill directs quarterly transfers of $100,000 from the Charitable Gaming Operations Fund to the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund through June 30, 2026, and permits remaining fund balances to be transferred to the General Fund and the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund per legislative direction. It authorizes Tax Commissioner investigators for enforcement, requires authorized gaming operators to remit winnings setoff deductions to the Department of Revenue (per section 9-1306), and allocates certain taxes and fees to the Operations Fund for division use. No provisions explicitly amend the Department of Revenue’s duties, budget, or appropriations.\n\nKey additions affecting funding flows:\n- Licensees must remit monies deducted (per §2-1207) to the official breed registrars for distribution; registrars must annually spend at least 80% of those deductions on purse supplements and breeder/stallion awards.\n- Failure to register an eligible Nebraska-bred horse within 90 days triggers an administrative fee up to $1,000 payable to the applicable official registrar; fees are earmarked to cover the registrar’s administrative costs.\n- Adds a requirement for the Racing and Gaming Commission to consult quarterhorse breeders before approving certain interstate simulcasts and to collaborate with the Nebraska Commission on Problem Gambling regarding annual gaming tax proceeds (citing §§9-1204, 9-1006), but it does not specify changes to Revenue Department allocations. 109-2-LB768_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB768_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development - The Department of Economic Development (DED) will administer the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (AHTF) as part of its housing affordability strategy. 109-2-LB770_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB770_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB770 amends distribution of revenue received from the Department of Revenue (per §77-6203). After the county treasurer receives those funds, the treasurer may retain 1% for collection costs; the remainder is distributed with 5% to the community college area where the renewable energy facility is located and the balance allocated among eligible local taxing entities by a levy-weighted formula. 109-2-LB771_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB771_Intro_Copy.docx LB771 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §75-327 governing transportation network companies (TNCs). It requires TNCs to file and keep current the rates they use (including dynamic pricing) with the commission and to charge consistent rates; otherwise TNCs remain largely exempt from rate regulation. When using dynamic pricing, TNC apps must give a clear visible notice, require passenger confirmation, and provide a fare estimator. The Governor may permit or prohibit dynamic pricing in any political subdivision named in a state of emergency proclamation or by executive order; prohibition is limited to the time specified. The bill also maintains limits that rides be prearranged and drivers work no more than 12 hours per 24-hour period, repealing the original section. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Gives the Governor discretion to allow or prohibit "dynamic pricing" in any political subdivision named in a gubernatorial state-of-emergency proclamation; any prohibition must be issued in the proclamation or by executive order and is limited to the time period the Governor specifies. Outside declared emergency areas, dynamic pricing is generally permitted unless another provision restricts it. No other agencies or departments are mentioned and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB777_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB777_Intro_Copy.docx LB777 amends §68-908, assigning the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) additional eligibility and expanded reporting duties as administrator of the Medical Assistance (Medicaid) program. DHHS must continue rulemaking, contracts, waivers/managed care (including under the Nebraska Behavioral Health Services Act), confidentiality, and retroactive coverage. The bill requires an annual report to the Governor and Legislature (by Dec. 1) with detailed program metrics and breakdowns by eligibility category, local public health district, and race/ethnicity; links to redacted fair hearing decisions; and expanded disclosures on community engagement requirements, concurrent enrollment identification, and cost‑sharing amounts/payment sources. It also requires DHHS to list external vendors used to verify compliance or identify concurrent enrollees, including links to each vendor contract. No appropriations or funding changes are provided. The original section is repealed. Requires "the department" administering medical assistance to: provide the maximum retroactive coverage permitted by federal law; report detailed status of proposed/implemented community engagement requirements (implementation plan, authority/effective date, affected recipients; counts of denials, verification failures, additional-information requests, exemptions and types, approvals by compliance type, re‑enrollments within 90 days and 12 months); list data sources used to verify compliance and identify external vendors the state contracts to assess compliance, with links to each contract. Also requires reporting on concurrent‑enrollment cases and vendors used to detect them (with contract links) and re‑enrollment rates after termination (90 days and 12 months). Finally, requires a description of cost sharing (premiums, copays, deductibles), their amounts, and the payment source for collected cost sharing. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB779_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB779_Intro_Copy.docx LB779 restricts medical-debt collection practices by entities defined in statute: health care facilities (per Neb. Rev. Stat. §71-413) and collection agencies (per §45-602). It bars charging interest or late fees on medical debt until 90 days after the final invoice due date and caps such interest/fees at 3% per year. It defines "medical debt" as obligations arising from receipt of health care services and prohibits placing liens on or foreclosing an individual's primary residence to collect medical debt. The bill contains no provisions for state agency implementation, funding changes, appropriations, or budget allocations. Adds limits on medical debt collection: health care facilities (per §71-413) and collection agencies (per §45-602) cannot charge interest or late fees on medical debt until 90 days after the final invoice due date, and such interest/fees are capped at 3% annually. Defines medical debt as obligations from receipt of health care services. Also prohibits liens or foreclosures on an individual’s primary residence to collect medical debt. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB780_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB780_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Insurance Section 3 expressly authorizes the Nebraska Department of Insurance to "adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to carry out sections 1 to 3 of this act." 109-2-LB782_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB782_Intro_Copy.docx Bill LB782 amends §9-648 of the Nebraska County and City Lottery Act to set the tax on gross lottery proceeds at one percent. Counties, cities, or villages conducting lotteries must submit the tax quarterly to "the department" on department-provided forms and remit payment within 30 days of quarter close. The department is directed to remit collected taxes to the State Treasurer for credit to the Charitable Gaming Operations Fund. Tax deficiencies accrue interest and penalties as provided under the Nebraska Revenue Act of 1967. The bill repeals the original §9-648, states an operative date of July 1, 2026, and declares an emergency so it takes effect when passed and approved. The only added text is the single word "one." It does not reference any government agencies or departments and makes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB783_Intro E and R Initial Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB783_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB783 amends section 76‑902 (documentary stamp tax exemptions). It adds assignments under the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act to the exemption list and requires, for transfers into a trust claiming an exemption, that the register of deeds be presented a signed certification and that supporting evidence be maintained and made available for inspection by the Department of Revenue. The bill contains no provisions altering funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue. For the Department of Revenue: the added Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act requires assignees to comply with Internal Revenue Service and state and local taxing authorities and treats post‑assignment taxes incurred by the assignee as administrative expenses payable from the assignment estate. Assignees must preserve records and provide information reasonably necessary to administer tax matters and may have to collect, account for, or turn over tax‑related amounts. The text contains no new appropriations, funding provisions, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB784_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB784_Intro_Copy.docx LB784 amends sheriff residency, certification, and continuing-education requirements and clarifies multi-county appointments. Key agencies and changes:\n- Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice: must issue law enforcement certificates/diplomas to sheriff candidates/appointees and award completion certificates for the Sheriff's Certification Course.\n- Nebraska Law Enforcement Training Center: conducts the Sheriff's Certification Course; its director must certify issuance of certificates for filing.\n- Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council: may waive certification or accept equivalent training.\n- County boards: may appoint a qualified Nebraska law enforcement officer from any county to fill a sheriff vacancy and contract for compensation; such appointees may serve multiple counties under that appointment.\n- Law enforcement agencies: annual continuing education requirements specified in amended 81-1414.07 (24 hours/year; specified topics; triennial requirements).\nPenalties: fines equal to a sheriff’s monthly salary per month of training noncompliance. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Sections 4 and 7 operative Jan 1, 2027. Adds residency and training requirements for county law enforcement. Key points:\n- Sheriff residency: In counties without a metropolitan/primary/first-class city, a candidate need not reside in the county when filing, but must reside in that county or an adjoining county while in office.\n- Training: Law enforcement officers (except noncertified conditional officers) must complete 24 hours of continuing education annually. At least once every three years that training must include refresher courses on de‑escalation, mental‑health and substance‑abuse issues; a minimum of two hours of anti‑bias/implicit‑bias training; officer wellness training; and a review of vehicular pursuit policies. Those hours count toward other required training totals.\n- No agencies/departments are newly created or renamed, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB785_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB785_Intro_Copy.docx LB785 adds a new Class IV felony prohibiting obtaining, possessing, duplicating, transferring, or using a key or lock for any postal-service mail receptacle with intent to defraud or deprive another. "Postal service" is defined to include the United States Postal Service, its contractors, and commercial couriers. The bill incorporates the new offense into existing financial-transaction and covered-offense provisions, enabling district courts and prosecuting authorities to seek forfeiture. Forfeited money, securities, and negotiable instruments from financial transaction offenses are to be credited to the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund. Law enforcement/seizing agencies may retain, use, sell, or destroy forfeited property per statutory procedures. Adds a definition of “postal service” to include the United States Postal Service, USPS contractors, and any commercial courier that delivers mail. Creates a new criminal offense—unlawful conduct involving a mail receptacle key or lock—covering knowingly obtaining, possessing, duplicating, transferring, or using a key or lock adopted by a postal service for any mail box or authorized receptacle with intent to defraud or deprive another. Violation is classified as a Class IV felony. No government funding, appropriations, or budgetary changes are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB786_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB786_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military Department - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): directs the DMV to design and issue Military Honor Plates, verify applicant eligibility by consulting the Department of Veterans' Affairs registry (section 80-414), provide application forms via county treasurers, and remit collected fees to the State Treasurer for credit as specified. DMV may charge postage/handling for mailed plates and receives credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund for certain fees (postage/handling, a $3 transfer fee, and 25% of the $40 personalized-plate fee).\n\n- Department of Veterans' Affairs (DVA): DMV eligibility verification is tied to the DVA registry; applicants may qualify by registering with the DVA pursuant to section 80-414.\n\n- Military Department: creates the Military Department Aid Fund, administered by the Adjutant General, funded by gifts/grants/legislative transfers and monies credited under section 60-3,122.04 (including 75% of the $40 personalized-plate fee). The fund is investable by the state investment officer; interest and gains credit to the fund. The Adjutant General may award nonreimbursable grants to needy Military Department uniformed service members and must adopt qualifying rules by January 1, 2027. If plate manufacturing costs exceed statutory plate fees, the excess is credited first to the Highway Trust Fund before the designated recipients. - Department of Motor Vehicles: directed to create license-plate designs honoring each armed force and persons who have served. Fees for specific plates are allocated to designated recipients.\n\n- Department of Veterans' Affairs: license-plate fee revenue for certain plates is designated to the Nebraska Veteran Cemetery System Operation Fund.\n\n- Military Department: creates the Military Department Aid Fund, administered by the Adjutant General. Fund sources include gifts, grants, bequests, public/private money, amounts credited under section 60-3,122.04, and legislative transfers. The state investment officer may invest available balances; interest and gains return to the fund. Uses are limited to this statute; the Adjutant General may award non‑repayable grants to Military Department members under rules to be adopted by Jan 1, 2027, which must limit eligibility to needy uniformed service members. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB787_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB787_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Labor, Department of Veterans' Affairs LB787 amends membership and reporting provisions for the Commission on Military and Veteran Affairs. 109-2-LB788_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB788_Intro_Copy.docx LB788 amends §84-222 to designate the Nebraska State Patrol as administrator of the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund (previously administered by another entity). The Patrol will prescribe application form/manner, determine qualifying losses and reimbursement amounts, and distribute available funds pro rata if claims exceed resources. The fund consists of assets forfeited from financial transaction offenses (per §28-1601) and any investable money is to be managed by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Forfeited funds remain in the fund for 36 months (or until resolution of applications filed in that period); thereafter remaining amounts are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution. The bill repeals the original section. The added text consists solely of repeated references to the Nebraska State Patrol (four instances). No other agencies, funding changes, appropriations, or budget allocations are included or altered in the provided insertion. DOCX | PDF

R. 27-804 to clarify who is "unavailable" as a witness and to add an explicit forfeiture-by-wrongdoing exception: a statement is admissible against a party who wrongfully caused or acquiesced in causing the declarant's unavailability with the intent to prevent testimony. 109-2-LB790_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB790_Intro_Copy.docx LB790 amends §83-1,119 (Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act). Key agencies/departments and actions:\n\n- Department (the correctional department referenced in statute): must develop a matrix of rewards, graduated administrative sanctions, and custodial sanctions; may use county jails that contract with the department as contract facilities. A custodial sanction of up to 30 days in a correctional or contract facility is designated the most severe response short of revocation.\n- Parole officers: may impose administrative sanctions for technical or substance-abuse violations (with parolee acknowledgement) or submit reports to the Board of Parole.\n- Board of Parole: receives reports, may dismiss charges, impose custodial sanctions (up to 30 days), issue warrants, and — for substance-abuse violations — may revoke parole under the Act; must adopt rules to implement the section.\n\nNo changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds procedures when a parole officer suspects a parolee of a substance-abuse violation but no flight or public-safety risk: the parole officer must either (a) impose administrative sanctions scaled to risk/severity if the parolee signs written acknowledgment and agrees to the sanction (if the parolee refuses, the officer must follow option (b)), or (b) submit a written report to the Board of Parole. The Board of Parole may dismiss, determine a violation, impose up to 30 days custodial sanction in a correctional or contract facility, revoke parole under the Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act, or issue an arrest warrant. Agencies/departments: parole officers, Board of Parole, correctional/contract facilities; references the Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB791_Intro Withdrawn Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB791_Intro_Copy.docx LB791 amends the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act to impose a contribution limit for candidates and ballot question committees. Beginning January 1, 2027, no person may contribute more than $3,500 in total to a candidate or ballot question committee during an election period; committees must refund excess contributions within ten days and report the contributor name, address, amount received, receipt date, and return date. A candidate’s personal funds are exempt. Beginning January 1, 2029, and biennially thereafter, the limit is adjusted by the cumulative change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers published by the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics, rounded to the nearest $100. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are made or changed by this bill. Establishes a $3,500 per-person contribution cap to any candidate or ballot question committee per election period effective Jan. 1, 2027. Committees must refund excess contributions within 10 days and report them on subsequent campaign statements (name, address, amount, date received, date returned). A candidate’s own personal funds are exempt. "Election period" is defined as the calendar year of the election. Beginning Jan. 1, 2029, the limit is adjusted every two years for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers published by the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics, rounded to the nearest $100. No agencies other than the BLS are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB794_Intro Select File Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB794_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Agriculture LB794 amends statutes affecting the Department of Agriculture by:\n\n- Specifying department powers and duties: encourage and promote agriculture; promote production/distribution methods; collect and publish agricultural statistics (cooperate with federal gov.); publish/distribute Weeds of the Great Plains and remit proceeds to the State Treasurer; investigate contagious animal diseases; adopt and enforce rules; employ special investigators; perform laboratory testing per section 81-2,293; and enforce the Foreign-owned Real Estate National Security Act.\n- Requiring the Department to submit electronically to the Legislature, before January 1, 2027, the Healthy Soils Task Force’s comprehensive action plan, findings/recommendations, agendas, minutes, and submitted documents.\n- Addressing funding: receipts under fertilizer/liming laws are credited to the Fertilizers and Soil Conditioners Administrative Fund for department administration (with transfers to the General Fund permitted by the Legislature). Requires the Department of Agriculture to electronically submit to the Clerk of the Legislature by January 1, 2027, all materials the department received from the Healthy Soils Task Force (created under Laws 2019, LB243, §2), specifically: the comprehensive action plan filed under former §2‑404 (as of Jan 1, 2021); the findings and recommendations reported under that same former section; and agendas, meeting minutes, and any other documents the task force submitted to the department. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are added or changed. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB795_Intro E and R Initial Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB795_Intro_Copy.docx LB795 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28‑405 (Rev. Stat. Supp., 2025) and repeals the prior section to update Nebraska’s controlled‑substances schedules. 109-2-LB796_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB796_Intro_Copy.docx LB796 amends §38‑2850 of the Pharmacy Practice Act to revise which activities and persons are excluded from the statutory practice of pharmacy.
