109-2-LB797_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB797_Intro_Copy.docx LB797 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§16-321 and 17-568.01 governing cities of the first class, cities of the second class, and villages. It raises the municipal competitive-bidding/approval thresholds so that contracts for enlargements or general improvements costing over $90,000 require prior approval and advertised bids. It also updates municipal electric utility bid-waiver tiers (waivers allowed up to $90,000 and higher graduated thresholds up to $1,000,000 depending on gross annual retail sales). The bill preserves emergency waiver authority and authorizes boards of public works to use engineering staff or hire consultants. Original sections are repealed. No state appropriations or funding allocations are included. Added language sets dollar ceilings for municipal electric utilities based on gross annual retail sales: (e) up to $500,000 where revenue exceeds $20 million; (f) up to $750,000 where revenue exceeds $30 million; and (g) up to $1,000,000 where revenue exceeds $75 million. No state agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to appropriations or budgetary allocations in the added text. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB798_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB798_Intro_Copy.docx LB798 amends municipal election and planning commission statutes.\n\nKey government entities referenced:\n- Mayors and city council members; chairperson and members of village boards of trustees — retain appointment/removal authority for planning commissions and alternates (appointments require council/board majority approval).\n- Planning commissions (cities of first class, second class, villages) — may now be established with three, five, seven, or nine regular members (city council or village board sets size by ordinance); alternate member provisions remain.\n- County clerks and election commissioners — responsible for petition verification and placing election questions on ballots.\n- Filing officers and governing bodies — must accept candidate filings consistent with approved at-large/ward arrangements; districts must be drawn by Oct. 1 following approval or follow statutory fallback procedures.\n- Counties, school districts, community redevelopment authorities, and citizen advisory review committees are referenced regarding eligibility and limits on holding simultaneous offices.\n\nFiscal impact: no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. Adds a provision allowing cities of the second class (except those with commissioner or city manager government) that elect council members by ward to adopt a mixed ward/at-large system by ordinance (majority vote) or voter petition at a general election. Requires at least two at-large members and no more than half the council to be at-large. Establishes staggered initial term lengths for at-large members based on how many are elected (two‑ or four‑year initial terms as specified); thereafter at-large terms are four years. Prohibits candidates from filing both as at-large and by ward. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB799_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB799_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services LB799 assigns reporting and compilation duties to the materiel division of the Department of Administrative Services (DAS). The division (defined as DAS’s materiel division) will receive annual service-contract reports from cities, counties, and state agencies, compile them, and electronically submit a comprehensive report to the Governor, Clerk of the Legislature, and Urban Affairs Committee by September 1 each year. The division must also publish the report on the DAS website. For enforcement, the division will notify any noncompliant city or county, after which the State Treasurer must suspend all state-aid distributions to that jurisdiction until the required report is submitted; suspended distributions are restored once the report is filed. The bill includes no direct appropriations to DAS. Creates the "Service Contract Reporting Act" and assigns the materiel division of the Department of Administrative Services (DAS) these duties: receive annual service-contract reports from cities, counties, and state agencies (due Aug. 1); compile and electronically submit a comprehensive statewide report to the Governor, Clerk of the Legislature, and Urban Affairs Committee (due Sept. 1); and post the report on DAS’s website. DAS must notify noncompliant cities/counties; upon such notice the State Treasurer is directed to suspend state-aid distributions to that jurisdiction until the report is filed (suspended funds are restored after filing). No explicit appropriations or new DAS funding or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB800_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB800_Intro_Copy.docx LB800 updates Nebraska's state building and energy code references to the 2024 editions and reallocates responsibilities among state and local authorities. Key agency actions:\n\n- Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE)/Director: adopts the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code as the Nebraska Energy Code; reviews plans/specifications for buildings constructed with state funds (unless a local jurisdiction already reviewed them); must receive verification from the funded agency that constructed buildings comply; may adopt alternative equivalent standards by rule.\n- Department of Administrative Services (State Building Administrator): in consultation with DWEE, may specify newer IECC editions, additional efficiency or renewable requirements, and grant waivers based on life‑cycle cost analyses; agencies seeking waivers must provide the analyses.\n- Local governments: must adopt or conform to the state building code, notify DWEE within 30 days if deleting specified chapters, and update codes within two years of state updates.\n- Section 72‑806: enforcement provisions of Chapter 1 of the 2024 IECC do not apply to buildings under section 72‑804.\n\nNo direct appropriations or budget allocations are included. Adds language incorporating the 2024 editions of model codes—specifically references to Chapter 13 of the 2024 International Building Code and Chapter 11 of the 2024 International Residential Code—and ties their applicability to the act’s effective date. No state or local agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB801_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB801_Intro_Copy.docx LB801 updates Nebraska’s state building code (amending §71-6403) and local adoption rules (§71-6406). It adopts by reference specified components of current model codes, notably chapter 13 of the 2024 International Building Code and chapter 11 of the 2024 International Residential Code, along with portions of the 2018 IBC, the 2018 International Existing Building Code (except §809), and the 2018 Uniform Plumbing Code. 109-2-LB803_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB803_Intro_Copy.docx LB803 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-1229 to clarify filing requirements for tangible personal property. Forms for listing taxable tangible personal property must be prescribed by the Tax Commissioner, made available by county assessors, signed, and filed with the county assessor by May 1 annually. Persons seeking personal property exemptions under §77-4105, the Nebraska Advantage Act, or the ImagiNE Nebraska Act must annually file copies of the required exemption forms with the county assessor in each county where the exemption is requested by May 1; failure to timely file forfeits the exemption for that tax year. Taxpayers with exempt filings and taxable property must still list and value that property per subsection (1). The bill repeals the original section. No appropriations or funding changes are included. The added text consists solely of the two-word phrase "All persons." It does not mention any government agencies or departments and contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. (Taken alone, it appears to broaden applicability to “all persons,” but no fiscal or agency impacts are specified.) DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB804_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB804_Intro_Copy.docx LB804 establishes confidentiality and privilege for peer support counseling provided to personnel of law enforcement agencies (per §81‑1401), emergency services providers (public employers of firefighters, dispatchers, EMS), and the Nebraska National Guard. It defines peer support specialists, peer support teams, and employee assistance programs, makes communications in peer support sessions nonpublic and inadmissible in judicial, administrative, arbitration, or discovery proceedings, and preserves confidentiality among specialists and EAP staff. Exceptions include threats of suicide or criminal acts, mandated reports of abuse/neglect, admissions of criminal conduct, and disclosures with participant or estate consent. The bill also preserves admissibility of information otherwise obtained in the course of employment and allows EAP‑to‑employer fitness‑for‑duty communications. 109-2-LB859_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB859_Intro_Copy.docx LB859 creates and integrates a new county conflict counsel role across Nebraska statutes. Counties may employ or contract for county conflict counsel and must notify presiding district, county, and juvenile court judges, child support referees, and the district court clerk/mental health board upon hiring. District, county, and juvenile courts, and mental health boards are directed to appoint county conflict counsel to represent indigent clients when the public defender is unavailable, except for conflicts or other good cause. In counties over 170,000, county conflict counsel must serve full time and may not privately practice. County conflict counsel must provide representation like the public defender and may only be paid county compensation. County boards are required to allow payment of fees and expenses as fixed by courts; no new statewide appropriations are specified. The Commission on Public Advocacy and Supreme Court rulemaking references are updated accordingly. Adds a definition and duties for “county conflict counsel” — attorneys employed by or under contract with a county to represent indigent clients when the public defender has a conflict or other good cause prevents representation. Counties with a public defender may hire one or more conflict counsel; when first hired the county board must notify: presiding judges of the county and district courts, presiding juvenile court judges, child support referees, and the district court clerk (for the local mental health board). Conflict counsel must provide the same indigent-defense services as the public defender, may not solicit private fees (only county compensation), and in counties over 170,000 must serve full time and not engage in private practice. No new appropriations or statewide funding changes are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB860_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB860_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to establish, by January 1, 2027, a program providing behavioral health services to individuals under 21 with complex, multisystem needs. The department must ensure family-centered care management, determine behavioral health regions for care coordination, and may procure a single statewide managed care plan and/or have a managed care organization perform administrative care coordination, utilization management, and quality improvement. The department is authorized to adopt implementing rules and to seek CMS approvals (state plan amendment, waiver, or other federal authorization) to obtain medical-assistance reimbursement. No funding, appropriation, or specific budget allocations are included. DHHS must establish by Jan 1, 2027 a program serving individuals under 21 with complex, multisystem behavioral health needs to support families and avoid institutionalization/out‑of‑home placement. DHHS will ensure individualized care management and provide services including mobile response/stabilization, intensive home‑based treatment, inpatient/outpatient care, psychiatric residential treatment, substance use disorder and psychiatric care, and developmental disability services. Care coordination will run through behavioral health regions; DHHS may procure a single statewide managed care plan to build provider networks and ensure a full continuum of services. DHHS or an MCO may handle administrative care coordination, utilization management, and quality improvement. DHHS may promulgate rules and must seek any needed CMS approvals (state plan amendment/waiver) to obtain Medicaid reimbursement. No specific funding, appropriation, or budget allocation is stated. 109-2-LB878_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB878_Intro_Copy.docx LB878 requires the State of Nebraska (state agencies and other state employers) to provide paid maternity leave to eligible state employees. Intermittent use allowed only by mutual written agreement or medical certification. Employees must provide 30 days’ notice when practicable. Employers must reinstate employees to the same or equivalent position and may not pay out unused maternity leave at termination. Retaliation against employees for using leave is prohibited. Adds a paid maternity leave entitlement for "state" employees: six weeks for full‑time employees (pro‑rated for part‑time), usable within six months of birth/adoption and generally non‑intermittent except by mutual written agreement or medical necessity for the child. Defines “maternity leave eligible employee,” “state employee,” and “retaliatory action” (e.g., dismissal, pay reduction, failure to promote). Requires 30 days' notice when practicable, prohibits charging this leave to sick/vacation/other leave, bars payout of unused maternity leave at termination, and guarantees return to the same or equivalent position. Fee rate caps and minimum inspection fees are specified. - Requires the State Treasurer to transfer all funds in the Nebraska Poultry and Egg Development, Utilization, and Marketing Fund to the Nebraska Agricultural Products Marketing Cash Fund by December 31, 2026; that transfer provision terminates January 1, 2027. \n- Adds/clarifies regulation of "beneficial substances" (including a defined term for "microorganism") under the Department of Agriculture, requiring product registration with the department, a $50 fee per product, and department approval. \n- Requires labeling details the department will enforce: nutrient guarantees for commercial fertilizers and expiration date/storage conditions for products claiming microorganisms. \n- References a Fertilizers and Beneficial Substances Administrative Fund to support departmental plant‑health program administration (no new appropriation amounts beyond the specified transfer and $50 fee). DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB949_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB949_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB949 (summary of provisions referencing the Department of Health and Human Services)\n\n- The bill defines “department” as the Department of Health and Human Services (71-2454; 81-6,124). \n- Hospital Quality Assurance and Access Assessment Fund (68-2106): directs the department to use the fund to enhance hospital rates; requires reimbursement to the General Fund of the first quarterly payment annually; authorizes an administrative fee to the department equal to 3% of the assessment (capped at $15 million/year); allocates 0.5% (capped $2.5 million/year) to the Nebraska Center for Nursing Board and 3.5% (capped $17.5 million/year) for nonhospital provider rates, continuous eligibility for children, or the designated health information exchange. \n- Health Information Technology Board: one board member must be a representative of the Department of Health and Human Services; several clinician appointees must be in good standing with the department. \n- The department may contract with a vendor to administer the board and PDMP and may use state funds, grants, or gifts to implement technology. The added text appears to be a definition/clarification of "vendor," referencing statute 81-6,124 and vendors under the State Procurement Act. It does not mention the Department of Health and Human Services and includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for that agency. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB950_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB950_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB950 amends the Population Health Information Act to require that several Health Information Technology Board appointees (physicians, pharmacist, dentist, nurse practitioner, veterinarian) be in active practice and “in good standing with the Department of Health and Human Services.” It also designates two board seats as representatives of the Department of Health and Human Services, including one specifically from the Division of Medicaid and Long-Term Care. The bill contains no explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department. Added provisions require health care providers to use only approved uniform prior authorization forms and, within 90 days after notice, to submit prior authorization requests via the approved API or other electronic methodology; utilization review agents must accept/process those forms and may grant extensions for good cause. The Department of Health and Human Services is explicitly given one representative (from its Division of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care) among the designated rule‑making members and is included in promulgation of rules under the Population Health Information Act. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB951_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB951_Intro_Copy.docx LB951 requires Nebraska municipalities to incorporate their extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction (ETJ) into municipal governing-board districts and to treat ETJ residents as municipal electors. Key government actors and changes:\n\n- Election commissioner: divides metro-class cities into seven council districts; census data (U.S. Dept. of Commerce, Bureau of the Census) governs population equality for districts.\n- City councils: apply zoning, building, and subdivision rules in ETJ; responsible for redrawing council districts.\n- City planning commission, city planning director, and public works and utilities department: approve subdivision plats and certify required improvements; register of deeds may not record plats without approval.\n- County boards: receive 30-day notice of proposed ETJ zoning changes (exceptions for large counties or joint planning bodies) and may comment.\n- Board of adjustment: may exempt qualifying farm buildings.\n- Section 32-553: cities/villages electing by district must redraw districts to include ETJ by January 1, 2027; governing boards draw boundaries.\n\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds provisions requiring cities and villages to include their extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction (ETJ) within districting and voter rolls. Specifically:\n- When a metropolitan-class city redraws council districts, its seven districts must include the ETJ.\n- Electors living in the ETJ are deemed electors of the city/village for metropolitan, primary, first-class (in areas), second-class cities, and villages as specified.\n- Any city or village that elects by district must redraw boundaries to include the ETJ by January 1, 2027, and must include the ETJ in future redistricting.\n\nNo state agencies or departments are newly created or mentioned; no funding or appropriations changes. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB952_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB952_Intro_Copy.docx LB952 (2026) restructures court-related funds and statutory sections.\n\n- Creates the Supreme Court Operations Cash Fund, administered by the State Court Administrator, to support court and probation programs. The fund will accept fees, grants, donations, gifts, and payments from political subdivisions and may be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.\n\n- Amends the appellate library statute to (nominally) create a Supreme Court Reports Cash Fund but immediately terminates it on the act's operative date and directs the State Treasurer to transfer any balance to the General Fund.\n\n- Clarifies the Commission on Public Advocacy Operations Cash Fund funding source (receipts under §33-156) and investment authority; the Legislature intends the commission be funded solely from that fund.\n\n- Terminates and repeals the Court Appointed Special Advocate Fund and other specified sections, with remaining balances transferred to the General Fund.\n\n- Emergency clause makes the act effective on enactment (operative date cited July 1, 2026). Creates the "Supreme Court Operations Cash Fund," to be administered by the State Court Administrator for court and probation programs that enhance justice administration and community safety. The fund is financed by fees, grants, donations, gifts, and payments from contracts with political subdivisions. Funds available for investment are to be managed by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The State Treasurer must transfer any balance to the General Fund when the fund terminates on the act’s operative date. The section itself terminates on January 1, 2027. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB953_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB953_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development The bill directs the Department of Economic Development to use the Site and Building Development Fund to finance loans, grants, subsidies, credit enhancements and other assistance, and to cover department administrative expenses as appropriated by the Legislature. The department shall use the fund subaccount to provide financial assistance to inland port authorities. Recipients must provide matching funds in amounts determined by the Department, at least equal to 100% of assistance. The Director of Economic Development must receive a U.S. Strategic Command letter of support and proof of $20 million in private/other funds (with Director certification to the budget administrator) before expending funds for that project. The Director must also receive specified DoD/contractor or association/mayoral documentation before approving certain grants (including golf-facility requirements and limits). Adds a new grant program administered by the Department of Economic Development for political subdivisions and nationally and state accredited golf associations to build golf facilities and related infrastructure, limited to sites inside a city of the metropolitan class. Prior to approval, applicants must submit to the Director of Economic Development: documentation of facility programming for veterans and for youth; letters of support from a nationally accredited golf association, a state accredited golf association, and the mayor of the host metropolitan-class city; and proof of funding equal to at least 8% of total construction costs. Grants are capped at 20% of total construction costs. No direct appropriations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB954_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB954_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue LB954 amends section 77-5701 of the Nebraska Advantage Act to require the Department of Revenue to recalculate a taxpayer’s base-year employees for tier 6 project agreements when the taxpayer sells part of the business operations to an entity outside the taxpayer’s unitary group. The recalculation subtracts the equivalent employees at the sold operations from the base-year employee count on the last Form 312N filed before the sale. The recalculation does not apply if the sold operations cease within 24 months or if the sale’s primary purpose was to close a location. Credits or incentives generated before the sale are not recalculated. The provision applies to agreements entered after December 31, 2016. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Requires the Department of Revenue to recalculate a taxpayer’s base‑year employees for tier 6 project agreements when the taxpayer sells part of the business and the sold operations continue under an entity outside the taxpayer’s unitary group. The recalculation subtracts the equivalent employees at the sold operations from the base‑year employee count on the last Form 312N filed before the sale. Exceptions: the rule does not apply if the sold operations cease within 24 months of sale or if the sale’s primary purpose was to close a location. Pre‑sale credits/incentives are not recalculated. Applies to agreements entered after Dec. 31, 2016. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are changed. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB955_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB955_Intro_Copy.docx LB955 amends the Pharmacy Practice Act (section 38-2867.03, R.S. Cumulative Supplement, 2024) to permit a physician assistant who prescribes under a collaborative agreement to enter into a practice agreement with a pharmacist. It also clarifies that a pharmacist intern may participate in such a practice agreement if supervised by a pharmacist who is a party to the agreement. The bill repeals the original section. No state agencies or departments are explicitly named in the text, and no funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. No underlined (added) text found in this bill. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB956_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB956_Intro_Copy.docx LB956 requires Nebraska public postsecondary institutions to collect and report specified employee compensation data and assigns implementation and reporting duties to the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education. The bill defines relevant terms, directs institutions on data collection/reporting, and authorizes the Coordinating Commission to receive/compile reports and adopt rules and regulations to implement the law. Sec. 7 sets an operative date of July 1, 2026; Sec. 8 contains an emergency clause making the act effective upon passage and approval. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the bill. Grants "the commission" authority to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement sections 1–6 of the act. No other state agencies or departments are named, and the provision includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB957_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB957_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB957 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-1351 to list "assault on a Department of Health and Human Services employee" (including related motor-vehicle assaults) among the predicate criminal acts that, if committed for the benefit of an organization, can support prosecution for unlawful membership recruitment. The offense remains a Class IV felony. The bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Health and Human Services. Adds definitions (child = under 14; handgun per existing statute) and two primary provisions: (1) imposes strict civil liability on a parent, guardian, or their spouse who knowingly allows a child to possess a handgun or handgun ammunition (except as already permitted by statute) for all damages resulting from use/possession; (2) creates a new criminal offense where a person stores or leaves a loaded firearm unsecured (no trigger lock, locked container, or other reasonable secure location) when they know or should know a child under 14 is likely to access it, the child gains access without parental consent, and the child publicly exhibits or uses the firearm to cause injury or death. Exceptions: unlawful entry or legally justified possession/use; violation is a Class I misdemeanor. No provisions in the added text amend funding, appropriations, or Department of Health and Human Services budgets. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB958_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB958_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends the Medical Assistance Act to (1) explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and (2) restrict the department’s authority to submit any 1915(c) waiver or amendment that would introduce an individual cost limit, reduce the aggregate number of service hours, or narrow eligibility criteria. Such waiver submissions require prior legislative approval. The bill also clarifies that "waiver" refers to applications submitted by the department to the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to obtain legislative approval before submitting any 1915(c) HCBS waiver application or amendment that would (1) introduce an individual cost limit, (2) reduce the aggregate number of service hours, or (3) narrow eligibility criteria. It also defines "nursing facility level of care" as a Medicaid recipient needing assistance with two or more activities of daily living who may receive services in a community setting provided the waiver program remains cost‑neutral. No explicit changes to appropriations or new funding/budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB959_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB959_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to establish two programs:\n\n- A youth afterschool credential for 16–17 year olds seeking work in school-age or temporary nonresidential child care. Requirements: registry and background checks, submission of background documentation, and a minimum seven-hour approved new-staff orientation. Provisional employment while checks pend is allowed with restrictions (not left alone with children, excluded from staff-to-child ratios, limited program types). Credentials expire after one year and may be renewed via an expedited process. The department may set rules, fees, training approval, and privacy/data-sharing protections.\n\n- An adult eligibility passport for persons 18+ to verify program-ready status and portable background-check compliance (including fingerprint-based criminal history). Passports are valid one year, renewable annually, auto-updated if new check data appears, and the department may charge fees up to actual administration cost and adopt implementing rules.\n\nNo funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified. The Department of Health and Human Services must create (1) a youth afterschool credential for 16–17-year-olds seeking work in school‑age or specified temporary nonresidential child care, and (2) an adult eligibility passport for adults 18+. Requirements: registry and criminal checks, background documentation, and a minimum seven‑hour new‑staff orientation for youth applicants; fingerprinting for adults. Youth applicants may work provisionally (not alone with children, not counted in ratios, limited to specified programs) while checks pend. Credentials/passports are valid one year, renewable via expedited processes; the department will accept them as portable verification across licensed child‑care and approved youth programs. The department may set rules (application, renewals, fees, training approval, privacy). An adult passport fee may be charged but limited to administrative cost. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB960_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB960_Intro_Copy.docx LB960 requires Nebraska school boards to include nonvoting "student school board members"—high school students serving in an advisory capacity—in a number equal to the board’s elected members. "School board" and "school district" reference section 79‑101. Selection rules: if a district has one high school all students come from it; if the number of high schools equals elected members, one from each; otherwise boards must adopt procedures to rotate representation equitably. Students (grades 10–12, in good standing) serve one‑year terms (start no later than the 2027‑28 school year). Duties: attend public meetings, receive materials, sit with the board, liaise with students, and introduce/advocate agenda items (sponsorship by an elected member may be required). Prohibitions: no voting, no closed‑session participation, no access to confidential records. Boards must adopt related policies by January 1, 2027. No funding or appropriations are specified. Adds a statutory requirement that school boards (as defined by section 79-101) must include nonvoting student school board members — one student member for each elected board member — drawn from district high schools. School districts/school boards must adopt selection procedures, one-year term rules (with initial terms beginning no later than the first day of the 2027–28 school year), and policies by January 1, 2027. Student members receive meeting materials, may participate in public discussion and introduce agenda items (subject to board rules), but may not vote, join closed sessions, or access confidential records. No state agencies beyond school boards/districts or changes to funding/appropriations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB961_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB961_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services LB961 contains no explicit references to the Department of Correctional Services. The bill amends statutes creating the Collateral Sanction Relief Act, modifies set‑aside and certificate‑of‑qualification procedures, and assigns duties to the State Court Administrator, Office of Probation Administration, and various courts and boards, but it does not mention the Department of Correctional Services nor includes any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations affecting that department. The added language requires the Department (along with the referenced board) to provide courts or the Office (e.g., Probation/State Court Administrator) any information about a petitioner that is relevant to petitions under the Collateral Sanction Relief Act. It otherwise leaves petition procedures, database maintenance, revocation, and presumption rules intact. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB962_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB962_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services The bill charges the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to establish the Youth Reentry and Transitional Support Program in coordination with the Office of Juvenile Services, the Office of Probation Administration, and the Division of Rehabilitation Services. DHHS must collaborate on individualized transition plans, assign aftercare coordinators, ensure continuity of behavioral health and Medicaid services, enroll eligible youth in rehabilitation services, and coordinate with family resource centers. DHHS (with the State Department of Education) must electronically submit annual reports to legislative committees detailing youth served, outcomes, and any federal or private funding leveraged. The Department of Labor is named as a co‑regulator: DHHS, Juvenile Services, Probation, DRS, and the Department of Labor must adopt rules on caseloads, training, allowable expenditures, interagency protocols, and outcome tracking. The bill contains no explicit appropriations or funding allocations. The Department of Health and Human Services must create a Youth Reentry and Transitional Support Program (with OJS, Probation, and the Division of Rehabilitation Services). DHHS duties: start transition/employment planning within 30 days, assign aftercare coordinators, provide up to 12 months of aftercare, ensure continuity of behavioral health and Medicaid, enroll youth in rehabilitation services, develop individualized employment plans, use credible-messenger mentoring, coordinate family supports, and file annual legislative reports (numbers served, education/housing/employment outcomes, estimated savings, and any federal/private funds leveraged). \n\nThe Department of Labor joins DHHS and other agencies to adopt rules (e.g., 1:15 coordinator caseload, training standards, allowable housing/employment expenditures, interagency protocols) and to track employment/education outcomes at 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-month intervals and assess workforce/system impacts. No explicit appropriations or new funding allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB963_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB963_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services LB963 amends the Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act to explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Correctional Services and "Director" as the Director of Correctional Services. It revises definitions to clarify that a committed offender or person committed includes those sentenced or committed to a facility operated by or to the custody of the department, and defines "facility" as institutions operated by the department. The bill also amends section 83-176 to state that sentencing to a specific departmental facility is deemed sentencing to the department and grants the director authority to designate suitable places of confinement (including nonstate facilities) and to transfer committed persons. No funding or appropriation changes are included. The added text merely repeats the phrase "the laws of this state." It contains no substantive provisions affecting the Department of Correctional Services and includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for that agency. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB964_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB964_Intro_Copy.docx LB964 enacts the "Nebraska Public Property Disclosure Act." It requires the governing body of any political subdivision to hold an open, public hearing before any sale or lease of real property owned by the subdivision or before any purchase of real property by the subdivision. Any person may speak at the hearing. If the governing body approves the transaction, it must be completed within two months or a new hearing is required. The governing body must publish notice at least ten days prior in a legal newspaper in or of general circulation, including legal description, address, assessed value, proposed price (and lease term), and the names of proposed parties. No state agencies or budget appropriations are specified. Creates the "Nebraska Public Property Disclosure Act." It requires the governing body of any political subdivision to:\n- hold an open public hearing before any sale, lease, or purchase of real property, with opportunity for public comment;\n- complete any approved transaction within two months of that hearing or, if not completed, hold a new hearing before proceeding;\n- publish notice at least 10 days beforehand in a legal newspaper circulating in the subdivision, stating legal description, address, assessed value, proposed price or lease terms, and names of the parties.\n\nNo specific state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB965_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB965_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends provisions affecting the Department of Correctional Services (DOC) and Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). It defines DOC terms and expands victim‑notification duties: county attorneys must provide victim names/addresses to DOC, and DOC must notify victims of furloughs, releases, escapes, discharges, and sentence calculations. DOC and DHHS must promulgate rules (with the Board of Parole and Board of Pardons) to implement victim‑notification provisions. Victim addresses/telephone numbers held by DOC and DHHS are exempt from public disclosure. The Board of Parole may recommend, and the DOC director may assign, eligible felony inmates to a short-term (up to 180-day) incarceration work camp before parole; persons convicted of certain sexual or capital offenses are ineligible. DHHS employees count as protected victims for pregnancy-related sentence enhancements; DHHS also manages alternative‑response child protection functions, report sharing, and must receive forwarded petitions and victim lists in commitment proceedings. No appropriations are included. - Defines “Department” to mean the Department of Correctional Services. \n- Adds new criminal offenses: sexual abuse by a conservator/guardian/guardian ad litem and sexual abuse by a child welfare service provider. Sexual penetration by a child welfare service provider is a Class IIA felony; sexual contact is a Class IIIA felony. “Minor” is defined as under 19. Convictions for these offenses are made subject to the Sex Offender Registration Act. These changes affect DHHS‑overseen child welfare providers. \n- Provides immunity for probation employees (as defined in section 29‑2246 and under the Office of Probation Administration) who, in good faith and per office policy, obtain and administer opioid‑overdose reversal medication: no administrative, criminal, or civil liability absent willful, wanton, or gross negligence. \n- No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included in the added text. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB966_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB966_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Agriculture LB966 (Hunger‑Free Schools Act) references the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) in defining "federal reimbursement rate" (Sec. 3(3)) and in tying qualified‑school participation to USDA child nutrition programs (Sec. 3(4)). State reimbursements to schools (Sec. 5) are calculated using USDA‑published federal reimbursement rates for free vs. reduced‑price meals. The bill contains no provisions altering funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Agriculture, nor does it appropriate funds to USDA. It does state legislative intent to appropriate General Fund money to the State Department of Education to implement the Act. Summary focused on the Department of Agriculture:\n\nThe added text creates the "Hunger-Free Schools Program" administered by the State Department of Education. Qualified schools must serve and report eligible reduced-price students' meals. The Department of Education will annually reimburse each qualified school an amount equal to the difference between the federal free- and reduced-price meal reimbursement rates (using USDA rates as of Jan 1, 2026), based on meals served in the second preceding school fiscal year. The State Board of Education may adopt rules, and the Legislature intends to appropriate General Fund money to the State Department of Education to implement the Act. No new duties, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are directed to the State or federal Department of Agriculture; USDA is referenced only as the source of federal reimbursement rates. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB967_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB967_Intro_Copy.docx LB967 amends the Mutual Insurance Holding Company Act by revising section 44-6122, prescribing requirements for electronic notice of annual meetings. The bill specifies that such notices may be provided at no cost to the member and may be delivered as part of policy language, an endorsement, a rider, or an amendment. The original version of section 44-6122 is repealed. No state agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds that a mutual insurance holding company may notify members of its annual meeting by including the notice in policy language, a policy endorsement, a rider, or an amendment (with no cost to the member). No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB968_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB968_Intro_Copy.docx Military Department Appropriates $4,000,000 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Military Department, Program No. 545 (Emergency Management), to provide grants for equipment for emergency rescue events. Grants are available to political subdivisions that demonstrate capability to assist in statewide rescue events. Funds are restricted to purchase equipment for water rescue, wide-area search (e.g., tornado and flood), structural collapse, and hazardous materials response. The bill includes an emergency clause making it effective upon passage. Appropriates $4,000,000 General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Military Department (Program No. 545, Emergency Management) to fund grants for emergency rescue equipment. Grants go to political subdivisions that demonstrate capability to assist in statewide rescue events. Awarded funds must be used exclusively to purchase equipment for emergency rescue operations, including water rescue, wide-area search (e.g., tornado/flood), structural collapse response, and hazardous materials incidents. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB969_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB969_Intro_Copy.docx LB969 requires the Nebraska Auditor of Public Accounts to develop, maintain, and publish online searchable financial databases for municipalities: cities of the metropolitan, primary, first and second classes, and villages. Each database must include revenue sources, expenditures, and balance sheets (assets and liabilities) drawn from the most recent municipal audits. Municipalities must provide current data annually and historical financial information beginning with calendar year 2016; the Auditor must update databases within 30 days of receipt. The Auditor must set implementation dates on or before January 1, 2027. Disclosure exclusions align with existing state and federal confidentiality and public-record law. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds requirements that the Auditor of Public Accounts (APA) create, maintain, and publish on its website a statewide financial database for cities of the metropolitan, primary, first, and second classes and for villages. The APA must include revenue sources, expenditures, and balance sheets (assets/liabilities) from the most recent municipal audits (and audit reports filed under section 19-2905 where cited), set an implementation date on or before January 1, 2027, and update the database within 30 days after receiving annual updates. Cities/villages must supply current and historical (from 2016) financial data. Confidential or nonpublic records are exempt. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB970_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB970_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (the department) to take multiple Medicaid actions and expansions, including:\n\n- Submit a state plan amendment by October 1, 2026 to expand EPSDT to add an early literacy promotion/intervention program for children birth–5. \n- Provide specified coverages by set dates: continuous glucose monitors (by Jan 1, 2023; expansion effective Aug 1, 2024), electric personal-use breast pumps and minimum lactation consultations (by Jan 1, 2025), translation/interpretation services (by Jan 1, 2024), targeted case management for nurse home visiting (seek SPA by Oct 1, 2025), and psychology services by advanced-level practitioners (by Jan 1, 2026). \n- Funding/appropriations: intent that up to $600,000 annually be appropriated from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for the glucose-monitor expansion; lactation consultations funded at a 145% rate increase over current departmental rates; multiple provisions to be funded from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (medical respite, translation services, nurse home visiting). Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, by October 1, 2026, to seek CMS approval (via a state plan amendment) to obtain federal Medicaid matching funds to expand EPSDT benefits to add an early literacy promotion and intervention program during well‑child visits for children birth through age five. The program must provide evidence‑based screening, referrals, and age‑appropriate materials and guidance for children enrolled in medical assistance as part of standard well‑child care. No explicit state appropriations or dollar amounts are specified; the provision seeks federal matching funds contingent on CMS approval. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB971_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB971_Intro_Copy.docx LB971 requires that Nebraska individual and group sickness and accident insurance policies, hospital/medical/surgical expense policies (other than limited‑benefit or specified‑disease plans), and self‑funded employee benefit plans (to the extent federal law does not preempt) cover prescribed asthma inhalers. Insurers must cover one rescue and one maintenance inhaler without deductible, copayment, coinsurance, or other cost‑sharing. High deductible health plans may apply the plan’s annual deductible if waiving it would jeopardize health savings account eligibility (citing IRC §223(c)(2)). No state agencies or departments are explicitly named; the bill references Neb. statute section 44‑3,131 and federal tax law. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Requires state-regulated individual/group sickness-and-accident policies, hospital/medical/surgical policies, and self-funded employer plans (unless preempted by federal law) to cover prescribed asthma inhalers. Plans must cover one rescue and one maintenance inhaler with no deductible, copayment, coinsurance, or other cost‑sharing; however, high‑deductible health plans may apply their annual deductible if necessary to preserve Health Savings Account eligibility under Internal Revenue Code section 223(c)(2) (IRS/Treasury HSA rules). References a state statute (section 44‑3,131) and the federal Internal Revenue Code; no specific government agency appropriations, budget allocations, or funding changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB972_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB972_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Transportation LB972 revises Department of Motor Vehicles authorities and fee flows. 109-2-LB973_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB973_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Transportation LB973 assigns the Department of Administrative Services (DAS) custody and operational control of most state-owned or leased buildings, and authorizes the DAS director to appoint an administrator with authority to lease and provide parking. 109-2-LB974_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB974_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue - The Department of Revenue is directed to collect the new excise tax at least once per taxable year on forms and in a manner prescribed by the department, and to remit amounts collected to the State Treasurer for credit to the newly created Tax Equity Cash Fund. \n- The Tax Equity Cash Fund is to be administered by the Department of Revenue; the fund consists of monies credited under the act. 109-2-LB975_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB975_Intro_Copy.docx LB975 (Private Attorney Retention Sunshine Act) imposes new transparency requirements on the Nebraska Attorney General’s retention of private counsel. Before retaining private attorneys for contracts exceeding $10,000, the AG must complete an open competitive bidding process (per §73-807) and file the proposed contract with the Legislature’s Appropriations Committee (if in session) or the Executive Board of the Legislative Council (if not). The committee/board must hold a public hearing within 10 days, issue a report, and the AG must file a proposed final contract (with explanation if committee changes are omitted); execution is permitted no earlier than 30 days after filing. Contingent-fee closures require disclosure of hours, expenses, and fee breakdowns; billable rates are capped at $1,000/hour. Act applies to AG contracts executed after its effective date and does not expand AG authority. Adds the "Private Attorney Retention Sunshine Act," affecting the Attorney General, the Legislature's Appropriations Committee, and the Executive Board of the Legislative Council. Key provisions:\n- Applies to Attorney General contracts for private legal services exceeding $10,000 (fees + expenses); requires an open, competitive bidding process per section 73‑807 before retention.\n- The AG must file proposed contracts with the Appropriations Committee (if in session) or the Legislative Council's Executive Board (if not); those bodies must hold a public hearing within 10 days and issue a report with recommended changes.\n- The AG must file a proposed final contract, explain any omitted recommendations, and wait at least 30 days before executing.\n- For contingent‑fee matters, retained counsel must disclose hours, expenses, aggregate fee, and an hourly‑rate breakdown. Legal fees are capped at $1,000 per hour (excesses reduced to $1,000). DOCX | PDF

109-2-LB977_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB977_Intro_Copy.docx LB977 amends Nebraska’s Rules of the Road to (1) redefine “vulnerable road user” to expressly include persons leading, herding, or driving livestock and users of electric personal assistive mobility devices, and (2) impose specific duties when approaching or passing such users. The Department of Transportation (and local authorities) may alter posted minimum freeway speeds, regulate operation of electric personal assistive mobility devices, and must post signage for minimum-speed limits. Motorists must yield, move over when feasible, use caution, and stop on a distress signal for livestock (defined as horse, mule, donkey, cattle, swine, sheep, or goat); peace officers, authorized emergency personnel, or road assistance personnel may direct traffic. Violations are traffic infractions, with repeat offenses elevated to a Class IIIA misdemeanor. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included. Adds provisions governing encounters with livestock on highways (refers to section 60-6,378.02). Defines “livestock” as horse, mule, donkey, cattle, swine, sheep, or goat. Requires motorists to: use caution when approaching or passing people leading/herding/driving livestock; promptly stop if a livestock handler gives a distress signal (raising a hand); and yield the right of way to livestock on the highway. Exception: these duties do not apply if moving the vehicle is necessary to avoid an accident. No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF

Civil penalties recovered are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, section 5, of the Nebraska Constitution. The bill limits liability for certain entities—Internet utilities (when merely providing access), courts, judges (good‑faith viewing/possession for official purposes), attorneys, and their agents/employees—in specified circumstances. Sovereign immunity is expressly not an affirmative defense for actions under the bill.\n\n[NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. 109-2-LB981_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB981_Intro_Copy.docx LB981 amends powers of cities of the metropolitan class and the Nebraska Housing Agency Act to regulate housing agencies and impose operational duties. Cities of the metropolitan class may require housing authorities to comply with city rental-inspection/registration ordinances, code enforcement, and residential rental inspections. The bill requires metropolitan-area housing agencies to implement a formal complaint process with timelines and tracking, mandates bed‑bug protocols (inspection by or via a pest control professional within 10 days, remediation within 21 days, disclosure before leasing, agency responsibility for remediation costs, two‑year recordkeeping), and to report semiannually to the city and the Legislature’s Urban Affairs Committee (pest control activity, evictions, complaints, vacancy rates, board updates). Pest control professionals must be licensed under the Pesticide Act. No new appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Adds requirements for housing authorities in a "city of the metropolitan class" to comply with local rental inspection/registration ordinances and code enforcement. Defines "bed bug" and "pest control professional" (licensed commercial applicator). Establishes procedural duties for the housing agency: regular complainant updates; advance tenant notice before unit entry; for bed‑bug complaints, inspection (including adjacent units) within 10 days and remediation secured within 21 days; maintain written complaint/remedy records for two years. Imposes pre‑rental visual inspections, prohibition on renting units known or suspected to be infested, mandatory disclosure of adjacent infestations, and assigns the agency responsibility for investigation and remediation costs. 109-2-LB983_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB983_Intro_Copy.docx LB983 amends Neb. Rev. 109-2-LB984_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB984_Intro_Copy.docx LB984 makes procedural and substantive changes affecting county clerks and the courts. County clerks are prohibited from issuing marriage licenses to anyone under 18. District and other courts presiding over emancipation petitions must advise minors of specified consequences, apply a clear-and-convincing proof standard, and may enter judgments of emancipation if in the minor’s best interest. A court-ordered emancipation confers most adult legal capacities (contracting, medical consent, property, litigation) while preserving age-specific constitutional/statutory limits; it also suspends existing custody, parenting-time, and support orders. The district court clerk must report any suspended orders to the jurisdiction that issued them. Several statutory sections are repealed. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included. Adds a requirement that no marriage license may be issued unless both parties are at least 18 years old. 109-2-LB987_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB987_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Insurance The bill requires insurers and vision benefit managers to disclose, as part of mandated transparency information, all formal complaints filed with the Department of Insurance against the insurer or manager in the current year and the preceding five years. 109-2-LB991_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB991_Intro_Copy.docx LB991 authorizes school districts to install, operate, or contract with private vendors to provide, operate, or support stop‑signal‑arm camera systems on school buses. Collected data must bear date, time, and location; buses with cameras must display a warning readable at 100 feet. School districts may disclose or copy collected data.\n\nThe bill amends enforcement in §60‑6,175 to permit citation for stop‑arm violations based on camera data only after a peace officer reviews the data. Citations must be mailed to the registered owner within six days. 109-2-LB993_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB993_Intro_Copy.docx LB993 creates a state cause of action for deprivation of federal or Nebraska constitutional rights by law enforcement officers and removes qualified immunity as a defense. It requires public employers — defined to include the State of Nebraska, state agencies, and political subdivisions — to indemnify officers for judgments under the new cause of action unless the officer acted in bad faith or with malicious intent, with notice procedures if indemnification is withheld. Sovereign immunity is waived for these claims and such claims are exempted from the State Tort Claims Act and the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act (amendments to sections 13-903 and 81-8,210). Any punitive damages awarded are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, §5. Operative date: January 1, 2027.\n\n[NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.] Adds a state civil cause of action for deprivation of constitutional rights by law‑enforcement officers and defines covered actors and employers. Key government entities and fiscal effects:\n\n- Definitions: “public employer” means the State of Nebraska, any state agency, or any political subdivision (but not contractors). “Law enforcement officer” includes officers defined in section 81‑1401, peace officers under section 49‑801, correctional officers, and probation officers; “state agency” and “political subdivision” reference existing statutory definitions.\n- Fiscal/legal duties: public employers must indemnify officers for judgments under the new cause of action unless the officer acted in bad faith or maliciously; if indemnification is denied, the employer must notify officer and plaintiff within 30 days.\n- Punitive damages are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution.\n- Sovereign immunity is waived for these claims, which are excluded from the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act and the State Tort Claims Act. No specific appropriation amounts are provided. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB994_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB994_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services LB994 assigns multiple duties to the Department of Correctional Services (the department). Key provisions:\n- Recalculate parole-eligibility dates for all committed offenders incarcerated on/after July 1, 2011, by April 15, 2027, in coordination with the Board of Parole using phased implementation; administrative recalculation delays cannot alone deny parole eligibility; affected parolees may request reduced parole terms.\n- Within 60 days of initial classification, prepare a department‑approved personalized program plan and provide specified programming (education, substance‑abuse, mental‑health, vocational, work programs, etc.).\n- Apply sentence reductions (six months per year; plus three days monthly after 12 months of good conduct); reductions affect parole eligibility and discharge dates; facility chief (with director approval) may forfeit/restore reductions.\n- Ensure release/reentry plans at 80% of sentence, provide community‑standard mental‑health care, evaluate before release, prepare parolee case plans within 30 days, and collaborate/share records with probation for post‑release supervision plans.\n\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The Department of Correctional Services must recalculate parole eligibility dates for all committed offenders incarcerated on or after July 1, 2011, and complete this work by April 15, 2027. Recalculations must be done in coordination with the Board of Parole, using a phased implementation to avoid administrative overload and protect public safety. No one may be denied parole eligibility solely because of administrative delay in recalculation. Individuals on parole who were discharged after July 1, 2011 and before this act’s effective date may ask the Board to reduce their parole term if affected. The bill clarifies that good‑time reductions apply to tentative release and parole eligibility (affecting minimum terms other than mandatory minimums and maximum terms). No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB995_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB995_Intro_Copy.docx LB995 amends juvenile justice statutes to strengthen appointment and waiver rules for counsel. It requires juvenile courts to appoint counsel when petitions allege jurisdiction under specified subsections of §43-247 and to continue that right at subsequent hearings. Juvenile courts must inform parties of rights and provide age-appropriate written materials explaining the right to counsel. Waivers must be made in open court, recorded, and signed; be affirmative, intelligent, voluntary, and informed (with courts considering age, intelligence, education, emotional stability, and case complexity); and follow the written-materials requirement. The court must ensure consultation with counsel before any waiver. Waiver is prohibited for juveniles under 14, detention hearings, dispositional hearings seeking out-of-home placement, and transfer-to-adult-court motions; parents may not waive counsel. Appointed counsel is paid by the county for indigent juveniles, and courts may later order parental reimbursement and enforce collection. The Supreme Court, juvenile courts, county governments, and county attorneys are implicated. Adds requirements for juvenile courts to ensure juveniles (and their parents/guardians) are informed of the right to counsel and, when applicable, appoint counsel at subsequent juvenile‑court hearings. If counsel is not appointed, the court must advise parties of the right to retain counsel, ask whether they wish to retain counsel, and provide written materials explaining the juvenile’s right to counsel. Materials must be written at a level understandable to the juvenile and developed using best‑practice methods to ensure comprehension. The bill also ties recordkeeping/waiver elements to having informed parties and having provided the written materials (see subdivision (1)(b) of §43‑279). No executive agencies or departments beyond the juvenile court are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB996_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB996_Intro_Copy.docx LB996 amends the Nebraska Juvenile Code to restrict shackling of juveniles and to require Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) transportation policies to extend to private contractors used by the Office of Juvenile Services (OJS) for transporting youth placed at youth rehabilitation and treatment centers. Section 1 prohibits shackling except where (1) a juvenile poses a recent, substantial risk of physical harm, (2) no less‑restrictive alternative will prevent the harm, and (3) shackling is limited to the minimum duration necessary. Shackling is defined to include handcuffs, leg irons, waist/belly chains, restraint chairs, etc.; only brief, temporary handcuffing for immediate articulable risk is allowed. DHHS policies must also prohibit routine mechanical restraints during transport; any exceptions must be narrowly limited, documented, and subject to review. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds a prohibition on shackling juveniles except where narrowly necessary: authorized persons may use mechanical restraints only if the juvenile poses a recent, substantial risk of physical harm, no less-restrictive alternative exists, and restraints are limited to the time strictly required. Defines “shackling” and permits only very brief handcuffing for immediate safety. Requires policies to bar shackling in violation of the new rule and to prohibit routine mechanical restraints during transportation; exceptions must be documented and reviewed. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and no funding or appropriation changes are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB997_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB997_Intro_Copy.docx LB997 amends §73-815 of the State Procurement Act governing sole‑source service contracts over $50,000. It requires preapproval by the division except in emergencies; in an emergency the state agency director or the director’s designee may approve the contract. Copies of the emergency contract and the agency’s written justification must be provided to the Director of Administrative Services and to the Auditor of Public Accounts within three business days, and the state agency must retain a copy. The Director of Administrative Services is directed to maintain a complete record of such sole‑source service contracts. The bill repeals the original section. No funding or appropriation changes are included. The added text designates the Auditor of Public Accounts as a recipient of copies (i.e., directs that copies be provided to that office). No other agencies are named and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB998_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB998_Intro_Copy.docx LB998 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2716 to expand state income tax treatment for members of the Nebraska National Guard. It allows individuals who are Guard members to exclude 100% of specified Guard compensation from Nebraska taxable income: for tax years 2025–2026 the exclusion applies to pay from 32 U.S.C. duty statuses, employment as a 32 U.S.C. federal dual-status technician, or state active duty; beginning January 1, 2027 the exclusion expressly includes pay from 10 U.S.C. or 32 U.S.C. military duty status. The statute remains administered under the state tax code (Tax Commissioner). No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are contained in the bill. Creates a state individual income tax exclusion, effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, allowing Nebraska National Guard members to exclude 100% of income (to the extent included in federal adjusted gross income) from: service in a 10 U.S.C. or 32 U.S.C. military duty status, employment as a 32 U.S.C. federal dual‑status technician with the Nebraska National Guard, or service in state active duty. References the Internal Revenue Code and federal statutes (10 U.S.C., 32 U.S.C.). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-2-LB999_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 2 (2026) 109 2 LB999_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor The bill contains no explicit references to the Department of Economic Development or the Department of Labor. Accordingly, it makes no direct changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency. (The bill does create a Business Innovation and Startup Fund, funded by transfers from the Legislature and administered by the new commission, but that provision does not assign funding or duties to the Department of Economic Development or the Department of Labor.) Creates a Business Innovation and Startup Fund (funded by legislative transfers) and the Business Innovation and Startup Commission to use it to support regional/sector innovation hubs (incubators, accelerators, entrepreneurial supports) via partnerships, technical assistance, and targeted grants in urban and rural areas. Money in the fund may be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Annual electronic reports to the Legislature are required on or before Dec. 1, 2027, and each Dec. 1 thereafter, including grant accounting, measurable outcomes (startup formation, access to capital, geographic and equity metrics), and budgetary recommendations. No explicit references to the Department of Labor or specific dollar appropriations; potential impacts to the Department of Economic Development are indirect (new grant/partnership funding administered by the Commission). LB319_Intro_Copy.docx Unknown session Legislative Bill 319 delegates several responsibilities to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The Department is tasked with maximizing federal funding to minimize the use of state General Funds for SNAP and is required to employ necessary personnel to explore available federal options for Nebraska.\n\nAdditional provisions include the development of a state outreach plan conforming to the Food and Nutrition Service's criteria, which is part of the United States Department of Agriculture. DHHS may seek gifts, grants, or donations to fund the outreach initiative, which must be submitted to the Food and Nutrition Service for approval. If approved, it may secure federal matching funds, aiming to supplement state funds for increased caseloads due to the outreach plan implementation.\n\nThe bill explicitly prohibits the use of General Funds by the Department of Labor for any action regarding a SNAP benefit partnership program, focused on encouraging higher employment among recipients. This program requires no state General Funds but may act with federal or other non-state funding. \n\nLastly, the DHHS is mandated to provide annual reports detailing the efficiencies and costs of these implementations to the Health and Human Services Committee of the Legislature. The legislative text modifies eligibility criteria for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) related to individuals convicted of felonies involving controlled substances. According to the new provisions under 21 U.S.C. 862, individuals convicted of such felonies will now be eligible for SNAP benefits only if they have either completed their sentence or are currently serving parole, probation, or post-release supervision. This change pertains to policies administered by the Department of Agriculture, which oversees SNAP. The amendment does not include any direct changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations within the specified departments. —
